title: Fast conversational core: streaming hot path + async task orchestration (Meet-first)
description:
# Fast conversational core: streaming hot path + async task orchestration (Meet-first)

## Why

Johnny's voice conversation was compared against openclaw's "Start Talk" feature, which responds near-instantly. Two code-verified deep dives (openclaw + Johnny) found the gap and the operator set direction: keep the split STT→router→LLM→TTS pipeline (no cloud speech-to-speech replacement) but refactor it — the router is slow and the pipeline underperforms. Google Meet (multi-participant) is the primary surface.

## Vision

Adopt openclaw's "Start Talk" lessons inside Johnny's split pipeline:

1. **Stream everything before the LLM** — STT runs DURING speech (interim + fast final), endpointing commits early when the utterance is confidently complete, providers are prewarmed, TTS head-of-line shrinks, the client cuts bot audio locally on barge-in.
2. **Router stays but becomes fast triage** — outcome set {silent | speak | delegate | status}. Simple asks answered immediately; complex asks get an instant verbal ack ("let me check on that") and are delegated.
3. **Async task threads** (openclaw's "forced consult" pattern, Johnny-shaped) — an operational controller (task registry, status, progress queries: "are you still working on that?") and an executional layer (tool calls: Calendar first, Gmail later; webhook/callback re-entry). LangGraph evaluated as the engine for multi-step kinds (operator-requested).
4. **Speech queue with conversational re-entry** — pending utterances (ack > requested-status > unsolicited-result > notice) delivered only at turn boundaries/silence, with expiry; never cuts a participant off.

## Preserved unchanged (invariants)

- INV-1 ("exactly one terminal per turn", TurnLedger) and INV-2 — hard constraints; a delegated turn's terminal is its ack utterance; async results are session-scoped speech (approval-reply precedent), never turn terminals.
- Replay-harness verdict parity: router schema changes are additive; old model outputs parse byte-for-byte identically.
- Meet/room turn-taking semantics untouched by Phase-1 endpointing work (browser-session-scoped knobs only).
- agentsession orchestrator (no legacy engine work); S2S/unified path out of scope (Johnny-20h stays deferred).
- Docker-only runtime; clean-install reproducibility (all new deps in pyproject); chrome-devtools browser validation for every UI-visible change.

## Replaced / built

- Plain VAD endpointing on the browser session → tuned endpointing + roomless semantic turn detector (in-process InferenceExecutor shim).
- Batch-only Parakeet → cache-aware streaming `transcribe_stream`.
- Router as monolithic should-speak gate → triage with delegate/status actions + task catalog + ~8 s budget.
- Nothing → agent_tasks table, TaskCoordinator, worker executor pass, ToolRegistry (calendar.upcoming_events first), task events, speech queue, webhook entry, Gmail scope, session-page tasks panel.

## Anchors

- Latency targets (docs/LATENCY.md, speech-end → first audible byte): p50/p95 = 300/500 ms all-local, 250/450 mixed, 200/400 all-cloud. Re-measured at every phase capstone via the Phase-0 harness.
- Live-Meet E2E scenario: complex ask → ack ≤ ~2 s → conversation continues → status query answered → result delivered at a conversational boundary.

## Phases (capstone-gated)

- Phase 0 — Baseline & foundations: Johnny-cxu baseline (absorbed as child), scripted latency harness, livekit-agents 1.5.17 surface verification (say()/user_state_changed), replay parity fixtures.
- Phase 1 — Hot-path latency quick wins: endpointing knobs, roomless semantic turn detector, Piper chunk_bytes 1024, provider prewarm, client-side auto barge-in, Meet bridge audit.
- Phase 2 — Streaming STT in the voice pipeline: Parakeet cache-aware streaming, live interim captions, Deepgram verification + all-cloud numbers.
- Phase 3 — Router triage refactor: parity-safe schema extension, gate branching + ack terminal, agent_tasks + TaskCoordinator + stub executor, triage budget/observability (+ deferred speculative-parallel spike).
- Phase 4 — Async execution: LangGraph evaluation spike, ToolRegistry + calendar tool, worker executor pass, task event plumbing.
- Phase 5 — Speech queue & re-entry: pure queue core, wiring + TaskEventListener + delivery timing, real status query, live-Meet validation.
- Phase 6 — Entry points & cutover: webhook callback endpoint, Gmail scope + tool, session-page tasks panel, docs + final acceptance.

Related (not duplicated): Johnny-20h (deferred S2S epic — explicitly out of scope here), Johnny-stt (Parakeet streaming provider work references it), Johnny-ckz.7 (shipped per-turn timing instrument this epic's measurements ride on), Johnny-1ge (shipped persistent TTS).

Full approved plan: /Users/nikita/.claude/plans/project-projects-openclaw-has-a-soft-barto.md (2026-06-10).
acceptance_criteria:
Definition of done (epic): all children closed across Phases 0-6 (3.5 may close as deferred-design-only); INV-1/INV-2 ledger invariants and replay verdict parity hold throughout; docs/LATENCY.md re-measured at every phase capstone with phase-over-phase deltas (final: all-local felt p50 <= 300 ms from speech-end, or documented attribution why not); live-Meet E2E scenario green (complex ask -> instant ack -> async execution -> status query answered -> result delivered at a conversational boundary); clean install (./stop.sh && ./run.sh) reproduces everything with no hand-patching; no S2S/legacy-engine changes.
Gating tests (all green before cutover): replay harness invariants, INV-1 unit suite, scripted latency harness, chrome-devtools browser validations for UI-visible changes, recorded live-Meet acceptance run under .validation/.
notes:
DESIGN REVISION 2026-06-10 (operator direction): tool layer rebuilt as an openclaw-style three-layer capability model — TOOLS execute (core sandbox.exec + MCP-contributed), SKILLS instruct (openclaw/AgentSkills-compatible SKILL.md packages on a shared volume, eligibility-gated by requires.bins inside the sandbox), MCP servers contribute tools (mcp__server__tool). All CLI execution happens in a new operator-customizable skills-sandbox compose service (Johnny-trt.35; gog preinstalled as reference). NO direct Gmail/Calendar API integration: Johnny-trt.23 rewritten (tool layer + skill registry + calendar-via-gog skill), Johnny-trt.32 rewritten (gmail-via-gog + non-Google skill + install flow, zero OAuth scope work). Added Johnny-trt.36 (MCP connector) and Johnny-trt.37 (capability management UI: tools policy, skills status/reload, MCP add/probe).
AGENTS PIVOT 2026-06-11 (operator direction): Phase 6 restructured around a first-class AGENT entity replacing templates + personalities + meeting overrides — clean wipe, no migration (unreleased product). Agents own: identity/character/behavior, pipeline_mode (split: LLM+TTS+voice actually applied; s2s: single S2S provider — requires S2S revival on AgentSession, absorbing Johnny-20h core), per-agent capability scope (policy engine layer), sectioned admin edit page. Meetings/playground assign agents with ONE per-assignment context field. FULL multi-agent meetings in scope: one bot session per assignment + shared speech floor + peer awareness (trt.46). New tasks: trt.41-46; trt.37/38/34 adjusted.
S2S REVERSAL 2026-06-11 (operator): trt.43 flipped from 'revive S2S on AgentSession' to 'remove S2S/unified pipeline from the surface' — agents ship split-only; S2S returns as a separate future epic (Johnny-20h placeholder). trt.41/42/44 simplified to split-only; trt.41 now depends on trt.43 so the agent entity is built after the removal.

title: docker compose exec api pytest fails on clean image — backend Dockerfile installs --no-dev
description: The api/worker image (backend/Dockerfile) runs 'uv sync ... --no-dev' on both the cached-deps layer and the post-COPY full sync, so the [dependency-groups] dev group (pytest, pytest-asyncio, ruff, mypy, aiosqlite, types-PyYAML) is never installed. Fix at the source-of-truth layer: install the dev group in the api/worker image so the documented test command works after a fresh build.

title: [SPIKE] Phase 0: Audio topology + double-hop/echo e2e in a real Meet call
description: The #1 unknown. Stand up LiveKit + a trivial stub/echo agent + the existing livekit_transport.py publishing REAL PulseAudio-monitor audio, then drive a live Meet call via chrome-devtools MCP. Measure round-trip latency, clock drift, resampling quality, and crucially whether the bot re-transcribes its own audio (echo/AEC) now that audio makes a double hop Meet->room->agent->room->Meet. Decision output: is the room topology viable, and what AEC/loopback-suppression config is required. Gates Phase 3. Validate 'hears me / talks back' before building anything else.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria (SPIKE — deliverable is a measured decision, not production code):
- A throwaway LiveKit + stub echo agent runs; the meet-worker bridge publishes REAL PulseAudio-monitor audio into a room and plays the agent track back into the Meet mic.
- Round-trip latency (mouth-to-ear, Meet->room->agent->room->Meet) measured and recorded with a target/threshold.
- Documented YES/NO on whether the bot re-transcribes its own audio (echo), plus the exact AEC/loopback-suppression config required to prevent it.
- Clock-drift and resampling quality assessed; go/no-go written on the room topology with the required config handed to Johnny-6nm/Johnny-9eh.

Tests:
- E2E manual+driven: live Meet call via chrome-devtools MCP; capture latency numbers, a console/log dump, and a short note under .validation/Johnny-4em/.
- No unit tests expected; the artifact is the measurement + decision doc (store as design notes on this issue).
notes:
[SPIKE DECISION 2026-06-08] GO — self-hosted room double-hop topology is viable.

Measured the new/unproven surface (the room double hop) with a throwaway
livekit-server:1.12.0 --dev + two REAL LiveKitTransport participants (bridge
publishes a known signal; stub agent echoes) so audio takes the real hop
bridge->SFU->agent->SFU->bridge through johnny.voice_pipeline.livekit_transport.

RESULTS (room double hop, 3 runs incl. a 75s window):
- Round-trip latency: median 105-150ms, p95 <=153ms, ~55-75ms one-way. Stable.
- Clock drift: NONE. recv/emit sample ratio = 1.015 over 75s; latency rises ~20ms
  then plateaus (jitter-buffer settling, not skew).
- Resampling/codec fidelity (16k->48k->Opus->48k->16k x2): exact pitch across
  300/1000/3000 Hz (0 Hz err), ~14 dB in-band SNR, THD <0.2% — voice-grade, STT-ok.
- Echo / self-transcription: NO. SFU never returns a participant its own track —
  bridge_heard_itself=False, agent_heard_itself=False (3 runs); agent idle-gap
  RMS=0.0 (no self-echo feedback). NO acoustic AEC applicable (all virtual PCM).

Echo is NO at all 3 layers: (1) room — SFU self-exclusion (measured); (2) PulseAudio
— johnny_speaker and johnny_mic_loopback are independent null sinks, no loopback
bridging them; (3) Meet/WebRTC — never returns your own uplink to your downlink.
The plan's "room reintroduces echo" only happens via MISCONFIG — a config-discipline
checklist, not an AEC problem.

REQUIRED CONFIG (handed to Johnny-6nm/9eh/6wx):
1. One room/session, exactly 2 participants (bridge + agent).
2. Agent STT subscribes ONLY to the bridge's meeting track (default RoomIO; if >2
   parties, restrict via RoomInputOptions so STT never ingests the agent's own TTS).
3. Bridge publishes ONLY meeting audio; NEVER re-publishes the agent track into the
   room (agent track terminates at pacat->johnny_mic->Meet).
4. Never add a PulseAudio loopback mixing johnny_mic* -> johnny_speaker.
5. STT may drain continuously — agent never hears its own TTS, so always-on stt_node
   is self-trigger-safe.
6. resample_pcm16 is linear (not anti-aliased); prefer native provider rate + let
   LiveKit do 48k conversion.
7. Latency budget: room hop ~55-75ms one-way is negligible vs Meet (~100-250ms/dir)
   and agent reasoning. Re-measure live mouth-to-ear in Johnny-6nm/9eh.

NOT measured here (deferred, gated by this spike): live Meet mouth-to-ear. meet-worker
image lacks livekit-rtc (added in Johnny-6nm); agent-worker (9eh) + LiveKit-in-compose
(6wx) don't exist yet. Full writeup + harnesses + logs: .validation/Johnny-4em/.

title: [SPIKE] Phase 0: Per-room JWT auth + agent dispatch contract (job payload)
description: Design how rooms are authorized and how the agent is dispatched per Meet session. Per-room JWT minting for meet-worker + agent; WorkerOptions/agent name; explicit dispatch (api.AgentDispatch) for one-room-per-session. Define the job payload contract (which providers, personality, mode, instructions the agent receives via room metadata or dispatch payload). Gates Phase 3 (bridge + worker).
design:
# LiveKit room auth + agent dispatch contract

Decision record for **Johnny-y4j** (Phase 0 spike, epic Johnny-7g5 — migrate
voice orchestration to LiveKit Agents `AgentSession`). It is the gating
contract for Phase 3: the meet-worker↔room bridge (Johnny-6nm), the agent-worker
service + dispatch lifecycle (Johnny-9eh), and threading session config into the
job (Johnny-7we).

## Topology recap

One **LiveKit room per Meet session**. The meet-worker bridges Meet audio into
that room (publishes the PulseAudio monitor as a track, subscribes to the agent
track → virtual mic); the agent worker joins the same room with LiveKit's
default `RoomIO`. The `livekit` SFU is internal-only (no host `ports:` mapping;
reachable only on the `johnny_default` compose network) and is configured with
`LIVEKIT_KEYS: "${LIVEKIT_API_KEY}: ${LIVEKIT_API_SECRET}"` — the same key/secret
pair handed to api/worker, so a token minted on the API validates on the SFU.

```
Meet ──> meet-worker (bridge token) ──> [ room: johnny-session-<id> ] <── agent worker (server-issued token)
                publish/subscribe                                          dispatched explicitly w/ job metadata
```

## 1. Token minting

**Who mints:** the **API / session orchestrator**. It already holds
`LIVEKIT_API_KEY` / `LIVEKIT_API_SECRET` and is the single component that knows
the session→room mapping. Code: `johnny/agent/room_auth.py`.

**What is minted:**

| Token | Identity | Scopes (`VideoGrants`) | Carried as |
|-------|----------|------------------------|------------|
| **Bridge** (`mint_bridge_token`) | `meet-bridge-<session>` | `room_join`, `room=<room>`, `can_publish`, `can_subscribe`, `can_publish_data`; `agent=false` | `LIVEKIT_TOKEN` env on the spawned meet-worker (the var `LiveKitTransport` already reads) |
| **Agent** (`mint_agent_token`) | `johnny-agent-<session>` | same + `agent=true` | only for non-framework joiners / the proof — see note below |

**`room_join` is pinned to the one session room**, so a leaked token cannot
wander into another session.

> **The framework path does not hand-mint an agent token.** With LiveKit
> Agents, the agent worker authenticates to the SFU with the raw key/secret
> (`WorkerOptions(api_key=, api_secret=)`); when a dispatched job is assigned,
> the **server issues** that worker's participant token. `mint_agent_token`
> exists for the spike proof, a console harness, or any hand-rolled participant.

**TTL & rotation:** `DEFAULT_TTL = 6 h` — longer than any real meeting, so a
per-session token never expires mid-call and **there is no in-session refresh**.
Tokens are per-session and single-use; a new session mints a fresh token. Key
rotation is operational: change `LIVEKIT_API_KEY`/`LIVEKIT_API_SECRET` in `.env`
and restart the `livekit` service — because tokens are short-lived per session,
subsequent sessions simply mint under the new key with no migration step.

## 2. Dispatch mechanism

**Chosen: explicit dispatch, one room per session** (`api.AgentDispatch`). Code:
`johnny/agent/dispatch.py`.

The agent worker registers with a **non-empty `agent_name`** (`AGENT_NAME =
"johnny"`) in its `WorkerOptions`. Naming the worker **disables LiveKit's
automatic dispatch** (which would otherwise fan every agent into every new
room), so the agent only runs jobs dispatched to it explicitly — exactly one
agent per Meet session, carrying that session's config.

Two supported trigger paths:

1. **Primary — out-of-band `dispatch_agent(room, config)`**: the API calls
   `AgentDispatchService.create_dispatch(CreateAgentDispatchRequest(agent_name,
   room, metadata))` over the server API. The orchestrator decides exactly when
   the agent joins (e.g. once the bridge is publishing).
2. **Secondary — `room_config_with_agent(config)`**: a `RoomConfiguration` with
   one `RoomAgentDispatch` embedded in a bridge token (via
   `AccessToken.with_room_config`) or a `CreateRoom` call, so the agent is
   dispatched the instant the bridge brings the room up. Use if the bridge
   should self-trigger the agent with no extra round-trip.

**Agent entrypoint (Johnny-9eh) will look like:**

```python
from livekit.agents import WorkerOptions, cli, JobContext
from johnny.agent.job_config import SessionJobConfig

async def entrypoint(ctx: JobContext):
    cfg = SessionJobConfig.from_metadata(ctx.job.metadata)   # the contract
    # build adapter factory + JohnnyAgent from cfg, then:
    await ctx.connect()

cli.run_app(WorkerOptions(
    entrypoint_fnc=entrypoint,
    agent_name="johnny",          # => explicit dispatch only
    ws_url=os.environ["LIVEKIT_URL"],
    api_key=os.environ["LIVEKIT_API_KEY"],
    api_secret=os.environ["LIVEKIT_API_SECRET"],
))
```

## 3. Job-payload schema

`johnny/agent/job_config.py :: SessionJobConfig` — the serialisable description
of one Meet session, **consumed by Johnny-7we**. It mirrors the legacy
`JOHNNY_*` launcher env contract field-for-field
(`app.services.docker_launcher._build_environment`) so the two paths stay in
lockstep during the migration; `from_env()`/`to_env()` bridge the two.

Fields: `bot_session_id`, `room_name`, `meet_link`, `meeting_config_id`,
`calendar_event_id`, `account_id`, `mode` (`listen_only` | `suggest_only` |
`approval_required` | `limited_auto_speak`), `pipeline_mode` (`split` |
`unified`), the prompt-assembly text (`instructions`, `personality_prompt`,
`context`, `calendar_context`, `calendar_attachments_text`,
`prior_session_context` → feeds `AgentInstructionsConfig`), `provider_config`
(the exact `build_provider_payload` shape: `{kind: {provider_name, display_name,
credentials, options}}`), and `redis_url`.

`to_metadata()` / `from_metadata()` are the JSON wire form; `from_metadata`
validates the enums strictly so a malformed dispatch fails loud at the agent.

**Transport — dispatch metadata, not room metadata.** Dispatch metadata is
per-job, set by the orchestrator, read as `ctx.job.metadata`. Room metadata is
global to the room and readable by every participant (incl. the bridge), which
needlessly widens exposure of the provider credentials in the payload.

**Security note** (same boundary as today's `JOHNNY_PROVIDER_CONFIG`): the
payload carries plaintext provider credentials. They travel the internal-only
control plane (API → in-compose `livekit` server → agent worker over its
authenticated connection). A future hardening — mirrored from
`app.services.provider_payload`'s note — is short-lived credentials fetched over
HTTP rather than embedded in the payload.

## Proof (this spike)

`backend/tests/agent/test_room_dispatch_smoke.py` (marker `livekit_smoke`),
green against the in-compose `livekit` SFU:

1. `mint_bridge_token` → a real `rtc.Room` participant connects to
   `johnny-session-<pid>`, the server lists it, and it leaves on teardown
   (proves the JWT + scopes — an under-scoped/invalid token is rejected by the
   server, so green means the grants are right).
2. `dispatch_agent` → the explicit dispatch is accepted, retrievable via
   `list_dispatch`, and its metadata round-trips back to the `SessionJobConfig`.

The agent **process** actually joining on dispatch is exercised end-to-end in
Johnny-9eh, where the agent-worker service is registered against the SFU; this
spike validates the auth + dispatch + payload contracts that gate it.

Unit tests: `test_job_config.py` (schema round-trips, validation, legacy-env
bridge, drift guard vs. canonical mode constants), `test_room_auth.py` (decoded
JWT scopes), `test_dispatch.py` (`agent_name`, URL scheme mapping, embedded
`RoomConfiguration`).

## Run the proof

```bash
# unit (no network):
docker compose exec api pytest tests/agent/test_job_config.py \
  tests/agent/test_room_auth.py tests/agent/test_dispatch.py
# integration (against the in-compose livekit SFU):
docker compose exec api pytest -m livekit_smoke tests/agent/test_room_dispatch_smoke.py
```
acceptance_criteria:

- Minimal proof: a token mints and a stub agent is dispatched into a named room and joins.

Getting this wrong forces a Phase-2 rewrite.

title: Kokoro mlx-sidecar: mlx-audio 0.4.4 generate() raises broadcast_shapes mismatch (distinct from the misaki dep fixed in Johnny-1ge.11)
description:
Johnny-1ge.11 fixed the missing 'misaki' dependency for the Kokoro mlx-sidecar (the venv now contains misaki + en_core_web_sm and the original 'Kokoro requires the optional misaki package' error is gone). But synthesis against the mlx sidecar now fails with a DIFFERENT, deeper error from mlx-audio 0.4.4 itself:

  POST http://localhost:8772/synthesize {voice:'af_heart',lang_code:'a'} -> HTTP 500
  kokoro mlx synthesis failed for voice='af_heart' lang='a': in-memory generate() raised ([broadcast_shapes] Shapes (1,36600,1) and (1,36900,9) cannot be broadcast.); the file fallback then raised (generate_audio produced no .wav output ...)

This is an mlx-audio runtime/tensor-shape bug (the '9' dim looks like a voice-style/token-count mismatch), not a missing dependency. sidecars/kokoro-mlx/pyproject.toml currently pins mlx-audio>=0.2.0 which resolves to 0.4.4.

Repro: ./scripts/start-kokoro-sidecar.sh start mlx ; curl -s -X POST localhost:8772/synthesize -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"hello","voice":"af_heart","lang_code":"a"}'

Likely fixes to investigate: (a) pin mlx-audio to a known-good version that synthesizes Kokoro without the broadcast error (verify load_model API still matches sidecars/kokoro-mlx/server.py:_load_model_sync); (b) adjust the generate() call / voice-pack handling in server.py for the 0.4.x API; (c) upstream mlx-audio issue.

Impact: LOW — Kokoro is fully usable via the in-container runtime (baked, working) and the http-sidecar (working after the misaki fix). mlx-sidecar is the Apple-Silicon perf fast path only.

Cross-link: Johnny-1ge.11 (dependency fix), Johnny-1ge epic, Johnny-1ge.6 (sidecar CLI).

title: TTS clean-install REGRESSION (supersedes .10 which was closed with a hot-patch): Kokoro + KittenTTS in-container library-missing on ./stop.sh + ./run.sh; Kokoro sidecars missing 'misaki' dep — fix at the Dockerfile / sidecar pyproject layer, not by exec'ing into containers
description:
## Why this exists

Johnny-1ge.10 was closed as "Completed by agent" — yet on the operator's next `./stop.sh && ./run.sh`, every TTS failure listed in .10 came back unchanged. The agent who closed it must have run `pip install kokoro` / `pip install kittentts` inside the running api container OR inside a running sidecar venv. Neither survives a compose-rebuild, because `./run.sh` runs `docker compose up -d --build` from the source-controlled Dockerfile + lockfiles. Nothing the previous agent did landed in those source-of-truth files.

This task supersedes Johnny-1ge.10 and FIXES the same symptoms — but at the layer `./run.sh` rebuilds from, not the layer that vanishes on `./stop.sh`. **Operator language, captured verbatim so it does not get glossed:** *"It must be explicitly told that all the Docker files, all our run.sh should do their job and boot up everything properly because regular users don't really want to sign in into the containers using SSH and installing some sort of libraries in there. Everything should be in containers."*

### MANDATORY pre-read

Before any code is written, read the new top-rule at `AGENTS.md` → "Top rule: clean-install reproducibility — never 'fix' by hot-patching a running container". If the rule is unclear, escalate; do not start coding around it.

## Reproductions (all from a fresh `./stop.sh && ./run.sh`)

### Kokoro × `in-container`

> synthesis failed: kokoro library not importable for the in-container runtime: No module named 'kokoro'. Install it (`pip install kokoro`) into the api image, or switch the runtime to 'mlx-sidecar' / 'http-sidecar' and run the sidecar on the host.

The error text is honest but the resolution it suggests ("install … into the api image") was not implemented in `backend/Dockerfile`. The api image comes up without `kokoro` on a clean boot.

### Kokoro × `mlx-sidecar`

> synthesis failed: kokoro sidecar (mlx-sidecar) returned HTTP 500: {"error":"kokoro mlx synthesis failed for voice='jf_alpha' lang='j': in-memory generate() raised (Kokoro requires the optional 'misaki' package for text processing. Install it with: pip install misaki

Different failure mode but same root cause: the mlx-sidecar venv install script pulled `kokoro` but not its transitive dep `misaki`. Pinning is incomplete somewhere in `sidecars/kokoro-mlx/` (pyproject / lockfile / launcher install step).

### Kokoro × `http-sidecar`

Same `misaki` missing error. Same root cause as the mlx-sidecar variant — almost certainly the same Python dep list is used by both sidecar flavours and both are missing `misaki`.

### KittenTTS × `in-container`

> synthesis failed: kittentts library not importable for the in-container runtime: No module named 'kittentts'. Install it (pip install the KittenTTS wheel from https://github.com/KittenML/KittenTTS/releases) into the api image, or switch the runtime to 'http-sidecar' and run the sidecar on the host.

Same pattern as Kokoro × in-container — `kittentts` not added to the api image build.

### KittenTTS × `http-sidecar`

**WORKS.** The bright spot that constrains the diagnosis: the http-sidecar install for KittenTTS IS complete (pyproject pins the wheel correctly and the launcher installs it). That is the shape the Kokoro sidecars and the in-container path must match.

## What "fixed" means here

For every cell that fails, the fix lives in one of:

- `backend/Dockerfile` (or `backend/pyproject.toml` under a new optional extra that the Dockerfile installs) — if the choice is to bake the lib into the api image.
- `~/.johnny/<provider>-packages` bind-mount + a runtime-install endpoint matching the Parakeet pattern (`backend/app/services/parakeet_packages.py` is the canonical example) — if the choice is to keep the libs out of the image and ship via the `Install package` button.
- `sidecars/<provider>-<backend>/pyproject.toml` (with a lockfile or pinned versions) + `scripts/start-<provider>-sidecar.sh` (which installs the venv on first launch) — for sidecar deps. The same shape that already works for KittenTTS http-sidecar must be ported to Kokoro mlx-sidecar and Kokoro http-sidecar.
- `./run.sh` itself, for any host-side dir creation / env var the stack now needs.

**Pick ONE install strategy for the in-container path** (Dockerfile-bake vs Parakeet-style runtime install) **and apply it consistently to Kokoro AND KittenTTS** so the operator does not have to learn two install flows. Recommend the Parakeet runtime-install pattern: the image stays small, downloads are persistent in `~/.johnny/…`, and the Install button UX is already familiar from Parakeet.

## Acceptance — REQUIRES the clean-install cycle, not a hot-patch verification

Closing this issue without running the cycle below verbatim is the failure mode this task exists to eliminate.

```bash
./stop.sh                       # full reset; no cached state survives
./run.sh                        # rebuild from source-of-truth
./scripts/start-parakeet-sidecar.sh start  # if needed, per Johnny-1ge.6
# (and the analogous start-kokoro-sidecar.sh / start-kitten-sidecar.sh
#  once .6 lands; until then, the manual launch script for each is used)
```

Then, via chrome-devtools MCP, verify each cell renders working audio + a non-trivial `peak_amplitude` (per the Johnny-1ge.7 smoke contract):

- Kokoro × `in-container`
- Kokoro × `mlx-sidecar`
- Kokoro × `http-sidecar`
- KittenTTS × `in-container`
- KittenTTS × `http-sidecar`
- (and re-check Piper × {subprocess, persistent-subprocess, http-sidecar} since .10 covered them too)

Each cell that passes gets a screenshot under `.validation/Johnny-1ge.11/<provider>-<backend>.png`. Each cell that legitimately cannot pass yet (sidecar still being built etc.) gets a SKIP note with the reason.

PR description includes:
- The structured `<provider>.synth: runtime=… ttfa_ms=…` log line from `docker logs api` per cell.
- Confirmation that `./stop.sh && ./run.sh` was the verification — not a re-exec into the existing container, not a manual `pip install`.
- Diff of `backend/Dockerfile` (or `backend/app/services/<provider>_packages.py`) and the affected `sidecars/<provider>-<backend>/pyproject.toml` files so a reviewer can see at a glance what landed at the source-of-truth layer.

## Out of scope

- Improving the `johnny-tts-smoke` matrix from Johnny-1ge.7 — that smoke should catch this AFTER the fix; making it catch it BEFORE is .7's job, not this task's.
- Auto-starting sidecars on `./run.sh` — Johnny-1ge.6 owns that. This task only needs sidecars launchable via `./scripts/start-*-sidecar.sh` from a fresh checkout.
- The Piper voice picker regression (symptom A in .10). Confirm it is fixed by whoever closed .10; if not, refile as a focused sub-issue.

## Cross-links

- **Johnny-1ge.10** (closed without fixing) — the issue this one supersedes. Inspect the close-commit / PR (if any) to understand which hot-patch the previous agent applied so the same surface gets a real fix here.
- **Johnny-1ge.7** (closed) — the audio-output smoke. Once this task lands, .7's smoke must reliably catch this class of regression on a clean install or it is misconfigured.
- **Johnny-1ge.6** — auto-start sidecars + standardised CLI. Once that ships the manual launch step in the acceptance cycle goes away.
- **Johnny-1ge.8 / .9** — voice picker UX work. Indirectly affected because a broken in-container path means the picker still cannot render previews on Kokoro / Kitten.
- **AGENTS.md → "Top rule: clean-install reproducibility"** (newly added in the same PR / commit that files this issue) — the durable invariant this task exists to enforce. **Read it before coding.**
- **README.md → "Clean-install contract"** (newly added in the same PR / commit) — the operator-facing version of the same rule.
close_reason: Fixed at the source-of-truth layer (survives ./stop.sh && ./run.sh): backend/Dockerfile now installs the new 'neural-tts' extra (kokoro + kittentts wheel + misaki[en] + en_core_web_sm), with torch pinned to the CPU wheel index in pyproject [tool.uv] so the api/worker image stays lean; docker-compose.yml + run.sh add persistent ~/.johnny/{kokoro,kitten}-models bind-mounts; both Kokoro sidecar pyprojects (http + mlx) now pin misaki[en] + en_core_web_sm so a clean sidecar launch can synth offline. Covers Kokoro/KittenTTS in-container + Kokoro http/mlx-sidecar misaki regressions.

title: TTS test surface broken across providers on a CLEAN install: Piper voice picker empty, Kokoro+KittenTTS in-container 'No module' errors, Kokoro sidecars HTTP 500 'no .wav output'
description:
## Symptom cluster — TTS test surface is broken across multiple providers

Operator opens Settings → Providers → TTS, picks a provider, tries to preview a voice (either via the in-row voice picker or the **Play sample** button in the modal footer). Each of the three local TTS providers fails in a distinct, reproducible way. Reported in one batch so a single agent can untangle the shared and per-provider causes together.

### A. Piper — voice picker is empty + "voice ID required" error

- The voice SELECT in the Local Piper modal shows nothing pickable. Click submit → error: **"voice ID required"**.
- The previous functionality (browse / install / play sample / delete installed Piper voice from the modal) is GONE from this surface. Either it has been replaced by a stub that does not load voices yet, or the in-progress unified voice picker (Johnny-1ge.8) is partially wired and the data-loading half is missing.
- Because no voice can be selected, Piper's `subprocess` runtime AND its `persistent-subprocess` runtime cannot be tested at all from the UI. The operator strongly suspects `persistent-subprocess` has its own bug but cannot confirm without first restoring voice selection.

### B. Kokoro — `in-container` runtime: library not installed in api image

Selecting the **In-container (kokoro in the api process)** runtime and clicking the per-voice preview button OR the Play sample button in the footer returns:

> synthesis failed: kokoro library not importable for the in-container runtime: No module named 'kokoro'. Install it (`pip install kokoro`) into the api image, or switch the runtime to 'mlx-sidecar' / 'http-sidecar' and run the sidecar on the host.

The error message is honest but the UX is broken: the in-container option is selectable in the schema (Johnny-1ge.3 wired it), the runtime is the default in some flows, and clicking Play sample is the most natural first-action — so a clean install lands the operator on a hard failure.

### C. Kokoro — `mlx-sidecar` AND `http-sidecar`: empty .wav output (HTTP 500)

Same provider, both sidecar runtimes, same error:

> synthesis failed: kokoro sidecar (mlx-sidecar) returned HTTP 500: {"error":"generate_audio produced no .wav output for voice='af_heart' lang='a' model='prince-canuma/Kokoro-82M' (checked ['/var/folders/rm/z2dzcvg933jcnv6709dyjr3w0000gn/T/kokoro-mlx-cl108ru_/out.wav'])"}

The sidecar process runs, the HTTP round-trip works, the synthesiser is called — but no audio file appears on disk where the sidecar then looks for it. This is the exact silent-output failure pattern that prompted Johnny-1ge.7 (the audio output validation smoke). Fixing it is part of the scope of this bug; preventing its return is the scope of .7.

### D. KittenTTS — `in-container` runtime: library not installed in api image

Symmetric to (B):

> synthesis failed: kittentts library not importable for the in-container runtime: No module named 'kittentts'. Install it (pip install the KittenTTS wheel from https://github.com/KittenML/KittenTTS/releases) into the api image, or switch the runtime to 'http-sidecar' and run the sidecar on the host.

### E. KittenTTS — `http-sidecar` runtime: WORKS

This is the one bright spot, and it constrains the diagnosis: the sidecar dispatch in `parakeet_stt.py`-style code IS working end-to-end for at least one provider, so the umbrella problem is NOT the sidecar HTTP path. The remaining failures are per-provider library wiring + the Kokoro sidecar-side empty-output bug + the Piper voice picker regression.

## What needs to be fixed (per provider)

### Piper

- Restore voice selection in the modal. Either:
    - Bring back the previous browse / install / play / delete component if Johnny-1ge.8 has not landed yet, OR
    - Finish wiring the unified voice picker (Johnny-1ge.8) backed by `PiperTTS.list_voices()` so the SELECT actually populates.
- With voice selection working, verify Piper `subprocess` plays a sample. Then verify `persistent-subprocess` plays a sample. If `persistent-subprocess` does NOT work, fix it as part of this bug (the operator predicted this and they are usually right).

### Kokoro

- In-container runtime: either bake the `kokoro` package into `backend/Dockerfile` as an optional extra (e.g. `--extra local-kokoro`), OR adopt the Parakeet-style runtime install pattern (`Install package` button → `~/.johnny/kokoro-packages` bind-mount). Pick whichever fits the operator's existing mental model — Parakeet's runtime install is the precedent.
- mlx-sidecar / http-sidecar runtimes: trace the `generate_audio produced no .wav output` path. Likely root causes (in priority order):
    - `kokoro` / `mlx-audio` API drift: the synthesis call returns the audio in-memory but the sidecar still reads from a temp file that the library no longer writes. Switch to in-memory return.
    - Voice / language tuple mismatch: `voice='af_heart' lang='a'` is the default; verify the library accepts that combination.
    - Temp dir permissions or cleanup race: less likely but easy to rule out.
- Whatever the root cause: assert non-empty wav at the sidecar layer BEFORE returning 200, and have it surface a real 500 with the actionable cause when zero bytes were produced.

### KittenTTS

- In-container runtime: same call as for Kokoro — bake into Dockerfile as an optional extra, OR adopt the Parakeet runtime install pattern. Match the choice made for Kokoro so the operator does not have to learn two install flows.
- http-sidecar already works — verify no regression after the in-container fix.

## Required chrome-devtools MCP verification

After every fix, run this trace per provider × runtime cell and screenshot the result:

1. `./scripts/start-chrome.sh`
2. Load tools: `mcp__chrome-devtools__navigate_page`, `take_snapshot`, `click`, `take_screenshot`, `list_console_messages`.
3. Navigate to http://localhost:5173/providers.
4. Add or open the TTS provider under test.
5. Pick the runtime under test (and start the matching sidecar via `./scripts/start-parakeet-sidecar.sh` / `start-piper-sidecar.sh` / `start-kitten-sidecar.sh` / `start-kokoro-sidecar.sh` if applicable).
6. Pick a voice from the voice picker. Click the per-voice preview button. Assert the response payload has non-empty `audio_bytes` AND a non-trivial `peak_amplitude` (per the Johnny-1ge.7 contract). Assert the audio element actually plays.
7. Click **Play sample** in the modal footer. Assert the same.
8. Screenshot before/after into `.validation/tts-fix/<provider>-<runtime>.png`.
9. Pull the structured `<provider>.synth: runtime=… ttfa_ms=…` line from `docker logs api` and include it in the PR description.

Cells the matrix must cover:
- Piper × subprocess
- Piper × persistent-subprocess
- Piper × http-sidecar
- Kokoro × in-container
- Kokoro × mlx-sidecar
- Kokoro × http-sidecar
- KittenTTS × in-container
- KittenTTS × http-sidecar

## Acceptance

- Each of the eight cells above renders a working preview when the appropriate sidecar (if any) is running.
- Voice picker on the Piper modal lists Piper voices and lets the operator install / delete / preview the same way it did before the regression.
- Error messages on every failure path name the runtime, the voice, and a concrete next step — no opaque "synthesis failed" with no detail.
- `johnny-tts-smoke` (Johnny-1ge.7) returns zero on every cell that has its sidecar running, and SKIP (not FAIL) on cells whose sidecar is intentionally stopped.
- Screenshots from the chrome-devtools MCP run attached to the PR via local `.validation/tts-fix/` references.

## Cross-links

- **Johnny-1ge.7** (in-progress, P1) — End-to-end audio output validation. This bug surfaces the exact silent-failure modes .7 is being built to catch; fixing them is in scope here, preventing their return is in scope there. The two should land together if practical.
- **Johnny-1ge.8** (open, P2) — Unified voice picker UX. The Piper voice-picker regression (symptom A) likely lives at the intersection of this work and whatever shipped for Piper voice browsing in Johnny-1ge.1.
- **Johnny-1ge.1** (closed) — Piper runtime picker (subprocess / persistent-subprocess / http-sidecar). The persistent-subprocess path landed here; verify it as part of this bug.
- **Johnny-1ge.2** (open) — KittenTTS provider. Same lesson applies if/when its in-container path needs the wheel installation.
- **Johnny-1ge.3** (closed) — Kokoro provider. The mlx-sidecar empty-output bug lives in code that landed here.
- **Johnny-1ge.6** (open) — auto-start sidecars + standardised CLI. Once that ships, every sidecar in the verification matrix above starts itself; until then, the verification script in `.6` carries the manual launch step.
notes: **Operator follow-up — reproduction is on a CLEAN install.** Reproduced after running `./stop.sh` and `./run.sh` from a clean repo state, then opening the Providers page and trying to add each TTS provider. This is NOT a stale-state / migration artefact: the failure modes are what a brand-new operator sees on first contact with each provider. Treats this as the primary boot UX bug for the TTS surface, not a stale-cache regression. The `stop.sh` step removes `-v` volumes so the providers seed (per Johnny-d3e) runs fresh too — the seed itself may need updating once the install path for Kokoro / KittenTTS is decided (runtime-install via Parakeet-style button vs Dockerfile extras).

title: (BUG) noVNC 'Replace session' manual-email entry rejects the email of the very bot being replaced — 'already used for meeting bot ID 1' when replacing bot 1
description:
## Symptom

Operator hit the email-scrape failure tracked under Johnny-ckz.26: a Workspace account signed in successfully through noVNC, but the supervisor could not scrape the email, so the bot row was saved as `unknown-51078bb5@johnny.local`. To recover, the operator clicked **Replace session** on the same bot row and was offered a manual email entry. They typed their real address. The backend rejected:

> this email address is already being used for meeting bot with ID 1

— but bot ID 1 **is the very row being replaced**. The validator is checking email uniqueness against ALL bot rows, including the row whose placeholder email the operator is trying to overwrite.

Result: the documented recovery path for Johnny-ckz.26 cannot be completed. Bots stuck with the placeholder address have no working route back to their real email.

## Reproduction

1. Sign in a Workspace bot through the noVNC flow such that the email scrape fails (Johnny-ckz.26 reproduces this; any Workspace account does the trick).
2. Bot row gets saved with a placeholder email (e.g. `unknown-51078bb5@johnny.local`).
3. On the Settings / Bots row, click **Replace session**.
4. When the modal offers manual email entry, type the real email of the Google account that just signed in.
5. Backend returns the 409 above, referencing the SAME bot the operator is trying to fix.

## Likely cause

The email-uniqueness query during the manual-email step of the Replace flow does not exclude the bot row that owns the current sign-in session. It looks like a one-line bug:

- The `rename_account` endpoint at `backend/app/api/bot_signin.py:460-497` already does the right thing — it excludes `collision.id != row.id` at line 487. The Replace-session manual-email path takes a different code path that does NOT carry the `current_bot_id` through to the uniqueness check.
- Candidate sites to audit:
    - The noVNC sign-in completion endpoint that finalises a signin into an account row (the `_resolve_account_for_signin` shape around `bot_signin.py:161-205`). Verify whether the "manual email override during Replace" branch passes a self-exclude id.
    - The "auto_replace" path in `backend/app/api/browser_sessions.py` (referenced at lines 106 and 832) — if Replace session reuses this and routes the email through it, the same omission lives there.
    - The frontend modal (the noVNC sign-in modal in `frontend/src/routes/settings/+page.svelte`) may simply fail to send the `current_bot_id` in the request payload, making this a frontend fix.

## Fix

Whichever endpoint handles the "user typed an email manually during Replace session" branch:

1. Accept (or already accept and just ignore) a `current_bot_id` parameter.
2. Exclude that id from the uniqueness query: `WHERE email = :new_email AND id != :current_bot_id`.
3. If the email matches the very row being replaced AND that row is currently a placeholder (`unknown-*@johnny.local`), treat the call as a rename — same semantics as `rename_account` — instead of a fresh claim.
4. If the email matches a DIFFERENT real bot row, keep rejecting (that case is correct — the operator is trying to attach a sign-in to the wrong bot).

Tests for each branch:
- Replace session on bot N, type bot Ns own placeholder-replacement: accepted, row renamed.
- Replace session on bot N, type bot Ms email where M is real: rejected.
- Replace session on bot N, type bot Ns email where bot N already has the real email (no-op): accepted as no-change.

## Acceptance

- Operator can replace session on a placeholder-email bot, type the real email, click Submit, and the bot row updates to that email.
- No regression to the existing rename flow at `bot_signin.py:460-497`.
- Browser-validated via chrome-devtools MCP: drive the Settings / Bots page, trigger Replace, complete with manual email, confirm the bot row reflects the new email.
- New backend tests cover the three branches above.

## Dependencies + cross-links

- Blocked-on-context-of: **Johnny-ckz.26** — the original email-scrape failure that produces the placeholder address this bug stops the operator from fixing. Should be reviewed in the same PR if practical.
- Related: **Johnny-105** (closed) — original noVNC sign-in containerisation + endpoints + modal; bug landed somewhere in the Replace branch that ticket added.
- Related: **Johnny-ckz.23** (closed) — sign-in method picker (CLI+upload alongside noVNC); the CLI+upload path may not exhibit this bug, which is itself a useful diagnostic comparison.
- Related: **Johnny-ckz.27** (open) — sidebar z-index bug in the same modals; not a fix dependency, just adjacency for whoever picks this up and notices.

title: End-to-end test matrix: backend integration + chrome-devtools MCP browser tests across personality CRUD → assign → session-start → verify
description:
## Why this exists

The personality library only works if the chain from "operator clicks Create" through "the bot in the meeting actually uses that LLM + that voice + that system prompt" holds end to end. Per-sub-task tests verify each layer in isolation; this sub-task verifies the chain.

The operator explicitly called out automated tests + browser tests as a requirement for this epic. This is where that promise lives.

## Scope

### A. Backend integration tests

In `backend/tests/integration/test_personality_e2e.py` — exercises against a live test DB + a real api + faked provider adapters (so we do not pay LLM cost in CI):

- Create two personalities A and B with different LLM provider rows and different TTS provider rows.
- Spin up a fake meeting session passing personality A; assert the loaded LLM is provider A's, the loaded TTS is provider A's, and the system prompt contains personality A's description verbatim.
- Same for personality B.
- Set personality B as default; spin up a session with no personality_id; assert provider B is loaded.
- Deactivate B's LLM provider; spin up a session targeting B; assert the structured `personality.fallback:` log fires AND a global default is used AND the session UI gets the fallback-warning payload.
- Delete B's TTS provider; assert B survives, `tts_provider_id` is NULL, fallback fires same as above.
- Delete A while A is the default: refused with 409.

### B. Browser tests via chrome-devtools MCP

In `backend/tests/e2e_browser/test_personalities_browser.py` (or wherever the existing chrome-devtools MCP tests live; verify the path during scoping). Cover the full operator flow:

- Navigate to `/personalities`, click "New personality", fill the form (name, description, LLM, TTS via the unified picker), click Preview on the TTS voice and assert audio plays, save.
- Clone the resulting personality, edit the description, save.
- Set the clone as default; assert the default badge moves.
- Navigate to a calendar event, pick the new personality, save the event.
- Start that meeting (or its playground equivalent — pick whichever is reproducible in the existing harness); assert the in-session character badge shows the right name; assert the chat surface uses the right voice.
- Delete the non-default personality; refresh; assert it is gone.
- Try to delete the default; assert the UI refuses with the expected message.
- Capture screenshots before/after for the PR description (kept under the gitignored `.validation/` path per the rule).

### C. Wiring into CI

- Backend integration tests run in the existing `uv run pytest` matrix.
- Browser tests run in the existing chrome-devtools MCP test stage; if that stage does not exist yet as CI, document the manual-run command in the PR + open a follow-up to automate.

### D. Regression coverage

Every closed sub-task in this epic gets at least one cell in the matrix that would catch its own regression. Cross-check: read the acceptance criteria of .oly.1 through .oly.5 and confirm at least one assertion in .oly.6 maps to it.

## Acceptance

- `uv run pytest backend/tests/integration/test_personality_e2e.py` passes.
- The chrome-devtools MCP suite passes manually before the epic closes; if/when CI is wired, it gates merges.
- Coverage report shows the new test file hits every endpoint and every fallback branch in the resolver.
- PR for this sub-task includes screenshots from the browser run under `.validation/personalities/`.

## Dependencies

Blocked-on Johnny-oly.2, .3, .4, .5 — all must land for the e2e flow to execute. Can scaffold the test file structure earlier in parallel.

title: Pipeline + decision-making revision: stop silent drops, enforce decision↔utterance parity, expose the bot's reasoning to the operator
description:
## Why this exists

Operator session at http://localhost:5173/sessions/14 shows two distinct failure modes on the default playground prompt (no custom instructions, nothing fancy):

1. **Silent drops** — the operator asked the bot to "tell us the progress for the upcoming week" and the bot just ignored the question. No reply, no error, no visible reason in the chat or decisions surfaces.
2. **Decision ↔ utterance divergence** — the decisions panel recommended one phrasing, but the bot actually spoke something different in the chat. Repeatedly. The operator cannot tell whether the decision system is being bypassed, overridden, or simply ignored downstream.

These are not "tune the prompt" problems. The operator already noted the instructions were defaults. The complaint is that the pipeline + decision-making layer is unreliable AND opaque — and the right fix is to take the whole pipeline + decision plumbing apart, find the gaps (silent drops, divergence, missing audit trail), redesign so divergence is impossible by construction, and surface a "what the bot is thinking" timeline so the operator can read the bots reasoning per turn the same way they read a debugger.

This is the scope captured here. Sub-tasks under this issue carve it into independently shippable pieces; the parent is the place to discuss the overall design and the dependency order between them.

## Operator’s ask, restated structurally

- An agent picking this up MUST first analyse session 14 end-to-end (transcripts, decisions, bot utterances, pipeline event log, LLM traces) before proposing any refactor. The bug is concrete and reproducible there; everything downstream depends on understanding what actually went wrong.
- The agent MUST then catalogue every observed gap between (a) what the user said, (b) what the router/decision system decided, (c) what the LLM was asked to produce, and (d) what the bot actually spoke. Each gap is a candidate for being made impossible by construction OR loudly visible in the UI.
- The agent MUST propose a redesign of the pipeline + decision-making layer that closes those gaps. The PRD shape (Context / Goals / Non-goals / Architecture / Acceptance) used by tasks/prd-piper-tts-runtime-options.md is the canonical example.
- The operator’s priority order, in their words: **decisions** matter most → **observability** of the bots reasoning second → **performance** a distant third. Optimise the refactor accordingly.

## Sub-tasks (filed as children below)

1. Root-cause analysis from session 14 — replay the session, document every silent drop + every decision/utterance divergence with exact pipeline-event timestamps, deliver a written failure-mode catalogue. **MUST happen first.**
2. Decision ↔ utterance parity: single source of truth for the spoken text — the decisions surface and the chat surface read from the same canonical record, or any divergence raises a visible error rather than going to the speaker.
3. Pipeline reliability: never silently drop a user turn — every transcribed user utterance ends in either (a) a final spoken reply, (b) an approved-but-not-yet-spoken suggestion, or (c) a recorded reason for not replying, surfaced to the operator. No turn falls off the floor invisibly.
4. "What is the bot thinking" — per-turn reasoning timeline surfaced in the session UI. STT in → router classification → context selection → LLM prompt → LLM raw output → guard/filter decisions → final spoken text. Customer-readable, not just dev logs.
5. Offline replay harness against persisted session history — take any past session id, replay its transcript through the current pipeline offline, assert the produced decisions and utterances match the recorded ones; lights up regressions in CI.

## Cross-links — earlier work that informs this

Closed issues whose context the agent should re-read before refactoring:

- **Johnny-vgl** — "Review and standardize bot free mode speech decision logic". The previous attempt at this exact territory; whatever decision logic landed there is the starting point for what to refactor here.
- **Johnny-cdw** — "Approving a pending suggestion doesn’t make the bot actually speak it". Same divergence pattern (decisions panel says one thing, bot does another) at a different point in the pipeline.
- **Johnny-arh** — "Bot speaks over user mid-sentence". Floor-management / partial-transcript gating; relevant to the silent-drop symptom because the same gate can over-suppress legitimate turns.
- **Johnny-ckz.14** — "STT artifacts trigger AI replies — no noise-floor gate". Same gate, opposite failure mode (false-positive replies). The redesign has to balance both.
- **Johnny-har** — "STT transcription of participants must never pause while bot is speaking or thinking". Relevant to the "Where did my question go?" silent-drop symptom.
- **Johnny-7qp** — "Bot loses conversation context mid-session". Reliability precedent.
- **Johnny-ckz.7** — "Per-session activity / timing log surfaced in chat history". Observability precedent — likely the substrate the new reasoning timeline (sub-task 4) extends.
- **Johnny-klh** — "Playground transcripts mislabel speakers". Reliability precedent.

Still-open issue that WILL collide with this refactor:

- **Johnny-ckz.25** — "Consolidate free_auto_speak into autonomous — remove FREE_AUTO_SPEAK BotMode". Touches the same decision-mode plumbing; sequence with sub-task 2 (parity) or absorb into it.

## Acceptance for the umbrella

- All five sub-tasks closed.
- Session 14 replays end-to-end through the new pipeline with no silent drops; every user turn lands in one of the three documented outcomes.
- The decisions surface and the chat surface for any given turn either show the same text, or the divergence is rendered as an explicit "spoke X instead of recommended Y because Z" line — never silently.
- A new operator opening any session can read the per-turn reasoning timeline and explain why the bot spoke what it spoke, without reading the source code or docker logs.
- The offline replay harness runs in CI against at least three persisted sessions including session 14, and gates merges.

## Non-goals

- Not changing the LLM / STT / TTS providers. Provider choice is orthogonal.
- Not tuning the default playground prompt. The complaint is that even with sane defaults the pipeline misbehaves; prompt tuning hides that.
- Not adding new bot modes. Consolidating the existing ones (Johnny-ckz.25) is in scope; inventing new ones is not.

## Reference for the agent picking this up

- Session under investigation: http://localhost:5173/sessions/14
- Canonical PRD shape: `tasks/prd-piper-tts-runtime-options.md`
- Pipeline source (current): `backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/`, `backend/app/services/browser_pipeline_runner.py`, `backend/app/services/session_scheduler.py`
- Decisions persistence: search `backend/app/db/models.py` for the decisions / approvals / utterances tables
