title: (BUG) Gemini model SELECT validator rejects models fetched live from Gemini's own API — 'gemini-3.5' returned by the catalog can't be saved
description:
## Symptom

Operator opens Providers → Gemini → Model dropdown. The dropdown is populated from the live model catalog fetched from Gemini’s API (per Johnny-9eq / Johnny-a9e). The operator selects `gemini-3.5` — a real model the API returned — clicks Save, and the form rejects with:

> Model must be one of: gemini-1.5-flash, gemini-1.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-pro

The model the operator just picked from the dropdown is not in the allow-list. Save fails. The operator cannot use any model newer than what was hardcoded at build time, even when Gemini’s own API advertises it.

## Root cause

`backend/app/providers/gemini_llm.py:158-164` declares the `model` field as a `FieldType.SELECT` with a hardcoded four-element `options` tuple:

```python
FieldOption(value="gemini-2.5-flash", label="gemini-2.5-flash (fast)"),
FieldOption(value="gemini-2.5-pro",   label="gemini-2.5-pro"),
FieldOption(value="gemini-1.5-flash", label="gemini-1.5-flash (legacy)"),
FieldOption(value="gemini-1.5-pro",   label="gemini-1.5-pro (legacy)"),
```

The schema validator (`backend/app/providers/schema_validation.py`, used by the PATCH/POST providers handler) enforces `value ∈ options` for SELECT fields and surfaces the rejection as the exact error message above. The frontend separately populates the dropdown from the live catalog endpoint, so the OPTIONS the user sees and the OPTIONS the backend validates against are two different lists — the live catalog is informational only.

This is the inverse of what Johnny-9eq was meant to deliver: fetching the catalog dynamically was supposed to free us from hardcoded lists, but the SELECT validator still enforces the static one.

The same shape is likely present on OpenAI / Anthropic / Ollama (Johnny-a9e is still open). This fix needs to land in a way that all dynamic-catalog providers benefit, not just Gemini.

## Fix

Two parts:

### A. Schema: a "dynamic catalog" hint on SELECT fields

Add a flag (`dynamic_options: bool = False`, or equivalently `catalog_endpoint: str | None`) to `FieldDef`. When set:
- The frontend renders the dropdown sourced from the live catalog instead of the static `options` tuple.
- The backend validator SKIPS the `value ∈ options` membership check. Non-empty string + reasonable length cap is the only constraint.
- The static `options` tuple stays as the fallback list used when the live catalog fetch fails (the dropdown should not be empty offline).

### B. Apply to every LLM that has a live model catalog

- Gemini (this bug): set `dynamic_options=True` on the model field at gemini_llm.py:158.
- OpenAI / Anthropic / Ollama / OpenAI-compatible: same flag. Verify each adapter actually has a live catalog wired (some may still need Johnny-a9e to finish first).

### C. Regression test

A unit test that constructs a `FieldDef(type=SELECT, dynamic_options=True, options=("a", "b"))` and validates a payload with `value="c"` — must pass. Same test for `dynamic_options=False` — must fail with the existing error. Keeps the static-allow-list semantics intact for fields like Parakeet `device` where we DO want the membership check.

## Acceptance

- Operator selects any model the live Gemini catalog returns, clicks Save, no rejection.
- Selecting a non-existent model id by hand (e.g. via curl PATCH) still surfaces a clean error from the upstream API on first use (not a hardcoded schema rejection).
- OpenAI / Anthropic / Ollama benefit from the same fix; once their live catalogs are wired (Johnny-a9e), no further validator changes are needed.
- Schema unit tests cover both `dynamic_options=True` (skip) and `dynamic_options=False` (enforce) paths.
- Browser-validated via chrome-devtools MCP: pick a non-hardcoded model from each providers dropdown, save, confirm it persists and the bot actually uses it.

## Cross-links

- Johnny-9eq (closed) — "fetch model list dynamically from each providers API instead of hardcoding". Delivered the catalog endpoints + the dropdown source. This bug is the validator half that was missed.
- Johnny-a9e (open, P3) — "Live model-catalog fetch for OpenAI / Anthropic / Ollama in /providers modal". The fix here removes one of that issues blockers and should bump its priority once the schema flag lands.

## Out of scope

- Validating the model on the upstream API side at save time (would slow down the form roundtrip with a per-save network call to every provider; the existing /test button already covers that explicitly when the operator wants it).
- Refactoring the `FieldType.SELECT` enum into separate static / dynamic variants. The bool flag on `FieldDef` keeps the change small.

## Reference

- Adapter: `backend/app/providers/gemini_llm.py:158-164` (the hardcoded options).
- Validator: `backend/app/providers/schema_validation.py` (search for the `SELECT` branch / "must be one of" message).
- Live catalog source: `backend/app/providers/gemini_llm.py:558-610` (the `_fetch_catalog` shape that already exists — proves the live list is reachable, it just is not being used to relax validation).

title: 'What is the bot thinking' — per-turn reasoning timeline in the session UI (STT in → router → context → LLM → guard → speak)
description:
## Why this exists

The operator opened session 14 and could not answer "why did the bot say X instead of Y?" without reading docker logs or the source. Today the decisions panel shows a recommendation; the chat shows an utterance; nothing in the UI tells the operator what happened between those two columns. That gap is the root of the operators trust complaint and the reason a refactor without observability would re-introduce the same confusion.

This task ships the customer-facing surface that turns the new canonical pipeline (sub-tasks .28.2 and .28.3) into something the operator can READ. One row per turn, expandable into a vertical timeline that walks every step the bot took, in plain language.

## Shape

### A. Per-turn collapsed row (default view)

For every turn in the session, render one row in the chat surface with:

- Speaker + final user utterance.
- Routers classification (one short word: `question`, `command`, `chitchat`, `noise`, etc. — comes from the existing router output).
- Bots terminal state (from sub-task .28.3): `replied` / `pending-approval` / `no-reply`.
- The spoken text (if `replied`) or the suggestion (if `pending-approval`) or the no-reply reason (if `no-reply`).
- An icon if the canonical record carries a divergence (sub-task .28.2) — clicking it expands the row.

### B. Expanded reasoning timeline

A vertical timeline inside the row, one entry per pipeline event for the turn:

1. **Heard** — STT final transcript + confidence, timestamp.
2. **Classified as** — router output + a one-line rationale string emitted by the router.
3. **Context selected** — which prior turns / which calendar event metadata went into the prompt (link, not the full text).
4. **Asked the model** — a "View prompt" disclosure that shows the full system + user messages. Default-collapsed because it is long.
5. **Model said** — the raw LLM output (text + any tool calls). "View raw" disclosure for the JSON.
6. **Guards / filters** — every suppressor or override that fired (sub-task .28.3 catalogue), in order, with the reason each emitted.
7. **Final decision** — the canonical `decision_recommended_text` + `final_text` + `divergence_reason` from sub-task .28.2.
8. **Spoke** — TTS in, audio rendered, timestamp.

Each entry shows the elapsed milliseconds from the previous step so the operator can spot which stage stalled.

### C. Plain-language rendering

The timeline is the operator-facing surface; technical jargon stays in the disclosure panels. Default labels are written for someone who has not read the source — "Heard you ask a question", "Decided to answer", "Filter blocked the reply because: <reason>". Hover tooltips link to the structured event name for engineers who want it.

### D. Live updates during the session

The timeline updates in real time during an active session (WebSocket already exists per Johnny-c8t / Johnny-ckz.6). Operator can watch the bot think turn by turn instead of waiting for a post-meeting scroll-through.

### E. Filter / search

A turn filter chip row at the top of the session: "Show only divergences", "Show only no-replies", "Show only autonomous", "Show only approved". One click to surface the subset the operator cares about during a post-meeting review.

## Acceptance

- Every turn in a fresh session renders the collapsed row.
- Expanding any row shows the eight timeline steps in order with elapsed milliseconds.
- A turn where the canonical record carries a divergence (sub-task .28.2) shows the override explicitly in the timeline, NOT as a fine-print footnote.
- A turn that terminated `no-reply` (sub-task .28.3) shows the reason in plain language; the structured suppressor name is reachable via tooltip.
- Filter chips work; "Show only divergences" applied to session 14 surfaces exactly the rows the operator complained about, with the override now explained inline.
- Live-update path works: a turn opened during an active session updates step-by-step as the pipeline writes pipeline event rows.
- No mock data — the timeline is sourced entirely from the canonical pipeline event log; if a step is missing, that is a real bug in upstream sub-tasks, not a UI omission to paper over.

## Cross-links

- Johnny-ckz.7 (closed) — "per-session activity / timing log surfaced in chat history" is the precedent; whatever it shipped is the substrate this task extends.
- Johnny-cdw (closed) — the approval-flow divergence pattern; this UI is where the override now becomes visible instead of silent.

## Dependencies

Blocked-on Johnny-ckz.28.2 (canonical record schema) and Johnny-ckz.28.3 (terminal state + suppressor reasons). Can develop in parallel with .28.5 (replay harness).

title: Pipeline reliability: never silently drop a user turn — every transcribed utterance ends in reply / approved-pending / explicit-no-reply
description:
## Why this exists

The operator asked the bot "tell us the progress for the upcoming week" in session 14 and got no reply at all. Not "I do not know"; not "this is outside scope"; not "approval pending". Just silence. From the operator side that is indistinguishable from a crash — and there is no UI affordance that explains where the turn went.

The fix is a hard invariant: every transcribed user turn terminates in exactly one of three states, persisted and visible. No silent drops. Ever.

## The three terminal states

| State | When | What the operator sees |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `replied` | The bot actually spoke something. | Final utterance in chat, decision row in decisions panel, both reading from the canonical record (sub-task .28.2). |
| `pending-approval` | Bot mode is approval-required and an approval is queued. | "Awaiting approval" badge in chat at the turns timestamp; the suggestion text shown inline. |
| `no-reply` | Bot deliberately said nothing. | Explicit "no reply: <reason>" row in chat AND in the per-turn reasoning timeline (sub-task .28.4). Reason comes from the router/guard that suppressed: `noise-gate`, `barge-in-protection`, `off-topic-per-instructions`, `model-empty-output`, etc. |

A turn that does not reach any of these states is a bug — caught by an integration test that replays a session and asserts every transcript row links to one terminal state.

## Implementation shape (after Johnny-ckz.28.1 lands)

### A. Turn state machine

Promote the implicit per-turn lifecycle in `backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/` to an explicit state machine: STT-final → routed → LLM-called → response-decided → spoken/queued/suppressed. Each transition writes a pipeline event row; the terminal-state row gets a `terminal_state` column with one of the three values above and (for `no-reply`) a non-null `no_reply_reason`.

### B. Catch-all suppressor accounting

Every code path that today returns early from the response loop — noise gate (Johnny-ckz.14), barge-in protection (Johnny-ckz.13, Johnny-arh), partial-vs-final guard (Johnny-arh), empty-LLM-output, profanity filter, "I am thinking" cooldown, anything — must register itself as a known suppressor and write a `no-reply` terminal row when it suppresses. An early return that does not write a terminal row is rejected by a runtime assertion in dev/test builds and surfaces as a loud error in prod logs.

### C. Operator-visible "no reply" affordance

The chat surface renders `no-reply` rows as muted but visible entries: "No reply at HH:MM:SS — <reason>". Operator can click for the full reasoning timeline (Johnny-ckz.28.4). This is the thing the operator needed in session 14 and did not have.

### D. Regression test

Replay test against persisted session 14 (or an equivalent fixture if .14 is too noisy) asserts every transcript row resolves to a terminal state. The offline replay harness from sub-task .28.5 is the natural home for this.

## Acceptance

- The state machine is the only way a turn can terminate; an assertion in dev/test catches any path that returns without writing a terminal row.
- Every existing suppressor is enumerated and writes its terminal `no-reply` row with a typed reason.
- Chat renders `no-reply` rows visibly; the reason is human-readable.
- A replay of session 14 produces zero unaccounted turns. Specifically: the dropped "tell us the progress" question terminates in a labelled state (`replied` after the fix, or `no-reply` with the right reason if the routers behaviour was actually correct).
- New `pipeline.turn.terminal:` structured log line lands per turn, visible in `docker logs`.

## Cross-links

- Johnny-arh (closed) — partial-transcript gating is one of the suppressor paths; folded into the state machine, not removed.
- Johnny-ckz.14 (closed) — STT noise gate is another suppressor; same treatment.
- Johnny-ckz.13 (closed) — barge-in protection idem.
- Johnny-har (closed) — "STT must not pause while bot is speaking" — guards against a different cause of silent drops; verify the state machine does not regress it.
- Johnny-7qp (closed) — context-loss bug had a similar "where did my prior message go?" feel; reuse whatever observability shipped there.

## Dependencies

Blocked-on Johnny-ckz.28.1 (failure-mode catalogue determines which suppressors exist) and Johnny-ckz.28.2 (canonical record is where `terminal_state` lives).

title: Decision ↔ utterance parity: single source of truth so the chat and the decisions panel cannot diverge silently
description:
## Why this exists

Session 14 shows the decisions panel recommending one phrasing while the chat shows the bot spoke something else — repeatedly, with no operator-visible reason. The two surfaces are reading from different parts of the pipeline, so any drift between them goes unnoticed.

The fix is structural: one canonical record per turn for "what the bot will speak", written once, read by every surface that displays it. Anything that wants to override that record either updates it (and the change is audited) or surfaces as an explicit "spoke X instead of recommended Y because Z" line in the UI — never silently.

## What to build (after the root-cause analysis in Johnny-ckz.28.1 lands)

### A. Canonical per-turn record

A single row written when a turn finishes: `final_text` (what was actually spoken), `decision_recommended_text` (what the router/decision layer recommended), `divergence_reason` (string when the two differ, NULL otherwise), `override_actor` (which layer rewrote it: post-LLM guard, approval flow, profanity filter, etc.).

Schema lives next to the existing decisions / utterances tables — exact placement decided in the .28.1 redesign doc.

### B. Surfaces consume the canonical record

- The decisions panel reads `decision_recommended_text` and (if the row has a divergence) shows the canonical `final_text` next to it with the `divergence_reason`.
- The chat reads `final_text` only.
- The pipeline event log emits a structured `decision.override:` line every time `divergence_reason` is non-null.

### C. Invariant enforcement

A write to `final_text` that differs from `decision_recommended_text` without setting `override_actor` AND `divergence_reason` is rejected at the DB / ORM layer. Tests cover every path that writes a final utterance (autonomous mode, suggest-and-approve, free auto-speak, S2S unified runtime) and asserts the invariant holds on all of them.

### D. Backfill / migration

For sessions written before the schema change: a one-shot migration sets `decision_recommended_text` from the legacy decision row and `final_text` from the legacy utterance row; rows where they differ get a synthesised `divergence_reason="legacy: pre-parity record"` so the new surfaces render the existing history without raising the invariant.

## Acceptance

- Schema migration lands, every utterance write goes through the canonical record.
- Decisions panel shows the divergence line whenever the bot speaks something other than the recommended text.
- A constructed test session reproducing the session-14 divergence renders the override explicitly in the UI.
- Every existing test in `backend/tests/` that asserts on decisions or utterances passes against the new schema.
- The pipeline event log carries the structured `decision.override:` line, visible in `docker logs` and surfaced by Johnny-ckz.28.4 (reasoning timeline).

## Cross-links

- Johnny-cdw (closed) — "approving a pending suggestion does not make the bot speak it" is the same divergence pattern at the approval-gate stage; whatever fix landed there is now incorporated into the canonical record.
- Johnny-vgl (closed) — "review and standardize bot free mode speech decision logic" is the decision-side counterpart to this work; align with whatever invariants that issue established.
- Johnny-ckz.25 (open) — autonomous-mode consolidation will collide with this; sequence with whichever lands first.

## Dependencies

Blocked-on Johnny-ckz.28.1 (root-cause analysis must deliver the schema shape).

title: Root-cause analysis from session 14: failure-mode catalogue (silent drops + decision/utterance divergence) + redesign proposal
description:
## Why this exists

Session http://localhost:5173/sessions/14 contains concrete evidence of every failure mode the parent issue (Johnny-ckz.28) aims to fix:

- At least one user question ("tell us the progress for the upcoming week") that the bot ignored entirely.
- Multiple turns where the decisions panel recommends one phrasing but the chat shows the bot spoke something else.
- Default playground instructions, so the failure is in the pipeline plumbing, not the prompt.

This task is the analysis pass. **No code refactor here.** Output is a written failure-mode catalogue + a proposed redesign. Every downstream sub-task of Johnny-ckz.28 depends on this output, so this MUST land before .2/.3/.4/.5 start.

## What to deliver

### A. Session 14 forensic timeline

Reconstruct, end-to-end, every turn in session 14 from the persisted data:

- User utterance (STT final) + timestamp + speaker label.
- Router / decision classification + classification rationale (whatever the router emits today).
- LLM prompt actually sent (full system + context window), exact LLM output.
- Any guard / filter / approval-gate decision between LLM output and the bot saying anything.
- Final bot utterance as actually spoken (TTS in), with timestamp.

Render as a table (one row per turn) in the deliverable doc. Each row tags which gap, if any, appeared at that turn:

- `silent-drop` — user said something, no final reply emitted.
- `decision-divergence` — the decisions panel recommended X, the chat shows Y, no operator-visible reason for the swap.
- `gate-suppression` — a noise/floor/barge-in gate dropped the turn; record whether the drop was correct.
- `ok` — turn handled cleanly.

### B. Failure-mode catalogue

For every distinct failure-mode label that appeared in (A), produce:

- A one-paragraph description of the pattern.
- The code path responsible (file + line range, traced through `backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/`, the router, the LLM adapter, the response loop, the TTS handoff).
- Why it is failing today (root cause, not symptom).
- The minimum invariant the redesign must enforce to make this failure impossible by construction (preferred) OR loudly visible to the operator (acceptable fallback).

### C. Redesign proposal

A PRD-shape document (Context / Goals / Non-goals / Architecture / Acceptance — same shape as `tasks/prd-piper-tts-runtime-options.md`) covering:

- New invariants that make decision↔utterance divergence impossible OR explicit.
- The single source of truth for "what the bot will speak this turn" — who writes it, who reads it, how the chat and decisions surfaces stay in sync.
- The "no silent drops" invariant: every transcribed user turn ends in exactly one of three terminal states (final reply / approved-pending-suggestion / explicit-no-reply-with-reason).
- The reasoning-timeline data model needed by sub-task .4 (parent: .28.4).
- The minimal refactor that gets there from current code, not a clean-room rewrite.

### D. Cross-link writeup

Concise paragraph per related closed issue (Johnny-vgl, Johnny-cdw, Johnny-arh, Johnny-ckz.14, Johnny-har, Johnny-7qp, Johnny-ckz.7, Johnny-klh, Johnny-ckz.25) explaining what survives, what gets replaced, what the previous fix missed that lets the current failure-mode re-emerge.

## Acceptance

- Deliverable is a single doc at `tasks/prd-pipeline-decision-revision.md` containing sections A through D.
- Session 14 timeline is reproduced from persisted data (not hand-edited), including at least one example of each failure-mode label observed.
- The redesign proposal explicitly maps each failure-mode label to one new invariant.
- The cross-link writeup is concrete: file paths, line ranges, named functions — not "see Johnny-vgl".
- Doc is reviewed by the operator before any code work in sub-tasks .2-.5 starts.

## Out of scope (here)

- Code changes. This is analysis + design. Implementation lives in sub-tasks .2-.5.
- New decision-mode designs (autonomous vs suggest vs approval-required) — leave the current mode set alone; the failure modes appear inside whatever mode session 14 used.

## Inputs

- Session under analysis: http://localhost:5173/sessions/14
- Persisted tables: bot_sessions, decisions, transcripts, utterances, pipeline events — exact names in `backend/app/db/models.py`.
- Current pipeline source: `backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/`, `backend/app/services/browser_pipeline_runner.py`, `backend/app/services/session_scheduler.py`.

title: Pipeline + decision-making revision: stop silent drops, enforce decision↔utterance parity, expose the bot's reasoning to the operator
description:
## Why this exists

Operator session at http://localhost:5173/sessions/14 shows two distinct failure modes on the default playground prompt (no custom instructions, nothing fancy):

1. **Silent drops** — the operator asked the bot to "tell us the progress for the upcoming week" and the bot just ignored the question. No reply, no error, no visible reason in the chat or decisions surfaces.
2. **Decision ↔ utterance divergence** — the decisions panel recommended one phrasing, but the bot actually spoke something different in the chat. Repeatedly. The operator cannot tell whether the decision system is being bypassed, overridden, or simply ignored downstream.

These are not "tune the prompt" problems. The operator already noted the instructions were defaults. The complaint is that the pipeline + decision-making layer is unreliable AND opaque — and the right fix is to take the whole pipeline + decision plumbing apart, find the gaps (silent drops, divergence, missing audit trail), redesign so divergence is impossible by construction, and surface a "what the bot is thinking" timeline so the operator can read the bots reasoning per turn the same way they read a debugger.

This is the scope captured here. Sub-tasks under this issue carve it into independently shippable pieces; the parent is the place to discuss the overall design and the dependency order between them.

## Operator’s ask, restated structurally

- An agent picking this up MUST first analyse session 14 end-to-end (transcripts, decisions, bot utterances, pipeline event log, LLM traces) before proposing any refactor. The bug is concrete and reproducible there; everything downstream depends on understanding what actually went wrong.
- The agent MUST then catalogue every observed gap between (a) what the user said, (b) what the router/decision system decided, (c) what the LLM was asked to produce, and (d) what the bot actually spoke. Each gap is a candidate for being made impossible by construction OR loudly visible in the UI.
- The agent MUST propose a redesign of the pipeline + decision-making layer that closes those gaps. The PRD shape (Context / Goals / Non-goals / Architecture / Acceptance) used by tasks/prd-piper-tts-runtime-options.md is the canonical example.
- The operator’s priority order, in their words: **decisions** matter most → **observability** of the bots reasoning second → **performance** a distant third. Optimise the refactor accordingly.

## Sub-tasks (filed as children below)

1. Root-cause analysis from session 14 — replay the session, document every silent drop + every decision/utterance divergence with exact pipeline-event timestamps, deliver a written failure-mode catalogue. **MUST happen first.**
2. Decision ↔ utterance parity: single source of truth for the spoken text — the decisions surface and the chat surface read from the same canonical record, or any divergence raises a visible error rather than going to the speaker.
3. Pipeline reliability: never silently drop a user turn — every transcribed user utterance ends in either (a) a final spoken reply, (b) an approved-but-not-yet-spoken suggestion, or (c) a recorded reason for not replying, surfaced to the operator. No turn falls off the floor invisibly.
4. "What is the bot thinking" — per-turn reasoning timeline surfaced in the session UI. STT in → router classification → context selection → LLM prompt → LLM raw output → guard/filter decisions → final spoken text. Customer-readable, not just dev logs.
5. Offline replay harness against persisted session history — take any past session id, replay its transcript through the current pipeline offline, assert the produced decisions and utterances match the recorded ones; lights up regressions in CI.

## Cross-links — earlier work that informs this

Closed issues whose context the agent should re-read before refactoring:

- **Johnny-vgl** — "Review and standardize bot free mode speech decision logic". The previous attempt at this exact territory; whatever decision logic landed there is the starting point for what to refactor here.
- **Johnny-cdw** — "Approving a pending suggestion doesn’t make the bot actually speak it". Same divergence pattern (decisions panel says one thing, bot does another) at a different point in the pipeline.
- **Johnny-arh** — "Bot speaks over user mid-sentence". Floor-management / partial-transcript gating; relevant to the silent-drop symptom because the same gate can over-suppress legitimate turns.
- **Johnny-ckz.14** — "STT artifacts trigger AI replies — no noise-floor gate". Same gate, opposite failure mode (false-positive replies). The redesign has to balance both.
- **Johnny-har** — "STT transcription of participants must never pause while bot is speaking or thinking". Relevant to the "Where did my question go?" silent-drop symptom.
- **Johnny-7qp** — "Bot loses conversation context mid-session". Reliability precedent.
- **Johnny-ckz.7** — "Per-session activity / timing log surfaced in chat history". Observability precedent — likely the substrate the new reasoning timeline (sub-task 4) extends.
- **Johnny-klh** — "Playground transcripts mislabel speakers". Reliability precedent.

Still-open issue that WILL collide with this refactor:

- **Johnny-ckz.25** — "Consolidate free_auto_speak into autonomous — remove FREE_AUTO_SPEAK BotMode". Touches the same decision-mode plumbing; sequence with sub-task 2 (parity) or absorb into it.

## Acceptance for the umbrella

- All five sub-tasks closed.
- Session 14 replays end-to-end through the new pipeline with no silent drops; every user turn lands in one of the three documented outcomes.
- The decisions surface and the chat surface for any given turn either show the same text, or the divergence is rendered as an explicit "spoke X instead of recommended Y because Z" line — never silently.
- A new operator opening any session can read the per-turn reasoning timeline and explain why the bot spoke what it spoke, without reading the source code or docker logs.
- The offline replay harness runs in CI against at least three persisted sessions including session 14, and gates merges.

## Non-goals

- Not changing the LLM / STT / TTS providers. Provider choice is orthogonal.
- Not tuning the default playground prompt. The complaint is that even with sane defaults the pipeline misbehaves; prompt tuning hides that.
- Not adding new bot modes. Consolidating the existing ones (Johnny-ckz.25) is in scope; inventing new ones is not.

## Reference for the agent picking this up

- Session under investigation: http://localhost:5173/sessions/14
- Canonical PRD shape: `tasks/prd-piper-tts-runtime-options.md`
- Pipeline source (current): `backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/`, `backend/app/services/browser_pipeline_runner.py`, `backend/app/services/session_scheduler.py`
- Decisions persistence: search `backend/app/db/models.py` for the decisions / approvals / utterances tables
- Session UI: `frontend/src/routes/sessions/[id]/+page.svelte` (and the playground page) — where the reasoning timeline needs to land

title: End-to-end audio output validation for every TTS provider × runtime combination
description:
## Why this exists

We hit a real silent-failure today: `kokoro sidecar (mlx-sidecar) returned HTTP 500: {"error":"generate_audio produced no .wav output"}`. The sidecar process was up, the HTTP round-trip succeeded, the api reported a finite `latency_ms`, but the PCM body was empty — so the user clicked Play sample and **heard nothing**. The 500 came from the sidecar internals, not from a missing voice file or a wrong URL.

The runtime picker turns one provider into N runtimes. We need a uniform end-to-end smoke that proves **every (provider × runtime × voice)** triple produces audible PCM, not just a successful HTTP response. Without it, the next combination that ships will repeat the same silent-failure pattern.

## Scope

### A. Add a strict "produces audio" assertion to the existing TTS test path

The existing `/play_sample` (catalog) and equivalent test endpoint already returns `latency_ms`. Extend the SAME response to include:

- `audio_bytes` — length of the PCM body returned by the runtime.
- `audio_ms` — duration in ms derived from byte count + sample rate.
- `peak_amplitude` — max abs sample value, normalised to [0, 1]. Anything ≤ ~0.001 is effectively silence.
- `runtime` — which runtime served the call (already filed under Johnny-1ge but call it out here so the smoke can assert it).

The api treats a response as OK only when all three hold:

- `audio_bytes >= floor` (default 16_000 bytes — 0.5 s of 16 kHz mono S16LE),
- `audio_ms` within 50–500% of the input text length × an empirical chars-per-second-of-speech constant (catches "synthesised 0.2 s of audio for a 6-word prompt" type bugs),
- `peak_amplitude >= 0.01` (rejects all-zero PCM that the kokoro bug produced).

Any failure becomes a `TTSError("runtime X produced no audible output: ...")` with the three numbers in the message so the user sees the diagnosis, not just "synthesis failed".

### B. New backend smoke: `johnny-tts-smoke`

A standalone command (like `johnny-smoke`) that iterates every saved TTS provider row × every runtime supported by that provider × the first available voice, and runs the strict /play_sample assertion above against a short canonical phrase (`"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."`). Prints one PASS / FAIL / SKIP row per cell; SKIP when a sidecar is offline or a voice is missing on disk. Exits non-zero on any FAIL.

```
$ uv run johnny-tts-smoke
piper        subprocess         PASS  93 ms, 18400 bytes, peak 0.31
piper        persistent-subproc PASS  47 ms, 18120 bytes, peak 0.30
piper        http-sidecar       SKIP  sidecar offline (curl http://localhost:8775/health)
kokoro       in-container       PASS  220 ms, 21200 bytes, peak 0.42
kokoro       mlx-sidecar        FAIL  0 ms, 0 bytes, peak 0.00  ← the bug we just saw
kokoro       http-sidecar       PASS  180 ms, 21100 bytes, peak 0.42
kittentts    in-container       PASS  110 ms, 19800 bytes, peak 0.28
```

Wired into the existing smoke test surface in `backend/johnny/smoketest/` so `johnny-setup` and CI can run it.

### C. Reproduce + fix kokoro mlx-sidecar specifically

The kokoro mlx-sidecar reproduces this every time (or sometimes — measure both). Open the sidecar log, find the `generate_audio produced no .wav output` site, and fix the cause. Likely candidates:

- Voice ID not in the loaded checkpoint (silent fallback to empty).
- Text length below the model’s minimum frame budget.
- mlx-audio API drift between what the sidecar calls and what the library returns (the sidecar may be reading the wrong field — e.g. `result.wav_bytes` instead of `result.audio` or `result.samples`).
- The `wav` mode is disabled and only `raw` is supported — sidecar should fall back.

Whatever the root cause: assert at the sidecar layer that the wav payload is non-empty before returning, and surface a real 500 with the actionable cause in the body, not a generic message.

### D. Browser validation

For each (provider × runtime) cell that PASS-es the smoke, drive the Providers modal via chrome-devtools MCP: switch the Runtime dropdown, click Play sample, assert the audio element actually renders + the latency badge reads back the runtime label. Screenshot for the PR.

## Acceptance

- `johnny-tts-smoke` exists, returns one row per (provider × runtime × voice), exits non-zero on any FAIL.
- The new `audio_bytes` / `audio_ms` / `peak_amplitude` fields land on the play-sample response and the frontend latency badge surfaces a "silent" warning when peak < threshold.
- The specific kokoro mlx-sidecar failure is reproduced in CI and fixed.
- All currently-shipping (provider × runtime) cells pass the smoke at HEAD.
- A regression test asserts an all-zero PCM body raises `TTSError` with a clear message — protects against the next silent-failure variant.
- README "Local TTS providers" table gains a "verified via smoke" column or a footnote pointing at the command.

## Dependencies

Cannot fully ship until enough providers × runtimes have landed to have a non-trivial test matrix — best done AFTER Johnny-1ge.1/.2/.3, but the new assertion fields + the `johnny-tts-smoke` skeleton can land earlier and fill in as each provider arrives.

title: run.sh :5173 orphan-sweep kills Docker Desktop's com.docker.backend (port proxy), taking the daemon down
description: run.sh sweeps any host process listening on :5173 before starting the dockerized frontend, assuming it's a stray host vite. But when the frontend container is ALREADY up, Docker Desktop's com.docker.backend proxies the container's published 5173 and shows as the listener. The sweep kills com.docker.backend → Docker Desktop daemon dies → socket /Users/nikita/.docker/run/docker.sock disappears → all subsequent docker commands fail and any in-flight build aborts. Repro: with the stack already running, run ./run.sh (or ./run-dev.sh). Fix: the sweep must skip Docker Desktop's own helpers (com.docker.backend / com.docker.*) and/or only kill a PID whose binary is a node/vite process, not Docker's port proxy. Encountered during Johnny-8zv work; had to relaunch Docker Desktop with 'open -a Docker'.
close_reason: Fixed: run.sh/stop.sh :5173 sweep switched from the com.docker.* denylist (defeated by macOS ps -o comm= returning the full /Applications/Docker.app/.../com.docker.backend path) to an allowlist that only kills node/vite/pnpm/npm/esbuild. Verified live: ./run.sh, ./run-dev.sh, and a full ./stop.sh && ./run.sh all ran with com.docker.backend on :5173 and Docker Desktop stayed up. Committed a10d81aa.

title: noVNC sign-in: email scrape fails for Workspace accounts → bot saved as 'unknown-<hex>@johnny.local' instead of real email
description:
## Context / Why
User repro (2026-06-07): added a new meeting bot via noVNC sign-in, completed Google sign-in with `nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi` (a Google Workspace account on a custom domain), saw the noVNC "success / you can close this window" screen, returned to /settings expecting to see the real email — instead the row was saved as `unknown-51078bb5@johnny.local`.

This is the placeholder generated by `placeholder_email(signin_id)` in `backend/app/services/bot_signin.py:353`. It's emitted when the supervisor's email scrape fails AND no `email_hint` was supplied. The user can rename it inline in the settings row, but the scrape SHOULD have worked — this case (a normal interactive sign-in to a real Google account) is the happy path, not the fallback path.

## Current behavior (the bug)
- noVNC supervisor lives in `backend/johnny/bot_signin/supervisor.py`.
- After `wait_for_signin(page)` resolves, the supervisor calls `_scrape_email(page)` (line 111).
- `_scrape_email`:
    - Navigates to `EMAIL_SCRAPE_URL = "https://myaccount.google.com/"` (line 54).
    - Tries TWO selectors in order: `[data-email]` and `[data-initial-email]` (lines 59-62).
    - Reads the email from the matching attribute via `get_attribute(...)`.
    - Returns `None` on any failure path (timeout / no element / no value).
- The marker is then written with `"email": scraped_email or email_hint` (line 207). If both are None, the API fallback at `backend/app/api/bot_signin.py:205` calls `placeholder_email(signin.id)` → `unknown-<short>@johnny.local`.

Likely root causes for the scrape failure in the user's case (Workspace `@aikamatkat.fi`):
- Both `[data-email]` and `[data-initial-email]` are STALE selectors. Google has migrated `myaccount.google.com` to a render-blocking app shell that no longer ships these data attributes in the static HTML.
- Workspace accounts may render a different account-chooser UI (org branding / domain-managed warning) that delays the email element.
- 4s per-selector timeout (line 129) may be too short if the page hasn't hydrated.
- The supervisor only tries `myaccount.google.com`. If anti-bot / interstitial / Workspace consent screens redirect away, scrape gives up.

## Expected behavior
After a successful interactive sign-in to ANY Google account (personal `@gmail.com`, Workspace custom-domain, or `@googlemail.com` legacy), the saved row's email column reflects the real signed-in identity. The placeholder is reserved for genuinely unscrapable edge cases (network failed, anti-bot triggered, etc.) — not for normal Workspace sign-ins.

## Repro steps (deterministic)
1. `./run-dev.sh`, open /settings.
2. Click "Add bot" → noVNC sign-in flow opens.
3. (Do NOT type an email hint in Johnny's modal — leave it blank.)
4. In the embedded Chromium, sign in with a Google Workspace account (custom domain, e.g. `<you>@<your-workspace>.<tld>`).
5. Wait for the supervisor's "you can close this window" screen → close.
6. Observe: /settings shows the new row with email `unknown-<8hex>@johnny.local` instead of the real Workspace email.

(For comparison, a `@gmail.com` sign-in MIGHT still work depending on whether Google currently ships the legacy data attributes on myaccount for that account class. Reproduce both ways and document.)

## Scope (in)
- Rewrite `_scrape_email` to be robust to current Google DOM and to Workspace accounts. At minimum:
    - Expand `EMAIL_SCRAPE_SELECTORS` to include current Google selectors (e.g. `a[aria-label*="@"]`, `[data-identifier]`, `[aria-label*="Google Account"]`, account-chip in the top-right that holds the email in `aria-label` or tooltip). Implementer must `web search` for the current set and try ≥4 selectors.
    - Add a text-content fallback: regex-match any element on the page whose innerText looks like an email and whose ancestor matches an account-chooser/info container.
    - Add a second scrape source: if `myaccount.google.com` doesn't yield an email, also try `https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/feed/atom` (returns XML with the user's email in `<title>` when signed in) or `https://accounts.google.com/ListAccounts?gpsia=1&source=ogb&json=standard` (Google's account-list JSON endpoint; structure changes over time, validate from the web).
    - Use `page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")` (with a sane upper bound) before reading selectors so we're not racing hydration.
    - Bump per-selector timeout from 4s to ~8s; cap total scrape time at ~20s.
- When ALL strategies fail, write the page's URL + a short snippet of the visible HTML (first 500 chars of `body.innerText`) into the marker for diagnosis (NOT user-visible — debug field in the marker payload, surfaced in logs and the existing supervisor log).
- Validate the scraped value is an actual email (`re.fullmatch(r"[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+", value)`) before accepting it.
- Keep `placeholder_email` as the genuine fallback when the user genuinely couldn't be identified, but make the placeholder genuinely rare for normal sign-ins.
- Surface the scrape outcome in the supervisor log line: which selector matched, or "all selectors failed; page URL was X; body snippet was Y".

## Playground / sandbox parity (REQUIRED)
The bot identity feeds both Meet and /playground sessions. After this fix, both surfaces must show the real email in any account-selector UI and in transcripts (where applicable).

## Scope (out)
- Auto-renaming the placeholder retroactively for already-saved rows — the inline-rename flow handles that. Optional follow-up.
- The CLI helper (`johnny.tools.seed_auth_state`) already gets the email via the user typing it; not affected.
- Re-architecting the supervisor's overall flow (covered by Johnny-105).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] User's repro (Workspace account, blank email hint) now saves the row with the real `@aikamatkat.fi`-style email; placeholder no longer appears for this case
- [ ] Personal `@gmail.com` sign-in also resolves to the real email (regression check)
- [ ] If Google genuinely fails to expose the email (e.g. anti-bot blocked myaccount), the supervisor log includes the page URL + body snippet so the next failure is debuggable
- [ ] Scraped value is validated as a proper email before acceptance; garbage values are rejected and fall through to placeholder
- [ ] Existing placeholder-rename UI flow (BotSigninModal.svelte) still works for cases that genuinely fail
- [ ] Unit tests for `_scrape_email` cover: each selector branch hits, all selectors miss → returns None, malformed value → returns None, network-idle wait timeout doesn't crash
- [ ] Integration test: stub the page object with a fixture matching the CURRENT real Google DOM (capture a real one and check it in as a fixture under `backend/tests/fixtures/google/`), assert `_scrape_email` returns the email

## Validation
- Backend: `docker compose exec api pytest backend/tests/johnny/test_supervisor.py` + new test fixtures.
- Browser (chrome-devtools MCP), MANDATORY:
    - `./scripts/start-chrome.sh`; `./run-dev.sh`
    - Reproduce the user's exact flow with a Workspace account → assert /settings row shows the real email, not the placeholder → screenshot
    - Repeat with a `@gmail.com` account → assert real email → screenshot
    - Save under `.validation/Johnny-ckz-novnc-email-scrape/NN-*.png`

## Required process — non-negotiable
- **Maximum-effort mode.**
- **Mandatory web search** for:
    - Current Google DOM selectors that reliably expose the signed-in email on `myaccount.google.com` (these change every ~6 months — do NOT trust training-cutoff knowledge)
    - Whether the `mail.google.com/mail/u/0/feed/atom` trick still works in 2026 for both Workspace and personal accounts (and whether it requires Gmail to be enabled — Workspace orgs sometimes disable it)
    - Whether `accounts.google.com/ListAccounts` is still the right JSON endpoint and what its current shape is
    - Patterns from Playwright recipes / Selenium gist communities for reading the signed-in Google email
- Cite each chosen selector / endpoint + fetch date + source URL in the PR description.

## Anti-patterns — do not close prematurely
- ❌ "Added one more selector to the tuple — closing." → reject. Repro must flip; ≥2 selectors AND a non-DOM fallback (atom feed or API) must be implemented.
- ❌ "Tests pass with the old fixture (no real DOM captured)." → reject. Fixture must be derived from a current real Google response.
- ❌ "Personal Gmail works but Workspace still gets placeholder." → reject; both must work.
- ❌ "Selectors match but value isn't validated as an email." → reject.
- ✅ "User's exact repro now resolves to the real email; gmail repro also passes; debug fields populated on failure path; tests cover all branches; screenshots attached." → accept.

title: Bot 'Verify session' button always returns connected — file-shape-only check, never round-trips to Google
description:
## Context / Why
The "Verify session" button on /settings (per bot account) gives false positives. User repro: added a completely fake bot, clicked "Verify session", got "connected". This is actively misleading — users trust the button, then their bot fails to join a Meet, and there's no signal until then.

## Current behavior (the bug)
- Frontend: `frontend/src/routes/settings/+page.svelte:638-645` — "Verify session" button calls `verifyAccount()` from `frontend/src/lib/accounts.ts:137`, which hits `GET /auth/google/accounts/{account_id}/verify`.
- Backend: `backend/app/api/auth.py:587 _verify_bot_session(...)`. The function's OWN docstring confesses (paraphrased): "File-level only — we never round-trip to Google with the cookies. What we verify: the file is present, well-formed JSON, has a non-empty cookies array, and the soonest persistent-cookie expiry."
- Net result: any JSON file with the right shape (valid `cookies: [{...}]` array with future expiries) passes, including:
    - cookies for the wrong Google account
    - cookies signed out / revoked / for a deleted account
    - hand-crafted cookies with the right shape but no real session
  Compare with the CALENDAR verify path in the same file (~line 580) which DOES round-trip to Google's `/userinfo` and reports the real status. The bot verify path is the outlier.

## Expected behavior
"Verify session" must report `ok=True` only when the bot's `storage_state.json` actually corresponds to a live, signed-in Google account that the bot can use to join a Meet. False positives must disappear — a fake / stale / wrong-account storage_state must be flagged.

## Repro steps (deterministic)
1. `./run-dev.sh`, open /settings.
2. Add a new Google account (any email).
3. Upload a hand-crafted `storage_state.json` containing one cookie `{ "name": "fake", "value": "fake", "domain": ".google.com", "path": "/", "expires": 9999999999, "httpOnly": true, "secure": true, "sameSite": "Lax" }`.
4. Click "Verify session".
5. Observe: UI reports ok / connected. Network tab shows `GET /auth/google/accounts/<id>/verify` returns `{"bot_session": {"ok": true, ...}}`.
6. Try to start a Meet session with that bot → bot fails to join (because the cookies are fake). The verify button never warned.

## Scope (in)
- Replace the file-shape-only check in `_verify_bot_session` with a real authentication check against Google. Pick ONE of the two options below during implementation — implementer documents the choice in PR:
    A. **Playwright probe** — spin a short-lived Playwright context loading the storage_state, navigate to a known signed-in URL (e.g. `https://accounts.google.com/SignOutOptions` or `https://meet.google.com/landing`), read the rendered identity (logged-in email / DOM marker), assert it matches the account's expected email. This mirrors how the meet-worker uses the cookies so the check is faithful.
    B. **Direct HTTPS probe** — hit a Google endpoint that accepts cookie auth (e.g. `https://accounts.google.com/SignOutOptions` or `https://myaccount.google.com/?pli=1`) with the cookies attached, follow redirects, and detect the signed-in landing vs the sign-in-page redirect. Cheaper than Playwright but riskier: Google may serve different content to bare HTTP clients, and anti-bot checks may produce flakes.
- Implementer's recommendation: **option A** unless the latency cost (cold-start Playwright) is unacceptable; in that case implement A but keep a pooled / pre-warmed Playwright context.
- Preserve the existing cookie-expiry warning (soonest persistent expiry) as additional info in the CapabilityCheck payload — useful even when the round-trip passes.
- Update `CapabilityCheck.message` text to be specific about what failed (e.g. "Cookies present, but Google returned the sign-in page — the session is no longer valid", or "Signed in as <email>, which does NOT match this account's expected email <other_email>").
- Update the docstring of `_verify_bot_session` so it no longer claims to be file-level only.
- Keep the existing fast-fail cases (file missing / bad JSON / bad shape / cookies expired) BEFORE the network probe, so the common failures don't pay the latency cost.

## Scope (out)
- Calendar verify path — already round-trips, don't touch.
- Auto-refresh on background timer (separate concern).
- Re-architecting the bot-auth flow (covered by Johnny-pia / Johnny-105 / Johnny-ckz.23).

## Playground / sandbox parity (REQUIRED)
The bot identity is the same regardless of session source. Verify must report the same answer for the same account whether the next session is launched from /calendar (Meet) or /playground.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The repro above no longer reports ok=true. With a hand-crafted fake storage_state, the response is `ok=false` with a message stating the session isn't actually signed in.
- [ ] With a real, currently-signed-in `storage_state.json`, the response is `ok=true` and the message reports the signed-in email.
- [ ] If the storage_state corresponds to a DIFFERENT Google account than the one this row claims, the response is `ok=false` with a clear mismatch message including both emails.
- [ ] Soonest-cookie-expiry warning still appears in the detail payload (regression check vs current behaviour).
- [ ] Fast-fail cases (no file / bad JSON / empty cookies) return quickly without paying the network/Playwright cost.
- [ ] No regression in the CALENDAR verify path.
- [ ] Backend test fixtures cover: valid live cookies (mocked at HTTP layer if option B, or with a fake-but-routed Google response if option A), fake-but-well-shaped cookies, expired cookies, mismatched-account cookies, missing file.

## Validation
- Backend: `docker compose exec api pytest backend/tests/api/test_auth.py` + new tests covering the fake / live / mismatched paths.
- Browser (chrome-devtools MCP), MANDATORY:
    - `./scripts/start-chrome.sh`; `./run-dev.sh`
    - Run the repro above (steps 1–5) → assert "Verify session" returns a clear NOT-connected status → screenshot
    - Upload a real, signed-in `storage_state.json` from `johnny.tools.seed_auth_state` → click Verify → assert connected, with the signed-in email reflected in the message → screenshot
    - If feasible, mismatched-account: upload account A's cookies on account B's row → click Verify → assert NOT connected with the mismatch message → screenshot
    - Save under `.validation/Johnny-ckz-verify-bot-session/NN-*.png`

## Required process — non-negotiable
- **Maximum-effort mode.**
- **Mandatory web search** for:
    - How others probe Google session validity from a cookie jar (Playwright `storage_state` reuse patterns, Selenium + Google anti-bot patterns, official Playwright recipes for sign-in verification).
    - Google's behaviour for cookie-auth + redirect to sign-in (the classic indicator of an invalid session).
    - Whether `accounts.google.com/SignOutOptions` is the currently-recommended probe URL — Google has changed the endpoint multiple times historically.
- Cite probe URL + decision (option A vs B) + fetch date in PR.

## Anti-patterns — do not close prematurely
- ❌ "Tightened the file-shape validator — closing." → reject. Tighter shape validation does not catch fake cookies; the user's repro must still flip from ok=true to ok=false.
- ❌ "Added a TODO and a log line." → reject.
- ❌ "Network probe added but only mocked — never hit real Google." → reject; at least one integration test must hit a real Google probe URL (skip cleanly if no network).
- ❌ "Works in Meet path but not playground." → reject.
- ✅ "Verify now round-trips to Google; the user's repro flips to ok=false; real-cookie path stays ok=true; mismatch case caught; screenshots attached; full test suite green." → accept.

title: Structural consistency: every page shares one header + menu + wrapper + container — enforce shared layout primitives across the app (REQUIRES PLAN MODE)
description:
User frame:

> *"After the final review I understand that the LLM cannot understand what's good or what's wrong. So can we structurize all our pages and ensure that we have a normal header with normal menu, with normal wrapper, with normal container and everything like that. Because right now the pages are still different as shit."*

## Action

Enforce one shared structural shell across every page: same header, same menu, same wrapper, same container. No page may render its own bespoke layout.

## Plan mode is required

`EnterPlanMode` first. Plan the shared layout primitives, the migration of every page to them, and the deletion of per-page bespoke shells, then implement.
notes: Clarification (2026-06-07): the 'header' is mobile-only. On desktop, keep the persistent left sidebar (240px per DESIGN.md). On mobile (<768px), sidebar collapses to a drawer triggered by a top-left icon button. Desktop has NO top bar — page title lives in the content area per DESIGN.md.
close_reason: Shared <Page>/<PageHeader> primitives ship; every page migrated; chrome-devtools MCP-validated on desktop + mobile across 9 routes; structural consistency enforced per DESIGN.md

title: Final pass: every page looks ugly — audit all surfaces, fix design, validate via chrome-devtools MCP screenshots
description:

- General "looks ugly" — surfaces don't read as the calm, dense, signal-yellow operator console DESIGN.md describes.

## Validation

title: STT provider catalog UI with per-provider Test button (mic record + transcribe + latency/cost)
description:
## Why
Right now there is no UI to browse, configure, or sample STT providers — users can't tell which one works best for their setup. Mirror the existing Piper voice-catalog UX shipped in Johnny-ckz.5.

## Scope
- New settings route (e.g. `/settings/stt`) listing every installed STT provider with: name, type (local/cloud), streaming-capable flag, model list (where applicable), API-key field (cloud), language picker.
- Per-provider/per-model **Test** button: records 5 seconds from user mic, posts to backend, displays transcript + latency (ms) + estimated cost (cloud providers report it; local providers show $0).
- Provider + model selection persists to user prefs; reloads on next visit.
- Initial release lists existing providers (`faster_whisper`, `deepgram`, `elevenlabs`, `openai_realtime`). New providers from Johnny-stt.1 and Johnny-stt.4 plug in as they ship.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/settings/stt` route lists all installed STT providers with their model count.
- [ ] Selecting a provider reveals its config form (key, model, language).
- [ ] Test button records mic for ~5s, posts to backend, displays transcript within 10s.
- [ ] Latency (ms) and provider-reported cost rendered next to the transcript.
- [ ] Selection is saved and re-loads on next visit.
- [ ] Empty / failing provider shows a usable error toast — not a stack trace.

## Validation
- Backend: integration test for the `/stt/test` endpoint with a mocked provider.
- Frontend: component test for the Test button state machine (idle → recording → uploading → done).
- **Browser (chrome-devtools MCP):** navigate /settings/stt → snapshot → select faster_whisper (or Parakeet once shipped) → grant mic → click Test → wait for `[data-stt-result]` → assert non-empty transcript → screenshot for PR.

title: STT provider catalog: VoiceInk parity + NVIDIA Parakeet + streaming-in-chat
description:
## Why this epic

First-class speech-to-text provider catalog for Johnny with the same breadth as VoiceInk (`/Users/nikita/Projects/VoiceInk`), plus NVIDIA Parakeet (`nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3`) as a fast local + streaming-capable option that VoiceInk doesn't ship.

## What ships under this epic

1. **Parakeet provider** (Johnny-stt.1) — `nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3`. Local, fast, streaming-capable. The priority piece.
2. **Catalog UI with Test button** (Johnny-stt.2) — model browser per provider, per-model Test button, latency + cost shown. Mirrors the existing Piper voice catalog UX (`Johnny-ckz.5`).
3. **Live streaming transcription in playground chat** (Johnny-stt.3) — mic icon + live partial transcripts as user speaks. Default: Parakeet local; fallback cloud streaming providers.
4. **VoiceInk parity bundle** (Johnny-stt.4) — Gemini, AssemblyAI, Groq, FluidAudio (P4 backlog). Whisper / Deepgram / ElevenLabs / OpenAI Realtime already exist in `backend/app/providers/`.

## Reference

- VoiceInk providers: `/Users/nikita/Projects/VoiceInk/VoiceInk/Transcription/{Cloud,Streaming,Whisper,FluidAudio}/`

title: Barge-in classifier LLM ReadTimeouts against Ollama Qwen 35B — every timeout is a missed interrupt + log noise
description:
## Why this exists

Validation under [[validate-in-browser-live-chat-live-talking-johnny-ckz-6-end-to-end-via-chrome-devtools-mcp-pure-verification-file-follow-up-bugs-for-any-gap]] (Johnny-ckz.10) found repeated `httpx.ReadTimeout` errors from the **barge-in classifier** during a normal playground session:

```
barge-in classifier failed for session=224 — leaving current response running
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File "/workspace/johnny/voice_pipeline/pipeline.py", line 819, in _maybe_barge_in
    decision = await self._classify_barge_in_intent(transcript)
  File "/workspace/johnny/voice_pipeline/pipeline.py", line 854, in _classify_barge_in_intent
    response = await self.router_llm.chat(...)
  File "/workspace/app/providers/openai_compatible_llm.py", line 274, in chat
    response = await self._client.post(url, json=body, headers=headers)
  ...
httpx.ReadTimeout
```

5+ occurrences over a single ~3-minute session. The configured LLM is "Ollama Qwen No Reason Uncensored" (fredrezones55/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Aggressive:latest, a 35B-parameter Q4_K_M model). On this hardware that model can easily take longer than the default `httpx` read timeout per turn.

When the barge-in classifier ReadTimeouts, the pipeline logs the error and **suppresses the barge-in decision** ("leaving current response running"). This is the right safe fallback when the bot IS actually speaking — but it doesn't fix the underlying latency problem and would still mask real barge-in attempts under [[run-the-two-bot-voice-interrupt-harness-end-to-end-against-real-models-fix-any-bugs-it-surfaces]] (Johnny-ckz.4)'s 500 ms p95 budget.

## Symptoms

1. Real user barge-in (saying "stop") will be missed when the classifier times out — every classifier ReadTimeout is a missed interrupt opportunity.
2. Worker logs are flooded with stacktraces, hiding other issues.
3. May contribute to the broader "bot never replies" symptom in [[playground-audio-path-never-opens-websocket-no-voice-no-bot-replies-johnny-ckz-6-regression]] if the same LLM is used for the conversation reply path.

## Fix shape (do not over-fit)

- The barge-in classifier is meant to be a low-latency router — it should NOT be using the main 35B reply model. Route it to a cheap small model (Llama 3.2 3B / Qwen 2.5 3B / a small distilled classifier) regardless of the user's "active" LLM choice.
- Or: keep the same model but use logit-bias/few-tokens-only sampling with a very short max-tokens to bound classifier latency.
- Independent of the model choice, set an explicit `httpx` timeout for the classifier call that's tighter than today's default — and if it times out, log at WARN (single line) instead of dumping a full traceback every time.

## Acceptance

1. Under load (mic active, free auto-speak mode), no `httpx.ReadTimeout` from the barge-in classifier appears in worker logs over a 5-minute playground session.
2. Worker log noise drops to a single WARN line on classifier-timeout, not a 30-line traceback.
3. Real "stop" barge-in test (drive via chrome-devtools MCP per Johnny-ckz.10 acceptance #4) is recognized and stops the bot within Johnny-ckz.4's p95 budget.

## Source

`johnny/voice_pipeline/pipeline.py:819` (`_maybe_barge_in`) and `_classify_barge_in_intent` at line 854.

title: Playground transcripts label every speaker=null row as 'You' — including STT hallucinations and any non-user rows
description:
## Why this exists

Validation under [[validate-in-browser-live-chat-live-talking-johnny-ckz-6-end-to-end-via-chrome-devtools-mcp-pure-verification-file-follow-up-bugs-for-any-gap]] (Johnny-ckz.10) found that the `/playground` page renders **every** `transcripts` row with `speaker = NULL` as "You", while the `/sessions/{id}` session-detail page correctly renders the same rows as "Speaker".

Concretely, for session 224 the `/playground` UI showed:
```
You — Hello can you hear me?
You — Does Olam A.P.I.
You — amwch ran i'n clo canwys.
You — . . . . . .
You — . . . .
```
…but on `/sessions/224` the same rows render as:
```
user      — Hello can you hear me?
Speaker   — Does Olam A.P.I.
Speaker   — amwch ran i'n clo canwys.
Speaker   — . . . . . .
Speaker   — . . . .
```

Only the first one ("Hello…") has `speaker = "user"` in the DB; the rest have `speaker = NULL` (mostly STT hallucinations and any future bot-side rows that don't carry a `speaker`). Labeling them all as "You" makes the playground conversation nonsensical.

## Fix shape

- Mirror the session-detail UI's labelling logic on the playground:
  - `speaker == "user"` → "You"
  - `speaker == NULL` and not "user" → "Speaker" (or "Bot" if we can disambiguate downstream)
- Consider rejecting any new transcript rows with `speaker = NULL` once the STT silence-hallucination bug is fixed; until then, at minimum do not label them as "You".

## Acceptance

1. On `/playground`, only `speaker = "user"` transcript rows render as "You".
2. All other speakers (`NULL`, `bot`, anything else) render with their correct label, matching `/sessions/{id}`.
3. Verified via chrome-devtools MCP `take_snapshot` showing the conversation feed after the linked STT bug fix.

## Source location

`frontend/src/routes/playground/+page.svelte` — the transcript rendering block defaulting `speaker` to "You".

title: STT hallucinations from silence: faster-whisper produces 'Does Olam A.P.I.', '. . . .', etc. on quiet mic and persists them as transcripts
description:
## Why this exists

Validation under [[validate-in-browser-live-chat-live-talking-johnny-ckz-6-end-to-end-via-chrome-devtools-mcp-pure-verification-file-follow-up-bugs-for-any-gap]] (Johnny-ckz.10) saw the playground accumulate STT garbage transcripts whenever there was no real speech:

- `Does Olam A.P.I.`
- `amwch ran i'n clo canwys.` (Welsh-shaped nonsense)
- `. . . . . .`
- `. . . .`

These are classic faster-whisper hallucinations on silence / low-energy audio frames. They are saved into `transcripts` with `speaker = NULL`, which both (a) pollutes the conversation feed and (b) feeds the decision LLM noise that it then has to suppress (the one decision row produced for session 226 was `should_speak=false` on `. . . .`).

## Reproduction (chrome-devtools MCP trace)

1. `new_page` against `/playground`, click Start (mic gets activated).
2. Type **nothing** — leave the browser tab in a quiet room for ~60 s.
3. `curl /sessions/{id}` shows new rows in `transcripts` every few seconds with `speaker=null` and silence-derived text.
4. On `/playground` these all render as "You" — actively misleading (see linked bug for the labelling half).
5. On `/sessions/{id}` they correctly render as "Speaker" but they still pollute the transcript and waste the decision LLM's tokens.

## Fix shape (do not over-fit)

- Apply a voice activity detection / energy gate before pushing a frame batch through faster-whisper, so pure silence never reaches the model.
- And/or post-filter: faster-whisper has a known set of hallucination phrases ("Thanks for watching", "Subtitles by the Amara.org community", `"...". "..."` patterns, the silence-dot pattern `". . . ."`). Drop transcripts whose text matches the hallucination filter, and/or whose `avg_logprob` / `no_speech_prob` indicates low confidence.
- Use the `condition_on_previous_text=False` and/or `no_speech_threshold` tuning that faster-whisper exposes.
- Whatever the gate is, it should also keep the silence rows out of the `bot_sessions.transcripts` table — even if they slip past the model, do not persist `.....`-shaped rows.

## Acceptance

1. Quiet room, mic on, 60 s of silence → **zero** new transcript rows for the session.
2. Real speech still produces transcripts (verified by typing into the text input or by speaking near the host mic).
3. Decision LLM no longer makes "should_speak=false because the transcript is empty/dots" decisions — the noise never reaches it.
4. Verified via chrome-devtools MCP (start session, wait silently for 60 s, screenshot the empty transcript).

## Evidence artifacts

- DB rows from session 224 and 226 (`/sessions/{id}` REST) showing the dot/Welsh/`Does Olam A.P.I.` transcripts.
- Screenshot `.validation-ckz10-artifacts/04-session-detail-page.png` (12 such rows on session 224).
- Same artifact for session 226 (2 dot rows).

title: Validate in-browser live chat / live talking (Johnny-ckz.6) end-to-end via chrome-devtools MCP — pure verification, file follow-up bugs for any gap
description:
## Why this exists

Johnny-ckz.6 (in-browser voice/text chat with the bot — per-event 'Try with bot' button + standalone playground) was implemented by an agent that **ignored the AGENTS.md top rule** requiring chrome-devtools MCP validation. The feature was marked done without anyone driving it in a real browser. The first visible symptom of that skipped step is already on file as the P0 schema drift in [[bot-sessions-schema-drift-orm-expects-source-and-playground-overrides-columns-that-don-t-exist-worker-monitor-plus-sessions-active-both-500]] (Johnny-ckz.9) — but that is almost certainly not the only thing the implementation skipped past.

This task exists to restore the validation that should have been done in-line, and to surface every other gap so each gap becomes its own follow-up bug. **No implementation work happens here.** Validation-only. If something doesn't work, file a new bug under Johnny-ckz and move on.

## Blocked by

[[bot-sessions-schema-drift-orm-expects-source-and-playground-overrides-columns-that-don-t-exist-worker-monitor-plus-sessions-active-both-500]] (Johnny-ckz.9) — until the schema drift is fixed, /sessions/active returns 500 and validation cannot proceed.

## What to validate (one-to-one with Johnny-ckz.6 acceptance)

Each item below must be exercised in a real browser via chrome-devtools MCP tools (loaded via ToolSearch first). For each, capture the noted artifacts.

### 1. Per-event 'Try with bot' button — opens session in <3s with audible greeting

- mcp__chrome-devtools__new_page against the calendar event detail page.
- mcp__chrome-devtools__take_snapshot — confirm 'Try with bot' button exists and is reachable.
- mcp__chrome-devtools__click the button. Start a wall-clock timer.
- mcp__chrome-devtools__wait_for the session UI to mount. Stop the timer. Must be < 3 s.
- mcp__chrome-devtools__evaluate_script on an audio element to confirm playback started (e.g. audio.currentTime > 0 within a few seconds of session start).
- mcp__chrome-devtools__take_screenshot of the active session.

### 2. Standalone /playground — persona pick, session-scoped overrides, voice + text

- Navigate to /playground.
- take_snapshot and assert the persona picker, override controls, and Start button exist.
- Pick a persona, override the active TTS provider (e.g. Local Piper if not currently active), click Start.
- Drive a voice turn (or text-fallback turn).
- After ending the session, navigate to the providers page and evaluate_script to confirm the **global** active TTS is unchanged.

### 3. Real bot_sessions rows with transcripts and utterances

- After exercising 1 + 2, hit /sessions/<id> for the just-created sessions in chrome-devtools MCP.
- take_snapshot and assert the transcript + utterance panels are populated.

### 4. Interrupts work within Johnny-ckz.4's latency budget

- Drive a user turn that triggers a long bot reply.
- Mid-reply, drive an interrupt ('stop'). Use the Speaker harness from [[run-the-two-bot-voice-interrupt-harness-end-to-end-against-real-models-fix-any-bugs-it-surfaces]] (Johnny-ckz.4) if it is available; otherwise type or play 'stop' manually with timestamps captured.
- evaluate_script on the audio element to confirm playback stopped.
- list_network_requests to capture the timing of the cut.
- Assert the interrupt latency is within the Johnny-ckz.4 budget (500 ms p95).

### 5. Playground sessions are visually distinct in the session list

- Navigate to the session list page.
- take_snapshot and assert there is a visible badge / tag separating playground sessions from real-meeting sessions.
- Screenshot.

### 6. Mic-denied falls back to text-only with no JS errors

- mcp__chrome-devtools__emulate or otherwise simulate a denied microphone permission (or use the browser's permissions UI directly).
- Start a playground session.
- take_snapshot — assert the UI offers a text input and a visible explanation.
- list_console_messages — confirm zero JS errors.
- Complete one text-turn round-trip end-to-end.

### 7. End-session tears down audio cleanly

- After a live playground session, click End.
- evaluate_script: assert no live RTCPeerConnection instances and that navigator.mediaDevices shows the mic is released.
- list_network_requests: confirm no lingering WebSocket / SSE.
- From the host shell, run docker ps --filter name=meet-worker-session and confirm **no** meet-worker container was spawned for this session at any point.

### 8. No meet-worker container for either surface

- During the live runs above, periodically run docker ps on the host and confirm no meet-worker container appears tied to these sessions.

## What to do when something fails

- File a new bug issue under epic Johnny-ckz with: which acceptance bullet failed, the chrome-devtools MCP command sequence that reproduced it, console + network artifacts, and a screenshot.
- Set the new bug's priority based on user-visible impact (P0 if blocking core flow, P1 otherwise).
- **Do not fix anything in this task.** Filing the bug is the whole deliverable per failure.

## Acceptance

1. Every numbered check above is executed via chrome-devtools MCP and the noted artifacts are captured (snapshots, screenshots, console / network captures, timing numbers).
2. A trace log of the validation run — command sequence + per-check verdict (pass / fail / blocked) — is recorded in this issue's notes when validation finishes.
3. Every failure has a corresponding follow-up bug filed under Johnny-ckz, with chrome-devtools MCP-captured evidence.
4. If every check passes, Johnny-ckz.6 is signed off as truly done and this task is closed clean.
5. No code in the application was modified as part of this task — verification only.

## Why this is a separate task and not a re-open of Johnny-ckz.6

The verification needs its own line-item with its own acceptance so it can be audited. It also has to be re-runnable: when Johnny-ckz.6's follow-up bugs land fixes, this validation is the gate they pass through.

## Process note

Going forward, any task that touches a UI must include browser validation IN-LINE during the implementation per the AGENTS.md top rule — not as a separate ticket. This task exists to clean up after a rule that was skipped, not to normalize the pattern of validating later.
