title: Kokoro + KittenTTS in-container runtime: adopt the Parakeet runtime-install pattern (No module named 'kokoro'/'kittentts')
description:
Split out of Johnny-1ge.10 (cells B + D). The other six TTS matrix cells were fixed and browser-validated there; the two **in-container** cells remain because the optional libraries are genuinely not in the api image.

## Symptom
- Kokoro `in-container` runtime → preview returns 502 `synthesis failed: kokoro library not importable for the in-container runtime: No module named 'kokoro'`.
- KittenTTS `in-container` runtime → 502 `No module named 'kittentts'`.

The api image is built `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --extra local-stt --extra local-tts` (backend/Dockerfile) — neither `kokoro` (torch-heavy) nor `kittentts` (GitHub wheel) is included, by design.

## Decision: adopt the Parakeet runtime-install precedent (NOT image baking)
Parakeet STT already solved this exact shape: an "Install package" button that `uv pip install --target`s into a host bind-mounted dir which the api prepends to sys.path on startup. Mirror it for both providers so the operator learns ONE flow.

Reference implementation to copy:
- `backend/app/services/parakeet_packages.py` — the service (get_packages_dir / register_sys_path / is_installed / package_status / install_packages_stream). DEFAULT_PACKAGES_DIR=/var/lib/johnny/parakeet-packages, env JOHNNY_PARAKEET_PACKAGES_DIR.
- `backend/app/main.py` ~lines 87-96 — calls register_sys_path() at startup.
- `backend/app/api/providers.py` ~lines 2126-2181 — GET `/providers/{id}/package` + POST `/providers/{id}/package/install` (currently hardcoded `if row.provider_name != 'parakeet'`).
- `docker-compose.yml` ~lines 44-53 (env) + ~138-143 (bind mount `${HOME}/.johnny/parakeet-packages:/var/lib/johnny/parakeet-packages`).
- frontend "Install package" UI: `onInstallParakeet` in `frontend/src/routes/providers/+page.svelte` (~line 923) + provider-card wiring.

## Work
1. NEW `backend/app/services/kokoro_packages.py` + `kitten_packages.py` mirroring parakeet_packages.py. Pip specs: kokoro pulls `misaki[en]` + torch (CPU in arm64 Linux container — slow but functional); kittentts is the GitHub-releases wheel (see kitten_tts.py:778). Pin versions to avoid resolver drift (parakeet pins tokenizers/hf-hub for the same reason).
2. Generalise the two providers.py package endpoints to dispatch on parakeet|kokoro|kittentts (consider a small registry instead of three if/elifs).
3. main.py: register_sys_path() for the two new dirs at startup.
4. docker-compose.yml: two new env vars + two bind mounts; also propagate to meet-worker (JOHNNY_MEET_WORKER_*_PACKAGES_VOLUME, see docker-compose.yml:52 + docker_launcher).
5. kokoro_tts.py:_load_pipeline (~943) + kitten_tts.py:_load_model (~773): after the failing import, attempt register_sys_path()+retry, and on miss point the error at the new "Install package" button (lead with it; keep "switch to a sidecar" as the fast alternative).
6. Frontend: surface the Install button on the Kokoro + KittenTTS provider cards (reuse the Parakeet streaming-progress component).

## Validation (chrome-devtools MCP, mandatory)
- Add Kokoro provider → in-container runtime → click Install → watch stream → after install, Preview af_heart → assert X-TTS-Audible=1 + X-TTS-Peak>0.01.
- Same for KittenTTS in-container (voice Bella).
- Screenshot both into `.validation/<task-id>/`.

## Note
On Apple Silicon the recommended fast paths already work post-Johnny-1ge.10: Kokoro→MLX sidecar (fixed), KittenTTS→http-sidecar. In-container is the portable CPU fallback, so this is P2, not P1.
close_reason: Superseded by Johnny-1ge.11. .8hq proposed the Parakeet-style runtime-install pattern for Kokoro + KittenTTS in-container; .11 shipped the Dockerfile-bake alternative instead (added a 'neural-tts' optional extra with kokoro + kittentts wheel + misaki[en] + en_core_web_sm, torch pinned to CPU index, persistent bind-mounts for ~/.johnny/{kokoro,kitten}-models). Both in-container cells (.10 cells B + D) now resolve at the source-of-truth layer and survive ./stop.sh && ./run.sh. No outstanding work in this ticket — closing as resolved-by-alternative rather than re-opening to argue install strategy after the fact.

title: Personality character: keep it ONE freeform textarea (the existing description field), inject verbatim into the LLM system prompt at session start
description:
## Why this exists

Operator decision after reviewing this task in its earlier form: keep **one** freeform textarea on each personality, do not split into structured columns (`character` / `communication_style` / `allowed` / `forbidden` / `examples`). It is the operator's text; they should be free to express the personality however they want — a paragraph, a bullet list, a mix, a YAML-ish blob, anything readable — without the schema dictating shape. The earlier structured-field design was over-engineering.

What this task DOES deliver:

1. The single freeform `description` field on `personalities` (already in scope of Johnny-oly.2) is **THE** personality's character text. There is no second field, no JSONB inner schema, no "but the structured version is in this other column" twist.
2. That text is injected verbatim into the LLM system prompt at session start, in the place the current global Johnny prompt is interpolated today (the exact file:line is settled by Johnny-oly.1's PRD).
3. The editor textarea in Johnny-oly.4 is sized and copy-coached so an operator who wants structure can write structure (in plain text); an operator who wants a paragraph can write a paragraph; both work without UI changes.
4. Tests prove the text reaches the model — not that the model obeys it.

## What the editor textarea looks like

- **Textarea** — not a single-line input. The operator may write paragraphs, bullet lists, or several screenfuls of guidance; the field has to comfortably hold many pages of text.
- ~10 visible rows by default, auto-resizes upward as the operator types, max-height capped so the modal still scrolls.
- Vertical resize handle exposed so the operator can grow the editor manually if they prefer.
- Monospace-friendly font so lists and indented examples render predictably.
- Character counter (no hard limit, but show counts past 4 000 chars in a muted "long prompts cost more tokens" hint — informational, not a block).
- Placeholder copy that nudges without dictating — operator sees an example like:

  ```
  Example (you can write anything, in any shape):

  You are Sarah, a calm therapist with a CBT background.
  Style: short sentences, warm but precise. Ask one clarifying
  question before offering a perspective.
  Always: discuss communication patterns and emotional regulation
  in general terms.
  Never: give medical advice or make diagnostic claims; redirect
  to a licensed professional instead.
  ```

  Placeholder disappears on focus. No "Communication style:" / "Forbidden:" labels rendered as separate UI affordances — the labels in the example are just text the operator can keep, rewrite, or delete.

## What gets injected

A pure function `build_personality_system_prompt(personality) -> str` returns the personality's description verbatim with at most a one-line preamble identifying the personality by name. Deterministic, no LLM call, no side effects, no templating beyond:

```
[personality: <display_name>]
<description>
```

Or, if the operator prefers, a flag to skip the preamble — but defaults stay simple. The function composes upstream of any per-mode / per-template prompt fragments that already exist; personality is the IDENTITY layer, mode/template is the JOB layer.

## Tests

- Unit test on `build_personality_system_prompt`: empty description returns the preamble alone (or empty when the flag says skip); non-empty description appears verbatim; no trailing whitespace surprises that would change the prompt hash across saves.
- Backend integration: a session started under a personality whose description contains a distinctive sentinel string ("`xx-marker-12345-xx`") receives that string in the LLM system prompt. The integration test captures the LLM call and asserts the sentinel is in the system message.
- Browser via chrome-devtools MCP: create a personality through the UI with a sentinel in the textarea, assign it to a playground session, start the session, verify the captured system prompt contains the sentinel. Screenshot the editor's placeholder + filled state for the PR.

## Acceptance

- One field. No second column. No JSONB inner schema.
- Editor textarea renders with the placeholder example above; placeholder disappears on focus; counter shows past 4 000 chars.
- `build_personality_system_prompt(personality)` is a pure function with unit tests; default output is `[personality: <name>]\n<description>`.
- The injection site (decided in Johnny-oly.1's PRD) is the single place the personality text reaches the LLM; the previously-global Johnny prompt no longer leaks into the call.
- Integration test confirms the sentinel-in-description shows up in the captured LLM system message.
- Browser test confirms the editor → DB → session-start → LLM chain end-to-end.
- README "Personalities" section describes the single-field shape in one sentence ("the personality's description is freeform text injected as the LLM system prompt — write a paragraph, a bullet list, whatever helps the model act like the character").

## Non-goals

- Structured columns / JSONB inner schema for character (explicitly rolled back).
- AI-assisted persona builder.
- Personality-conditioned routing / decision logic — router stays personality-agnostic in v1; reasoning timeline at Johnny-ckz.28.4 surfaces "system prompt: <personality>" as a step but does not branch on it.
- Voice-cloning or voice-style transfer per personality.

## Cross-links

- Parent: **Johnny-oly**.
- **Johnny-oly.1** — PRD still settles WHERE in the existing prompt-assembly path the personality text is injected. No need for that PRD to design column-per-field anymore; one column, decided.
- **Johnny-oly.2** — Owns the `description` column on the personalities table. No schema growth for this task; .2 keeps its scope.
- **Johnny-oly.3** — Resolver calls `build_personality_system_prompt` at session start and passes the result through to the LLM call site.
- **Johnny-oly.4** — UI editor renders the textarea + placeholder. No new textareas to add beyond what .4 already plans.
- **Johnny-oly.7** — E2E matrix gains the sentinel-in-description assertion.
- **Johnny-etu.1** (Pipeline tech doc) — "where the system prompt lives" section gets the personality-prompt-assembly path once this ships.

## Dependencies

Blocked-on Johnny-oly.1 (PRD must settle the injection site) and Johnny-oly.2 (the `description` column it injects from). Lands in lockstep with Johnny-oly.3 (resolver invokes the assembly function).
