title: Frontend: personality picker on calendar events + playground + active-session badge + history bot-name rendering (replaces hardcoded 'Johnny' constant)
description:
## Why this exists

The management page from sub-task .4 builds the library; this sub-task wires it on the two surfaces that actually pick a personality at session start, surfaces the active personality on the running-session card, and stops the history page from rendering the hardcoded `'Johnny'` constant.

> **Surface audit.** Verified frontend routes: `calendar/`, `history/`, `playground/`, `providers/`, `sessions/`, `settings/`, `templates/`. There is no separate "chat" route — playground is the chat-style live surface, history is the read-only transcript view. The hardcoded `'Johnny'` label lives at `frontend/src/routes/history/[id]/+page.svelte:217` (transcript rows) and `:234` (page title); both must read from a per-session snapshot of the personality's display name instead.

## Scope

### A. Calendar event detail

Add a "Personality" dropdown next to the existing mode picker. Default = the personality marked `is_default`. Blank = "Use global default providers (no personality override)". Persisted on the calendar event row (new column — coordinate the migration with sub-task .oly.2 OR file a follow-on if the migration there does not already include this).

### B. Playground

Add the same dropdown above the prompt textarea. Same default + blank semantics. Persisted on the playground session row. Sticky in `localStorage` so the last-picked personality is pre-selected on the next page load.

### C. Session bot-name snapshot (drives history rendering)

At session start (calendar event → meet-worker, OR playground → browser pipeline runner), snapshot the resolved personality's `display_name` onto the session row as `bot_name`. The history page then reads `session.bot_name` and renders it where `frontend/src/routes/history/[id]/+page.svelte:217` currently hardcodes `'Johnny'`, and where line `:234` currently sets the page title. Sessions created before this lands keep showing "Johnny" because that is what the snapshot would have been.

This is the smallest version of the operator's request "we always have a hardcoded Johnny name" — the bot's name varies per session, history reflects it, and nothing else changes about that page.

### D. Active-session badge

On the running-session card (sessions list + per-session detail page), show "Character: <name>" right next to the existing meeting metadata. Click opens the personality detail in a read-only side panel — so the operator can verify quickly without leaving the session.

### E. Fallback warnings

When the resolver in sub-task .oly.3 falls back (personality references an unconfigured provider), the active-session card shows a one-line warning chip: "Personality '<name>' uses TTS '<provider>' but that provider is inactive — using global default '<other>' instead." Operator clicks to navigate to the personality editor.

### F. Tests

Required:
- Unit tests for the picker component covering the three default-vs-blank cases.
- Unit test for the history page: bot rows render `session.bot_name` when present, fall back to `'Johnny'` when null (legacy session).
- Browser tests folded into sub-task .7 (end-to-end matrix).

## Acceptance

- Personality dropdown appears on the calendar event detail and the playground; default + blank semantics work; per-surface persistence works.
- New session bot_name snapshot column populated at session start; history pages read it.
- History page no longer references the hardcoded `'Johnny'` constant on `:217` / `:234`; legacy sessions still display "Johnny" via the fallback.
- Active-session card shows the personality name and the fallback warning when applicable.
- `pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm lint` clean.
- Switching the personality on a calendar event AND starting that meeting picks up the right LLM + TTS (verified end-to-end by the matrix in sub-task .7).

## Dependencies

Blocked-on Johnny-oly.2 (need CRUD + the bot_name column on sessions, added in the same migration) + Johnny-oly.3 (resolver must honor the choice) + Johnny-oly.4 (need the library page to navigate to from the picker "Edit" link).

title: Frontend: /personalities management page — list / create / clone / edit / delete / set-default
description:
## Why this exists

The operator needs a dedicated page to build their personality library: create new characters, edit existing ones, clone an existing one as a starting point, set a default, delete what they no longer want. This sub-task ships that page.

## Scope

### A. Route + nav

New route `/personalities`. New sidebar nav entry between "Providers" and "Templates" (placement decided in .oly.1 PRD).

### B. List view

- Card or row per personality, default badge on the default one.
- Each entry: name, one-line truncated description, LLM provider/model summary, TTS provider/voice summary, optional mode badge.
- Quick actions per row: Edit / Clone / Set as default / Delete (delete disabled with tooltip on the default row).
- Top-of-page "New personality" button + an empty-state for first-run.

### C. Editor modal (used by Create / Edit / Clone)

- `display_name` — text input, validates unique.
- `description` — textarea, monospace-friendly, character counter, auto-resizes; placeholder copy gives an example ("Warm, supportive, never sarcastic. Asks clarifying questions before drafting code. Avoids hedging.").
- `llm_provider_id` — SELECT of configured + active LLM rows from `/providers`. "Use global default" is the blank option.
- `tts_provider_id` + voice picker — uses the unified component shipped by Johnny-1ge.8. Voice preview button included. Blank = "Use global default TTS".
- `default_mode` — SELECT with the existing bot modes + "Use meeting/playground default" blank option.
- Submit posts to the CRUD endpoints from sub-task .oly.2.

### D. Tests

Required:
- Unit tests for the editor modal validation (every field, every error path) in `frontend/src/routes/personalities/+page.test.ts`.
- Browser tests via chrome-devtools MCP folded into the matrix in sub-task .6 — this task focuses on unit + render coverage; the cross-page browser flow lives in .6.

## Acceptance

- Page renders, all listed actions work, deletion of default is refused with a clear UI message.
- Operator can create a "Friendly Customer Support" personality from scratch, clone Johnny, edit the clone, set the clone as default, then revert — all without a page reload.
- `pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm lint` clean.
- Page is keyboard-navigable (tab order, Enter / Escape on modal).
- Empty state on first load offers "Start from Johnny" as a one-click clone action.

## Dependencies

Blocked-on Johnny-oly.2 (CRUD endpoints) and Johnny-1ge.8 (unified voice picker component).
Companion to Johnny-oly.5 (picker).

title: Backend: personality-driven provider resolution at session start (LLM + TTS override with loud-fallback)
description:
## Why this exists

A personality is useless until the session loader actually honors it. This sub-task wires the resolver: at session start, the chosen personality overrides the global active LLM + TTS providers, and the resulting bundle is what the meet-worker + playground actually use. STT stays global.

## Scope

### A. Resolver

Refactor `backend/app/providers/loader.py:load_active_providers` (and any per-kind-loader helpers) to accept an optional `personality_id`. When set:

1. Look up the personality row.
2. For LLM: if `llm_provider_id` is set AND the referenced row is `is_active=true`, return that row instead of the global active LLM. Otherwise fall back to the global active LLM + log a structured `personality.fallback: kind=llm personality_id=N reason=<unconfigured | deactivated | missing>` line.
3. Same for TTS via `tts_provider_id`.
4. Mode override: `default_mode` is consumed downstream by whatever today reads the meeting/playground mode; document the exact integration point in the .oly.1 PRD before coding.
5. Decorate the returned bundle with which personality served it + which kinds fell back, so the session UI (sub-task .5) can render a one-line warning when a fallback fired.

### B. System-prompt injection

Where the global Johnny system prompt is interpolated today (named in the .oly.1 PRD), insert the personality `description` instead. If the personality is the migrated Johnny default, the description IS the old global prompt, so behavior is identical pre/post.

### C. Callsite updates

Every caller of `load_active_providers` learns to pass the session-scoped `personality_id`:
- Meet-worker session start (`backend/app/services/session_scheduler.py`).
- Playground session start (`backend/app/services/browser_pipeline_runner.py` — verify exact entry point).
- Any chat surface that today uses the global active providers.

### D. Tests

Required in `backend/tests/providers/test_loader_personality.py`:

- Happy path: personality with both slots set returns those rows.
- Personality with one slot NULL: that slot falls back to global active; structured log emitted.
- Personality referencing a deactivated provider: same fallback path.
- Personality referencing a DELETED provider (FK is NULL because of the ON DELETE SET NULL from sub-task .2): fallback path; no exception.
- No personality_id passed: behavior is identical to the current `load_active_providers` (regression guard).
- Concurrent session starts with different personalities do not leak state across sessions (provider instances are per-session, not shared via a stale registry singleton).

## Acceptance

- All `load_active_providers` callsites pass a personality_id (or explicitly None for "use global default personality"); audited via a one-line grep included in the PR.
- Structured `personality.fallback:` log lines appear in `docker logs api` whenever a fallback fires; can be filtered to surface "operator deleted a provider that is still wired into a personality" alerts.
- Existing tests in `backend/tests/providers/test_loader.py` pass unchanged (regression guard).
- New tests pass; `uv run mypy` + `uv run ruff check` clean.

## Dependencies

Blocked-on Johnny-oly.1 (PRD must settle override rules) and Johnny-oly.2 (resolver needs the schema + FKs).
Blocks Johnny-oly.5 (picker is only useful if the resolver actually honors the choice).

title: Backend: personality data model + CRUD API + Johnny-default Alembic migration
description:
## Why this exists

Ship the schema + REST endpoints that make personalities a first-class object in the backend, plus the bootstrap migration that lifts the current global "Johnny" defaults into the first personality. No behavior change for an operator who never opens the page.

## Scope

### A. Schema

New `personalities` table per the .oly.1 PRD. SQLAlchemy model in `backend/app/db/models.py`; partial unique index on `is_default WHERE is_default = true` so exactly one personality is the default at any moment. Foreign keys to `provider_credentials.id` with `ON DELETE SET NULL` so deleting a provider does not nuke the personality (warning surfaces in the UI instead, sub-task .5).

### B. Alembic migration

- Create the new table.
- Insert one row: `display_name="Johnny"`, `description=<current global system prompt>`, `is_default=true`, `llm_provider_id=<current active LLM row id>`, `tts_provider_id=<current active TTS row id>`, `default_mode=NULL` (so meeting/playground mode wins).
- Idempotent: re-running the migration on an already-migrated DB is a no-op.
- Rollback-safe: down migration drops the table cleanly.

### C. REST endpoints

Under `/personalities`, follow the existing providers router conventions (`backend/app/api/providers.py`):

- `GET /personalities` — list all, default first.
- `POST /personalities` — create from scratch.
- `POST /personalities/{id}/clone` — duplicate with `display_name="<original> (copy)"`.
- `GET /personalities/{id}` — read one.
- `PATCH /personalities/{id}` — partial update.
- `DELETE /personalities/{id}` — refuses if `is_default=true` (operator must promote another first).
- `POST /personalities/{id}/set-default` — atomic flip (deactivate current default + activate this one in a single transaction).

Schema validation matches the same `FieldDef` / `ProviderSchema` style used by provider config so the frontend renders consistently.

### D. Tests

Required test coverage in `backend/tests/api/test_personalities.py` + `backend/tests/db/test_personalities_model.py`:

- Every endpoint: happy path, validation errors, 404, 409.
- Set-default atomicity: rapid alternating POSTs to `set-default` between two personalities never produce a state with zero or two defaults.
- Migration: stand up an empty DB, run migration, assert exactly one Johnny default row with the migrated globals copied across; idempotency test runs the migration twice and asserts no duplicate.
- Deletion of a provider row referenced by a personality: assert the personality survives, `llm_provider_id` / `tts_provider_id` go NULL, no orphaned FK.
- Refusing to delete the default personality.

## Acceptance

- Schema migration applies cleanly on top of the current head; `alembic downgrade -1` rolls back without data loss for unaffected tables.
- Every endpoint returns the documented shape; tests at 100% line coverage on the new files.
- The "Johnny" personality exists post-migration and matches the operators current setup exactly.
- `uv run pytest backend/tests/api/test_personalities.py backend/tests/db/test_personalities_model.py` passes; `uv run mypy` and `uv run ruff check` clean.

## Dependencies

Blocked-on Johnny-oly.1 (PRD must settle the schema).
Blocks Johnny-oly.3 (resolver), Johnny-oly.4 (mgmt UI), Johnny-oly.5 (picker).
notes: **Scope addition (per .oly.6 dependency):** the same Alembic migration that creates the `personalities` table also adds a `bot_name VARCHAR` column to the `bot_sessions` table (and the playground-session equivalent if separate). At session start (in .oly.3), the resolved personality's display name is snapshot into this column so the history page can render the per-session bot name instead of the hardcoded 'Johnny' constant at frontend/src/routes/history/[id]/+page.svelte:217 / :234. NULL = legacy session, falls back to 'Johnny' in the UI.

title: Design + PRD: read current provider-loader / system-prompt flow end-to-end, propose personality data model + override rules
description:
## Why this exists

Before any code lands for the personality library (parent: Johnny-oly), an agent must read the CURRENT provider-resolution + system-prompt-assembly pipeline end to end and write a PRD describing exactly how personalities slot in. This is the design pass; nothing downstream starts until the PRD is signed off by the operator.

## What to deliver

A single file: `tasks/prd-personality-library.md`. PRD shape mirrors `tasks/prd-piper-tts-runtime-options.md` (Context / Goals / Non-goals / Architecture / Acceptance / Open questions).

### Required sections

1. **Where the system prompt lives today** — trace from `backend/app/services/` through to the LLM call. Name the assembly function, the file:line where the global Johnny prompt is injected, every other source of system-prompt text (mode-specific instructions, template overrides, calendar event description, anything else). Diagram with Mermaid.
2. **Where the active provider per kind lives today** — `backend/app/providers/loader.py:load_active_providers`. Document every callsite + every place a session-scoped provider override could be inserted without breaking the rest.
3. **Proposed personality data model** — table schema, every column with type + nullability + intent. Specifically:
    - `id`, `display_name` (unique), `description` (text), `is_default` (bool, partial unique index), `created_at`, `updated_at`.
    - `llm_provider_id` (FK to `provider_credentials.id`, nullable) — when set, overrides the global active LLM.
    - `tts_provider_id` (FK to `provider_credentials.id`, nullable) — overrides global active TTS.
    - `default_mode` (enum, nullable) — overrides meeting/playground default mode.
    - `metadata` JSONB for forward-compat (voice-tuning params per-personality, etc.).
4. **Override resolution rules** — precise precedence at session start.
    - Personality references an unconfigured / deactivated provider → fall back to global active OR fail loudly? Make a recommendation with a reason. The operator wants reliability, so the recommendation should err toward "fall back AND surface a one-line warning in the session UI", not silent failure.
    - Mode override interaction with the calendar-event mode override (Johnny-ckz today supports per-meeting modes).
    - Default personality semantics: exactly one personality is `is_default=true` at any time; bootstrap migration sets Johnny to default.
5. **UI placement decisions** — propose: new `/personalities` route for the library; personality dropdown on the calendar event detail page; personality dropdown above the prompt textarea in the playground; small "active personality" badge on the running-session card. Justify each placement, not just list them.
6. **Migration plan** — describe how the bootstrap migration creates the Johnny personality from existing globals, with zero behavior change for an operator who never touches the page. Specifically: which global setting / which provider row gets copied where.
7. **Test plan outline** — name the unit / integration test files that need to land, name the chrome-devtools MCP scenarios the test matrix (sub-task .6) needs to cover. This is an OUTLINE, not the tests themselves.
8. **Open questions for the operator** — at minimum: how to handle personality references that point at a deleted provider row (set NULL with warning vs cascade-block delete); whether multi-account bots (Johnny-al3) can each carry their own default personality OR whether the default is global; whether personality export/import belongs in v1 or v2.

### Acceptance

- PRD lands at `tasks/prd-personality-library.md` with every section above filled in with CONCRETE references (file paths, function names, table columns) — no hand-waving.
- The operator reviews + sign-offs the override-resolution rules and the UI placements before sub-tasks .2/.3/.4/.5/.6 start.
- Every open question has a recommended answer with reasoning; the operators role is to ratify, not to invent.

## Out of scope

- Code. Pure design + PRD. Implementation lives in the other sub-tasks.

## Dependencies

Blocks everything else under Johnny-oly. Self-contained — can start immediately.

title: Personality library: reusable character profiles (name + description + LLM + TTS voice) assignable to calendar events / playground; renders the per-session bot name in history
description:
## Why this exists

Today the bots character lives in two implicit places: a single system prompt buried in the global settings, plus whichever LLM + TTS providers happen to be active. Switching from "Johnny — neutral assistant" to "a different character" today means editing that prompt, swapping the active LLM, and swapping the active TTS — for every session, by hand, with no way to keep the old setup around.

The product idea is to lift "the character" into a first-class object: a **personality**. Each personality is a name + a plain-text description (traits, communication style, anything else the operator writes) plus the LLM provider/model and TTS provider/voice that personality should use. Once created, personalities are assignable on the two surfaces the bot actually runs from today — calendar events (one per meeting) and the playground page — and revertible without re-typing anything.

> **Surface audit.** Existing frontend routes (verified): `calendar/`, `history/`, `playground/`, `providers/`, `sessions/`, `settings/`, `templates/`. There is NO standalone "chat" route — the playground is the chat-style live surface and history is the read-only transcript view. Both display the bot under the hardcoded name "Johnny" (`frontend/src/routes/history/[id]/+page.svelte:217,234`). Personalities replace that hardcoding by snapshotting the personality's display name onto the session at start and rendering history rows / titles from the snapshot instead of the constant.

The operator can have a library: "Johnny" (the default), "Friendly Customer Support", "Skeptical Code Reviewer", "Calm Therapist". Each carries its own voice and its own model. Switching between them is a one-click assignment, not a config rewrite.

## What lives ON a personality vs OFF it

| On the personality | Off the personality (stays global) | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Display name | — | The name the operator picks the personality by. |
| Description (free text) | — | Goes into the system prompt at session start. Where the character lives. |
| LLM provider + model | — | Different models have noticeably different voice / pacing / tone. The operator explicitly called this out. |
| TTS provider + voice | — | The single biggest carrier of perceived character. |
| Default bot mode (listen / suggest / approval / autonomous) — OPTIONAL | If the personality leaves it blank, falls back to the meeting / playground default. | Some characters only make sense in certain modes (an "autonomous skeptic" is a different bot from a "suggest-only skeptic"). |
| — | STT provider | STT does not meaningfully affect perceived character; keeping it global avoids re-configuring the STT side every time the operator wants a different voice on the same recording pipeline. |

## How it composes with the existing system

- Personalities are **NOT** template substitutes. A template is a conversation pattern (intro / interview / standup); a personality is *who* is running it. The two compose: a meeting picks a template AND a personality.
- At session start, the providers loader (`backend/app/providers/loader.py:load_active_providers`) reads the chosen personality FIRST and uses its LLM + TTS overrides; falls back to the global active providers when the personality leaves a slot blank.
- The existing global "Johnny" system prompt + the currently-active LLM + the currently-active TTS get migrated into a built-in personality called "Johnny", marked as the default. Nothing changes for an operator who never touches the personalities page; the default keeps working.

## Sub-tasks (filed as children below)

1. **Design + PRD** — read the current provider-loader + system-prompt flow end to end, propose the personality data model, decide override rules (what fallback when the personality references an unconfigured provider), decide UI placement. Blocks everything else.
2. **Backend: data model + CRUD API + Johnny-default migration** — new `personalities` table, REST endpoints (list / create / clone / get / update / delete / set-default), Alembic migration that lifts the current globals into a built-in "Johnny" personality without data loss.
3. **Backend: personality-driven provider resolution at session start** — `load_active_providers` reads the chosen personality, swaps LLM + TTS to the personality-specified rows, falls back loudly (logged + surfaced in the session UI) when the personality references a provider the operator deleted or deactivated.
4. **Frontend: personality library management page** — list / create-from-scratch / clone / edit / delete / set-as-default. New route `/personalities`. Form fields: name, description (textarea), LLM picker, TTS picker (uses the unified voice component from Johnny-1ge.8), optional bot-mode override.
5. **Frontend: personality picker integrated into calendar events + playground + history bot-name rendering** — the two surfaces that pick a personality at session start (calendar event detail, playground) gain a dropdown; the history view stops rendering the hardcoded `'Johnny'` constant and reads the per-session bot name from the snapshot taken at session start. Active-session card surfaces the personality name too.
6. **End-to-end test matrix** — backend unit + integration tests for every CRUD endpoint, every override-resolution branch, every fallback path. Frontend browser tests via chrome-devtools MCP that drive: create a personality, assign it to a calendar event, start a session, verify the right LLM + TTS were loaded, verify the system prompt contains the personality description. Reproducible in CI without a live Meet.

## Acceptance for the epic

- A new operator with no personalities defined sees nothing change — the Johnny default behaves exactly like the current global setup.
- An operator can create a second personality, assign it to a calendar event, start that meeting, and the bot uses the personality-specified LLM + TTS, with the description in the system prompt.
- History rows for that session render the personality's name where today they render the hardcoded `'Johnny'`. Pre-personality sessions keep showing "Johnny" because that is what was true at the time.
- The personality the bot is currently using is surfaced in the active-session UI (so the operator can tell at a glance which character is in the meeting).
- Every sub-task lands with its own tests; the test matrix in `.7` runs in CI on every PR.
- README has a new "Personalities" section explaining the concept in 4-5 sentences and pointing at `/personalities`.

## Non-goals

- Mid-session personality swap. Personality is picked at session start and held for the rest of the session.
- Personality-conditioned templates / personality-conditioned routing. The personality is consumed by the LLM (as system prompt) and the TTS (as voice). Anything that needs the router to *behave differently* per personality belongs in the Johnny-etu pipeline epic, not here.
- Multi-personality conversations (Johnny + a second character in the same meeting). Single-personality-per-session is the v1 scope.
- Cloud personalities marketplace, sharing, presets. Local-only library; one operator owns their personalities the same way they own their providers.

## Cross-links

- **Johnny-1ge.8** (unified voice picker UX) — HARD DEPENDENCY for sub-task .4 (the TTS slot inside the personality form uses that component).
- **Johnny-etu** epic (pipeline + decision-making revision) — the per-session reasoning timeline (Johnny-ckz.28.4) should display which personality is active so an operator reading the timeline knows whose voice they expect.
- **Johnny-etu.1 / .etu.2** (pipeline docs) — both get a short subsection on how personalities feed into the pipeline at session start.
- **Johnny-fe** (frontend overhaul epic) — the new `/personalities` page must be designed in the shadcn-svelte system landing under that epic.
- **Johnny-ckz** epic — every closed sub-task that touched "system prompt" or "active provider selection" (Johnny-vgl, Johnny-7qp, Johnny-ckz.2 autonomous mode, Johnny-d3e provider seed) is context the design agent should re-read.

## Reference

- Current provider loader: `backend/app/providers/loader.py:load_active_providers`.
- Where the system prompt lives today: search `backend/app/services/` for prompt assembly; specifically the place that interpolates the global Johnny prompt into the per-turn LLM call.
- Templates table (do not confuse with personalities): `backend/app/db/models.py`.

title: Pipeline overview (non-technical): plain-language explainer + simple schematic so the operator understands what the bot does between hearing and speaking
description:
## Why this exists

The operator needs to understand what the bot does between hearing a question and speaking an answer — without reading code, without learning the component names, without parsing a sequence diagram. They are the customer of this system, not its engineer; they should be able to open one page and walk away with an honest mental model.

This task ships that page. Companion task (filed alongside) ships the dense technical reference for engineers; this one is its plain-language sibling.

## Deliverable

A single file: `docs/PIPELINE_OVERVIEW.md`. Short. Designed to be readable in under 10 minutes by someone who has never written a line of Python. One simple schematic at the top, plain-language explanation underneath.

### Required sections

1. **The journey of a single question** — narrated, plain English, no jargon.
    > You ask a question in the meeting. Johnny hears it, decides whether it should answer, drafts an answer with an AI model, double-checks the answer for problems, and speaks it back. Each step is a chance for Johnny to decide "no, do not answer this one" — and when that happens, Johnny tells you why.
    
    Walk the reader through the steps in that voice. Five to seven paragraphs total. No code, no class names. Use "Johnny" not "the pipeline".
2. **The simple schematic** — one boxes-and-arrows diagram. Mermaid `flowchart LR` is fine. Maybe seven boxes max:
    - **You speak** → **Johnny listens** → **Johnny decides** → **Johnny drafts** → **Johnny checks** → **Johnny speaks**, with a side branch off "Johnny decides" labelled **Johnny stays quiet (and tells you why)**.
    - No technical jargon in the box labels. "STT" never appears; it is "Johnny listens".
    - Mode-specific behaviour is mentioned in the prose, not the diagram.
3. **The three things Johnny can do at each turn** — same as the terminal-state machine in Johnny-ckz.28.3, but in human language:
    - Johnny answered you (here is what Johnny said).
    - Johnny drafted an answer and is waiting for you to approve it.
    - Johnny chose not to answer this one (here is the reason).
    
    For each, one sentence on what the operator sees in the UI and one sentence on when to expect it.
4. **The modes Johnny can be in** — listen / suggest / approval-required / auto-speak-limited / autonomous, in plain language. One sentence each. "In Suggest mode, Johnny drafts replies but waits for you to click Approve before speaking. Use this when …"
5. **Where things can go wrong (and how the UI tells you)** — preview of the customer-facing observability work in Johnny-ckz.28.4. The operator should know that when Johnny stays quiet, the UI will say WHY, and that the new reasoning timeline lets them open any past turn and see what happened.
6. **For the curious: read on** — one link to `docs/PIPELINE.md` (the technical sibling). That is where the engineer-facing detail lives.

### Tone

Warm, plain English. Sentences under 20 words on average. No acronyms without spelling them out. Read it aloud and it should sound like talking to a colleague over coffee, not a system manual.

### Diagram

One Mermaid `flowchart LR` at the top of the doc. Renders on GitHub. Boxes have plain-language labels. Maximum eight boxes including the side-branch.

## Acceptance

- `docs/PIPELINE_OVERVIEW.md` exists, covers all six sections above.
- A non-technical reader (operator profile: knows what STT and TTS are because they are setting them up in the UI, but does not read Python) can answer these three questions after reading the doc:
    1. What does Johnny do between hearing me and speaking?
    2. What are the three things Johnny might do at a turn, and how can I tell which one is happening?
    3. Where in the UI do I look when Johnny stays silent?
- The schematic at the top is one boxes-and-arrows diagram (Mermaid `flowchart LR`), with no more than eight boxes, no jargon in the labels.
- Cross-linked from the README "Layout" section right next to `docs/PIPELINE.md`.
- Validated by the operator before the epic closes — this is the surface they read.

## Out of scope

- Anything that requires engineering vocabulary. If the explanation needs the word "asyncio", "WebSocket", or "FastAPI", it belongs in the technical doc, not here.
- Diagrams of internal states (per-turn lifecycle, table relationships). Those live in `docs/PIPELINE.md`.

## Relationship to the other sub-tasks

- Companion: the technical reference (filed alongside).
- Mentions Johnny-ckz.28.4 (the reasoning timeline UI) as the place the operator GOES when Johnny stays silent and they want to know why. Doc gets updated when that UI lands so the screenshots and language line up.

title: Pipeline architecture doc (technical): full deep-dive into how STT → router → decisions → LLM → guards → TTS actually work today
description:
## Why this exists

Before any agent (or operator) can reason about the redesign work in this epic, they need a written, source-of-truth description of how the conversational pipeline works TODAY. The decision-making layer, the guards, the gating logic, the modes, the message shapes — all of it. Right now this lives in the code and in the heads of whoever last touched it. That is the exact gap that makes the bugs the operator hit in session 14 hard to triage.

This task ships the technical reference. Companion task (filed alongside) ships the non-technical overview.

## Deliverable

A single file: `docs/PIPELINE.md`. Long-form, dense, accurate. Audience is an engineer (or a future agent) who needs to know what every component does and where to change it.

### Required sections

1. **High-level data flow** — one Mermaid sequence diagram covering: meet audio in → STT → router → decision → LLM → guards/filters → TTS → meet audio out. Same diagram for both split-pipeline and unified-S2S routes; call out divergence points.
2. **Component reference** — one subsection per major component. For each:
    - Source path + the top-level class/function entry point.
    - Inputs and outputs (with concrete type names from `backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/events.py` etc.).
    - State it owns (in-memory, DB-persisted, redis-cached).
    - Lifecycle (when constructed, when destroyed, per-meeting vs per-process).
    - Where its decisions are logged + how they surface in the session UI.
3. **The router / decision layer** — this is the bit the operator cares about most.
    - Every classification category the router emits, what it means, what triggers it.
    - Every gate / suppressor (noise gate, barge-in, partial-vs-final, profanity filter, "thinking" cooldown, anything else).
    - The mode matrix (listen / suggest / approval-required / auto-speak-limited / autonomous / free-mode if still present) — what each mode does at each gate.
    - The decision record shape: what gets written, what fields exist, who reads them.
4. **Message + event shapes** — exhaustive list of pipeline events with their fields, including which ones the session UI renders and which are dev-only.
5. **Storage** — every table the pipeline writes to (transcripts, decisions, utterances, pipeline events, approvals) with column-level schema and the timing of each write.
6. **Failure modes documented in code today** — every place the pipeline catches an exception, every place it silently returns early, every place it overrides an LLM output. Document each with the file:line and the reason it exists.
7. **Cross-references** — point at the per-turn timeline UI (Johnny-ckz.28.4), the canonical record (Johnny-ckz.28.2), the terminal-state machine (Johnny-ckz.28.3), and the replay harness (Johnny-ckz.28.5) once those land.

### Diagrams

Mermaid in the markdown so they render on GitHub. At minimum:
- One end-to-end sequence diagram per pipeline route (split vs unified).
- One state diagram for the per-turn lifecycle.
- One ER-ish diagram for the persisted tables that hold pipeline state.

### Tone

Dense. No marketing. Concrete file:line refs. Reads like the existing `docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md` and `docs/LATENCY.md`, not like the README. Worked examples beat prose.

## Acceptance

- `docs/PIPELINE.md` exists, covers every section above with at least one code-traced example per subsection.
- Every component subsection links into the source at a stable anchor (file + function name; line numbers as a hint, not load-bearing).
- A reader who has never touched the pipeline can read the doc + open the named files and arrive at the same mental model the people who wrote it have.
- Every closed-issue mention of pipeline behavior (Johnny-vgl, Johnny-cdw, Johnny-arh, Johnny-ckz.14, Johnny-har, Johnny-7qp, Johnny-ckz.7, Johnny-klh) is reconciled against the doc — if the issue describes behavior the doc does not cover, the doc is incomplete.
- Linked from the README "Layout" section so a fresh operator finds it.

## Out of scope

- The redesign. This doc describes what exists TODAY, including the bugs. The redesigned pipeline gets its own section (or its own file) once Johnny-ckz.28.2 / .28.3 / .28.4 land.
- The non-technical overview — filed as a sibling task.

## Relationship to the other sub-tasks

- Informs Johnny-ckz.28.1 (root-cause analysis): the analyst should read this BEFORE diving into session 14, so they can name the components they see breaking.
- Gets updated after Johnny-ckz.28.2/.3/.4 land, to document the new invariants.
- Companion task: the non-technical overview (filed alongside) — these two ship together.

title: Offline replay harness: feed any persisted session transcript through the pipeline and assert decisions + utterances match
description:
## Why this exists

Without an offline replay harness, every pipeline change ships on hope: the operator runs a fresh Meet, watches the bot, and forms a judgement from a single session. Sub-tasks .28.1 through .28.4 each rest on a "the redesign is correct" claim that is only verifiable by running the new pipeline against past sessions and confirming the failure modes are gone AND the previously-working sessions still work.

This task builds that harness. Given a saved session id, replay every STT-final transcript through the pipeline at the same cadence, capture every pipeline event row produced, assert against either (a) the originally recorded events (regression test) or (b) declarative invariants from sub-tasks .28.2 / .28.3 (correctness test).

## Implementation shape

### A. Replay engine

A standalone command (analogous to `johnny-tts-smoke` in Johnny-1ge.7): `johnny-replay --session-id <N> [--mode invariants|regression]`.

- Loads the persisted transcripts for that session in order, including timestamps.
- Spins up the pipeline against fake STT / fake TTS adapters (PCM in/out replaced with the recorded text), but the REAL LLM provider OR a deterministic recorded-LLM fixture (`--use-recorded-llm` flag) so runs are repeatable in CI.
- Drives the pipeline at the recorded inter-turn cadence so timing-sensitive guards (barge-in, partial-vs-final) behave the same as live.
- Captures every pipeline event row + canonical turn record produced.

### B. Two assertion modes

- `--mode invariants` — for every captured turn, assert the invariants from sub-tasks .28.2 (canonical record consistency) and .28.3 (terminal state present). This is the CI default and gates merges.
- `--mode regression` — compare the produced events against the originally recorded events for the session; flag any divergence row by row. This is the manual-review mode for "did my refactor break sessions that used to work?"

### C. Fixture set

At least three sessions captured as durable fixtures: session 14 (the operators failing one), plus two known-good sessions across split-pipeline and unified-S2S runtimes. Fixtures live at `backend/tests/fixtures/sessions/<id>/` with all the transcripts + LLM responses + recorded utterances.

### D. CI wiring

`uv run johnny-replay --mode invariants` runs over every fixture as part of the existing test suite. Any invariant failure fails the build. The regression mode runs nightly against the same fixtures to catch slow drift.

### E. UI hook

A "Replay" button on the per-session page (sub-task .28.4 UI) that fires the replay against the current sessions persisted transcripts and opens a diff view comparing the new pipeline output against the recorded one. Lets the operator iterate on prompt / config changes against the same session without re-running a live Meet.

## Acceptance

- `johnny-replay --session-id 14 --mode invariants --use-recorded-llm` runs to completion and exits non-zero TODAY (because the bugs from sub-tasks .28.1 are still present) and zero AFTER the redesign lands. The exit code transition is the proof the refactor closed the gap.
- The harness is wired into `backend/johnny/smoketest/` so it runs in CI on every PR.
- At least three fixtures committed under `backend/tests/fixtures/sessions/` covering split + unified runtimes.
- Replay button on the session UI works end-to-end.
- The harness is documented in `docs/REPLAY_HARNESS.md` and referenced from the per-session page (the operator should find it without reading code).

## Cross-links

- Johnny-1ge.7 — `johnny-tts-smoke` is the model for the CLI shape and exit-code semantics.
- Johnny-cxu (open) — "Real 20-turn p50/p95 latency capture" — adjacent observability; the replay harness can produce the same numbers from any fixture without running a live Meet.

## Dependencies

Best done last in the parent epic — Sub-tasks .28.1/.28.2/.28.3 define the canonical records the harness asserts against, and .28.4 is where the UI hook lands. Can scaffold the CLI + the fixture loading earlier in parallel.

title: Unified voice picker UX: SELECT with preview / language / sample-rate across every TTS provider
description:
## Why this exists

Voice selection is inconsistent across the local TTS providers. Piper has a real voice catalog with a Browse / Install flow and a structured `voice_id` like `en_US-amy-medium` that the schema enforces. Kokoro / KittenTTS (and any future provider) currently just expose a free-text `voice_id` field — the user has to know the canonical voice id (`af_bella`, `am_adam`, …) and type it correctly, with no preview, no language filter, no indication of whether the voice even exists on disk.

The pattern Piper set is the right one: SELECT field, voice metadata visible in the dropdown, a Preview button next to each voice. Lift it into a shared interface so every TTS provider gets the same UX with zero per-provider frontend work.

## Scope

### A. New backend endpoint: GET /providers/{provider_id}/voices

Returns the canonical voice catalog the runtime currently has access to. Shape:

```json
{
  "voices": [
    {
      "id": "af_bella",
      "label": "Bella (US English, female)",
      "language": "en-US",
      "sample_rate": 24000,
      "gender": "female",
      "preview_url": null,
      "installed": true,
      "size_bytes": 318000000,
      "tier": null
    }
  ]
}
```

Backed by a new method on every `TTSProvider`: `list_voices() -> tuple[VoiceMeta, ...]`. Default implementation returns the empty tuple (so cloud TTS providers that already have their own voice flow can opt out). Local providers implement it:

- **Piper** — reuse the existing voice browser data already exposed at the voice catalog endpoint; just normalise the field names to the shared shape.
- **Kokoro** — hardcode the canonical voice list (`af`, `af_bella`, `am_adam`, `bf_emma`, …) with language + gender + sample_rate per voice. Cross-check against the `kokoro` package metadata so the list stays accurate when the package upgrades.
- **KittenTTS** — same, from KittenTTSs published voice manifest.

### B. Generic `voice_id` field type in the schema

Add a new `FieldType.VOICE_SELECT` (or extend the existing SELECT with a `voice_catalog_url: "/providers/{id}/voices"` hint). The frontend renders the same component for any provider that declares it. The component:

- Shows the list with label + language + sample-rate per row.
- Filterable by language and gender.
- Has a Preview button next to each row that POSTs the canonical short phrase to `/play_sample` with that voice_id and plays the returned PCM inline. Same wire we use for the existing per-provider Play sample button.

### C. Voice-not-installed surfacing

Some providers fetch voices on demand (Piper downloads on first use; Kokoro caches via HuggingFace). The dropdown distinguishes installed vs available: installed rows are bold, available rows show a "(download on first use)" tag. The first synthesis triggers the fetch; the frontend polls a progress endpoint so the user sees "Downloading voice ... 35%" instead of a frozen Play button.

### D. Migrate existing providers to the shared shape

- Piper: drop the textbox + browser pair, use the unified component pointing at the new `/voices` endpoint.
- Kokoro / KittenTTS: replace the free-text `voice_id` with the same component.
- Any other TTS provider that has voice_id today (ElevenLabs, OpenAI TTS, Cartesia): wire the `list_voices` method against their voice-catalog API so the UX is the same for cloud and local — even though those wont need the install/download branch.

### E. Schema validation

`voice_id` becomes a required selection; the backend rejects an unknown voice id with a 422 + the available list, so the modal can show "voice `foo_bar` not found; pick from: ..." instead of letting a typo through to a runtime failure.

## Acceptance

- `GET /providers/{id}/voices` returns the canonical list per provider.
- Voice picker component renders consistently for Piper, Kokoro, KittenTTS, and at least one cloud TTS provider in the catalog modal.
- Preview button works for every (provider × voice) cell that the play-sample test currently passes.
- Selecting a not-yet-installed voice triggers the download flow with a visible progress UI, NOT a hung Play button.
- Typing an unknown voice_id via the API returns 422 with the available list in the error body.
- Browser-validated via chrome-devtools MCP for each provider.

## Dependencies

Best done in lockstep with — or shortly after — Johnny-1ge.2 (KittenTTS) and Johnny-1ge.3 (Kokoro) so we are not refactoring those modal forms twice. Can land before Johnny-1ge.5 (docs pass) so the doc screenshots show the final UX.

title: Auto-start sidecars from ./run.sh + standardised per-launcher CLI (commands, env vars, exit codes, log layout)
description:
## Why this exists

Today, after `./run.sh` brings the Docker stack up, the operator still has to remember to run `./scripts/start-parakeet-sidecar.sh mlx` separately before a Parakeet sidecar runtime works. Same pain is about to land for the TTS sidecars (Piper / Kitten / Kokoro): a saved runtime that points at `host.docker.internal:8775` returns `synthesis failed: piper sidecar at http://host.docker.internal:8775 unreachable: All connection attempts failed. Start it with ./scripts/start-piper-sidecar.sh` — a real error the user already hit.

The runtime picker UX is great; the boot UX is not. Fix: make `./run.sh` start every available sidecar by default, with a clear opt-out for any the operator does not want, and a clear status surface afterwards.

The user accepted the memory cost ("I don’t think they’re gonna be super heavy") — a 0.6 B Parakeet model is ~600 MB, a Piper voice is ~60 MB, Kokoro is ~300 MB. Total ceiling around 1.5 GB resident on a host that already has Docker Desktop and probably 16+ GB of RAM. Worth the always-on convenience.

## Scope

### A. New umbrella launcher: scripts/start-sidecars.sh

Wraps the per-provider launchers (start-parakeet-sidecar.sh today, start-piper-sidecar.sh / start-kitten-sidecar.sh / start-kokoro-sidecar.sh as they ship) behind one entry point:

```
./scripts/start-sidecars.sh start           # start every enabled sidecar
./scripts/start-sidecars.sh stop            # stop every running sidecar
./scripts/start-sidecars.sh status          # one line per sidecar: running / stopped / disabled / unavailable
./scripts/start-sidecars.sh restart         # stop + start
./scripts/start-sidecars.sh --help          # what each command does, what env vars exist
```

Idempotent on `start` (already-running sidecars are a no-op). Top of the file has a help block with: which sidecars exist, their default ports, the env vars that disable them, what to do when one fails to start.

### B. Default = everything on. Disable list via env var.

`JOHNNY_DISABLED_SIDECARS` is a comma-separated list of sidecar keys to skip. Empty by default. Read by both `start-sidecars.sh` and `./run.sh`.

Recognised keys: `parakeet-mlx`, `parakeet-coreml`, `piper-http`, `kitten-http`, `kokoro-mlx`, `kokoro-http`. Unknown keys are warned about but do not error (forward-compatible when new sidecars ship).

Example:

```bash
JOHNNY_DISABLED_SIDECARS=parakeet-coreml,kokoro-mlx ./run.sh
```

### C. ./run.sh integration

After `docker compose up -d --build`, `./run.sh` invokes `./scripts/start-sidecars.sh start` (unless the env var lists every sidecar). Run.shs trailing log block updates to also list sidecar status — something like:

```
[run.sh] Stack started in the background.
[run.sh]   Frontend:    http://localhost:5173
[run.sh]   API:         http://localhost:8000
[run.sh]   Sidecars:    parakeet-mlx :8765 ok, parakeet-coreml SKIPPED (no swift), piper-http :8775 ok
[run.sh] Sidecar logs: tail -f .validation/parakeet-mlx-sidecar.log
[run.sh] Stop stack:   ./stop.sh
```

### D. ./stop.sh integration

Invokes `./scripts/start-sidecars.sh stop` BEFORE `docker compose down -v` (so running synthesis calls drain into a clean error instead of a half-torn-down stack).

### E. Graceful skip for unavailable sidecars

`start-parakeet-sidecar.sh coreml` currently errors out hard if Xcode command-line tools are not installed. Promote that to a soft skip: log "coreml sidecar SKIPPED: swift not on PATH" and continue. Same idea for any sidecar whose deps are missing — the stack still comes up, just without that runtime.

### F. Sidecar status endpoint visible to the api

Add a `/sidecars/health` endpoint in the api (or a small extension of an existing health endpoint) that probes each sidecar URL the api knows about, returns `{name, url, ok, latency_ms, error}` per entry. The frontend providers modal can then surface "sidecar running ✓" / "sidecar offline ✗ — start with ..." right next to the Runtime picker, so a saved sidecar-runtime that does not have its sidecar up shows the user WHY before they click Test.

### G. Help / docs

- Top-of-file help block in every shell script (`start-sidecars.sh`, the per-provider launchers, `run.sh`).
- README "Sidecar management" subsection under the existing "NVIDIA Parakeet STT runtimes" / "Local Piper TTS runtimes" tables.
- Mention the env var in `.env.example` so a new operator sees it.

### H. Standardise the per-provider launcher CLI

Today `scripts/start-parakeet-sidecar.sh` uses `mlx | coreml | status | stop` as positional commands. The Piper / Kitten / Kokoro launchers landing in this epic should NOT each invent their own argument shape — the umbrella `start-sidecars.sh` (section A) needs a uniform interface to dispatch to.

Lock the convention now, then refactor any drift:

**Common commands every `start-*-sidecar.sh` MUST accept (same name, same exit semantics):**

```
./scripts/start-<provider>-sidecar.sh start [<backend>]   # start one or all backends for this provider
./scripts/start-<provider>-sidecar.sh stop  [<backend>]   # stop one or all
./scripts/start-<provider>-sidecar.sh restart [<backend>] # stop + start
./scripts/start-<provider>-sidecar.sh status              # one line per backend: running | stopped | disabled | unavailable
./scripts/start-<provider>-sidecar.sh logs  [<backend>]   # tail the .validation/<provider>-<backend>-sidecar.log file
./scripts/start-<provider>-sidecar.sh --help              # full help block
```

The optional `<backend>` arg names a specific variant (`mlx`, `coreml`, `http`, `python`, etc.). Omitted = the provider's default = "every backend this provider supports". Unknown backend = exit code 2 with a message listing valid backends. The current Parakeet launcher's `mlx` / `coreml` positional shape becomes `start mlx` / `start coreml`, with a transitional alias kept for one release so existing muscle memory does not bite operators.

**Common env vars (same name across every launcher):**

- `PARAKEET_MLX_PORT`, `PARAKEET_COREML_PORT`, `PIPER_HTTP_PORT`, `KITTEN_HTTP_PORT`, `KOKORO_MLX_PORT`, `KOKORO_HTTP_PORT` — already de-facto standard, formalise the `<UPPER_PROVIDER>_<UPPER_BACKEND>_PORT` rule.
- `<UPPER_PROVIDER>_<UPPER_BACKEND>_HOST` — bind host, defaults to `127.0.0.1`.
- `<UPPER_PROVIDER>_<UPPER_BACKEND>_MODEL` — model id or path override.
- `JOHNNY_SIDECAR_LOG_DIR` — where all `.log` and `.pid` files land. Defaults to `.validation/` to match what `start-parakeet-sidecar.sh` already does.

**Common exit codes (same meaning across every launcher):**

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Success (or already in the requested state — start of running = ok, stop of stopped = ok). |
| 1 | Generic failure (build error, model download failed, port bind failed). |
| 2 | Bad usage (unknown command, unknown backend, conflicting flags). |
| 3 | Toolchain unavailable (no `swift`, no `uv`, no `piper` binary). Used by the umbrella to print SKIPPED. |
| 4 | Sidecar already running on a different port than the one this invocation asked for (lets the umbrella surface the conflict instead of silently overwriting the PID file). |

**Common log/PID layout:**

```
.validation/parakeet-mlx-sidecar.log     .validation/parakeet-mlx-sidecar.pid
.validation/parakeet-coreml-sidecar.log  .validation/parakeet-coreml-sidecar.pid
.validation/piper-http-sidecar.log       .validation/piper-http-sidecar.pid
.validation/kitten-http-sidecar.log      .validation/kitten-http-sidecar.pid
.validation/kokoro-mlx-sidecar.log       .validation/kokoro-mlx-sidecar.pid
.validation/kokoro-http-sidecar.log      .validation/kokoro-http-sidecar.pid
```

Naming rule: `<provider>-<backend>-sidecar.{log,pid}` — no other shapes. Lets `start-sidecars.sh status` and the new `/sidecars/health` endpoint discover every sidecar by globbing one directory.

**Help block shape every script SHARES:**

```
NAME
    start-<provider>-sidecar.sh — manage the <provider> sidecar(s) on the macOS host

USAGE
    ./scripts/start-<provider>-sidecar.sh <command> [<backend>] [flags]

COMMANDS
    start [<backend>]    Start a backend (or all backends if omitted).
    stop  [<backend>]    Stop a backend (or all).
    restart [<backend>]  stop + start.
    status               One line per backend: running | stopped | disabled | unavailable.
    logs [<backend>]     Tail the matching sidecar log file.

BACKENDS
    <list each backend this provider supports, with default port>

ENV
    <UPPER_PROVIDER>_<UPPER_BACKEND>_PORT   bind port (default: …)
    <UPPER_PROVIDER>_<UPPER_BACKEND>_HOST   bind host (default: 127.0.0.1)
    <UPPER_PROVIDER>_<UPPER_BACKEND>_MODEL  model override (default: …)
    JOHNNY_SIDECAR_LOG_DIR                  log/PID directory (default: .validation/)

EXIT CODES
    0=ok  1=failure  2=bad usage  3=toolchain unavailable  4=port conflict
```

## Acceptance

- A fresh `./run.sh` on a clean checkout brings the Docker stack up AND starts every available sidecar AND logs one-line status for each.
- `JOHNNY_DISABLED_SIDECARS=parakeet-coreml ./run.sh` skips that one cleanly and reports it as DISABLED in the status line.
- `./stop.sh` stops every running sidecar before tearing down compose.
- `./scripts/start-sidecars.sh status` prints one line per known sidecar.
- A `/sidecars/health` endpoint reports per-sidecar reachability JSON.
- The Providers modal for a runtime that points at a sidecar shows a live "sidecar running" / "sidecar offline" badge next to Runtime.
- `--help` flag on every script returns the help block.
- Missing toolchain (no swift, no uv, no piper binary) results in SKIPPED with a clear reason, NOT a hard failure.
- Every `start-*-sidecar.sh` accepts the seven canonical commands above with identical exit semantics — verified by a one-page shell script that loops over every launcher and runs `--help`, `status`, `stop bogus-backend` (expects exit 2), and asserts the help block matches the shared shape regex.
- `start-parakeet-sidecar.sh mlx` keeps working as a transitional alias for `start mlx`; running it prints a one-line deprecation note pointing at the canonical form.
- The umbrella `start-sidecars.sh` contains zero per-provider branching beyond a list of which launcher scripts exist — every backend-specific decision lives in the per-provider script.

## Out of scope / follow-up

- True process supervision (systemd / pm2 / launchctl). For now, killing the host TTY kills the sidecars via parent PID. If a sidecar crashes mid-meeting, the api error already tells the user to restart — auto-restart is a separate concern.
- Sidecar autoscaling. One process per sidecar is fine for single-user Johnny.

## Dependencies

This task can land BEFORE the TTS sidecars (Johnny-1ge.1/.2/.3) ship — even with just the existing Parakeet sidecars wired in, the auto-boot UX is a win. The umbrella script just gains entries as each TTS sidecar ships.

title: Piper TTS runtime picker: subprocess / persistent-subprocess / http-sidecar
description:
## PRD

Full requirements at `tasks/prd-piper-tts-runtime-options.md` — read that first; this issue tracks implementation against it.

## TL;DR

Add a `runtime` SELECT field on the Local Piper provider with three options, matching the Parakeet pattern:

- `subprocess` (default) — todays behaviour, fresh `piper` subprocess per call. Safe debug baseline.
- `persistent-subprocess` — module-cached long-running `piper --json-input` process per `(model_path, native_sample_rate)`. Target <=100 ms time-to-first-audio warm.
- `http-sidecar` — `piper --http` server on the macOS host. Sidecar at `sidecars/piper-http/`, launcher at `scripts/start-piper-sidecar.sh`. Mirror of the Parakeet sidecar pattern.

## Why now

Today every PiperTTS.synthesize_stream call (`backend/app/providers/piper_tts.py:693`) spawns a fresh subprocess; the existing tip at piper_tts.py:612 already flags it as "the next big win" — ~200-400 ms of pure ONNX-runtime cold-start per turn, on the meeting hot path.

## Reference implementation

Copy the shape from the Parakeet runtime split (merged this session):
- Module-level `_LAST` / `_LOAD_LOCKS` / `_GLOBAL_LOAD_GATE` in parakeet_stt.py.
- Per-key asyncio.Lock + post-lock cache re-check pattern in `_ensure_model`.
- `evict_process_cache` classmethod.
- Autouse test fixture wiping module state between tests.
- Sidecar launcher script at scripts/start-parakeet-sidecar.sh.

## Acceptance criteria

- Provider modal renders the runtime picker with three options + a sidecar_url field.
- `subprocess` preserves todays behaviour bit-for-bit.
- `persistent-subprocess`: second Play sample click on the same provider returns audio in <=100 ms TTFA (vs ~300 ms cold). Verified via the latency badge + `piper.synth: runtime=persistent-subprocess ttfa_ms=...` log line.
- `http-sidecar`: with the sidecar started, Play sample works; with it stopped, the api returns a clear TTSError mentioning the start script.
- Real meeting smoke: a typical Johnny reply on the persistent runtime starts speaking within ~150 ms of LLM completion.
- All existing tests in `backend/tests/providers/test_piper_tts.py` continue to pass on the `subprocess` default. New tests cover persistent + http-sidecar paths.
- README + tips section updated to describe the runtime picker (existing tip at piper_tts.py:612 gets rewritten).
- Browser-validated via chrome-devtools MCP.

## Open questions (called out in the PRD)

1. Does `piper --json-input --output_raw` emit a reliable per-utterance separator on stdout? Verify with `piper --help`. If not, Option B may need to switch to the piper-tts Python library.
2. Does the bundled `piper --http` server ship in the version installed via the `local-tts` extra in backend/Dockerfile, or is it a separate binary?

title: Local TTS performance + new providers: persistent processes, sidecars, KittenTTS, Kokoro
description:
## Why this exists

Today every PiperTTS.synthesize_stream call spawns a fresh piper subprocess (backend/app/providers/piper_tts.py:693 -> _spawn_process at line 746). The ONNX runtime + voice-model cold-start adds ~200-400 ms of pure overhead PER conversation turn. Unlike Parakeet (where per-request load only hurt the catalog Test button — meeting providers are pre-loaded by load_active_providers), TTS pays this cost on every reply Johnny speaks in a real meeting.

This epic does for TTS what the Parakeet runtime split did for STT:

1. Give the existing Piper provider a runtime picker (subprocess / persistent-subprocess / http-sidecar), defaulting to the safe current behaviour. PRD already written at tasks/prd-piper-tts-runtime-options.md.
2. Add two new local TTS providers (KittenTTS, Kokoro) with the same 3-runtime shape so the user can pick whichever voice + speed trade-off they want.

Each provider exposes the same kind of Runtime dropdown in Settings -> Providers, with structured `<provider>.synth: runtime=... ttfa_ms=...` INFO logs visible in docker logs api so the user can verify the picker is actually doing what they expect and debug runtime-specific failures independently.

## Acceptance for the epic as a whole

- Three providers (Piper, KittenTTS, Kokoro) each ship with three selectable runtimes covering the in-container default, an in-container optimised path, and an out-of-container sidecar option.
- Real meeting hot-path TTS latency drops from ~300 ms cold to <= 100 ms warm on whichever provider the user picks for the in-container optimised path.
- README has a new "Local TTS providers" table listing voices, sample-rate quirks, and the three runtime options per provider.
- Browser-validated via chrome-devtools MCP for each provider: switch runtime in the modal, click Play sample, observe latency badge + structured log.

## Child issues

- Piper runtime split (subprocess / persistent / http-sidecar) — PRD at tasks/prd-piper-tts-runtime-options.md.
- KittenTTS provider (https://github.com/KittenML/KittenTTS) with the same 3-runtime picker.
- Kokoro provider (https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro) with the same 3-runtime picker.

## Reference implementation

The Parakeet runtime split is the canonical example to copy:
- Module-level cache + per-key asyncio.Lock + global load gate: backend/app/providers/parakeet_stt.py (search for `_LAST`, `_LOAD_LOCKS`, `_GLOBAL_LOAD_GATE`, `_ensure_model`, `evict_process_cache`).
- Runtime dispatch inside transcribe_stream: parakeet_stt.py:_transcribe_in_container vs _transcribe_via_sidecar.
- Sidecar wire protocol + launcher script: sidecars/parakeet-mlx/ and scripts/start-parakeet-sidecar.sh.
- Test seam (autouse fixture evicts the module cache between tests): backend/tests/providers/test_parakeet_stt.py:_reset_parakeet_process_cache.

title: Verify the CoreML / FluidAudio Parakeet sidecar builds and serves on a clean macOS host
description: The Swift sidecar at sidecars/parakeet-coreml/ was written based on the FluidAudio API as used by VoiceInk, plus Hummingbird 2 for the HTTP layer. It hasn't been built in this session — the MLX sidecar was end-to-end verified (~107 ms warm /stt_test), but the CoreML sidecar needs an actual swift build run to confirm: 1) Package.swift dependency versions resolve (FluidAudio >= 0.5.0, Hummingbird >= 2.0.0). 2) Hummingbird 2 router/handler API matches what main.swift uses (Response/jsonResponse/Router are imported from the right modules). 3) FluidAudio's AsrManager.transcribe(samples, decoderState:) signature matches what we call. 4) The wire protocol round-trips end-to-end against the api container. Steps: xcode-select --install if not present; ./scripts/start-parakeet-sidecar.sh coreml; switch Parakeet runtime to coreml-sidecar in the UI; record sample; verify ~150 ms latency.

title: Sidebar (z-1300) renders above modals — noVNC sign-in + BotSigninUpload + BotSigninMethodPicker use bare z-50 instead of --z-modal tokens
description:
## Context / Why
User repro (2026-06-07): opened the noVNC sign-in modal from /settings; the left sidebar (with menu / navigation) renders ON TOP of the modal overlay, obscuring the embedded Chromium and the close affordance. The modal is supposed to be a focused, blocking surface — a sidebar floating over it breaks the mental model and partially hides controls.

## Current behavior (the bug — two compounding issues)
The project already has a documented z-index token scale in `frontend/src/app.css:165-172`:
  --z-base: 0
  --z-raised: 10
  --z-dropdown: 1000
  --z-sticky: 1100
  --z-modal-backdrop: 1200
  --z-modal: 1300
  --z-toast: 1400
  --z-tooltip: 1500

But:

### Bug A — Sidebar sits at modal-layer z-index
`frontend/src/routes/+layout.svelte:344` puts the `<aside>` sidebar at `z-[1300]`, which is the same value as `--z-modal`. So it competes with (and beats) any modal that uses anything below 1300. The mobile-only sidebar backdrop is at `z-[1200]` (= `--z-modal-backdrop`) and the menu toggle at `z-[1100]` — those are reasonable, but the sidebar itself should NOT be at modal level. A global navigation element should sit no higher than `--z-sticky` (1100) so any modal automatically wins.

### Bug B — noVNC sign-in family uses bare Tailwind z-50, ignoring tokens
`frontend/src/lib/components/settings/BotSigninModal.svelte:254` — modal overlay uses `z-50` (= literal z-index: 50). That's 26× lower than the sidebar. Even with bug A fixed, the modal would still need to use the proper tokens. Same pattern needs auditing in:
  - `frontend/src/lib/components/settings/BotSigninUploadModal.svelte`
  - `frontend/src/lib/components/settings/BotSigninMethodPicker.svelte`
  - And the bare `z-10`/`z-20` overlay layers inside `BotSigninModal.svelte:369, 381, 389` (status overlays — should be relative to the modal's own stacking context, fine as-is, but worth confirming)

Compare with the correct pattern in `frontend/src/routes/calendar/+page.svelte:703` (`z-[var(--z-modal-backdrop)]`) and `:709` (`z-[var(--z-modal)]`). Calendar got it right; settings bot-signin family did not.

## Expected behavior
- When the noVNC sign-in modal is open, it covers the sidebar and the rest of the chrome.
- The sidebar should NEVER be above any modal-backdrop or modal-foreground element.
- All modal overlays in the app use the documented `--z-modal-backdrop` / `--z-modal` tokens (or a `calc(var(--z-modal) + N)` for nested layers within the same dialog), so future modals stack predictably.

## Repro steps
1. `./run-dev.sh`; open /settings.
2. Trigger a noVNC sign-in (Add bot → noVNC method).
3. With the modal open, observe the left sidebar overlapping the modal overlay (sidebar text/icons visible on top of the dimmed backdrop and the iframe area).
4. Inspect DOM: sidebar `<aside>` has `z-[1300]`, modal overlay has `z-50`.

## Scope (in)
- **Bug A fix**: in `frontend/src/routes/+layout.svelte:344`, change the sidebar from `z-[1300]` to `z-[var(--z-sticky)]` (1100). Validate the mobile-sidebar backdrop (currently `z-[1200]`) still sits between body content and the sidebar — if it now overlaps the sidebar visually on mobile, drop it to `z-[var(--z-sticky)]` minus a hair, OR keep it at `--z-modal-backdrop` and move the sidebar to a hair above (e.g. 1199). Pick whichever preserves mobile behaviour without re-introducing the bug.
- **Bug B fix**:
    - `BotSigninModal.svelte:254` `z-50` → `z-[var(--z-modal)]`
    - Audit `BotSigninUploadModal.svelte` and `BotSigninMethodPicker.svelte` for the same anti-pattern and migrate to the tokens.
    - Inner overlays at `z-10` / `z-20` inside `BotSigninModal.svelte` are stacked within the modal's own positioned ancestor — confirm they're inside a `relative` / `transform`-creating parent so they're scoped to the modal, NOT competing with the global scale. If they're not scoped, fix the parent positioning OR re-express them as small offsets above the modal token (e.g. `z-[calc(var(--z-modal)+1)]`).
- **Audit sweep** (don't expand scope, but flag): grep the rest of `frontend/src` for bare `z-[0-9]+` / `z-[N]` outside `z-[var(--z-...)]` and list each occurrence in the PR description. Don't auto-migrate other surfaces in this ticket — just leave a note so we can file follow-ups.

## Scope (out)
- Re-architecting the layout/sidebar (Johnny-fe handles broader frontend redesign).
- Adding new z-index tokens to the scale.
- Migrating non-modal surfaces away from bare `z-50`/`z-40` etc. (out of scope; document and move on).

## Playground / sandbox parity (REQUIRED)
The sidebar exists on every authenticated route, including /playground. Any modal triggered from /playground (currently there are some — confirm during validation) must also sit above the sidebar after the fix.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With the noVNC sign-in modal open, the sidebar is NOT visible on top of the modal backdrop or overlay — confirmed by chrome-devtools MCP screenshot
- [ ] On mobile width (< md), the existing slide-out sidebar behaviour still works correctly (open / close / backdrop dismiss), with no z-index regression
- [ ] `BotSigninModal.svelte`, `BotSigninUploadModal.svelte`, and `BotSigninMethodPicker.svelte` all use `z-[var(--z-modal-backdrop)]` / `z-[var(--z-modal)]` (and nested-layer offsets via `calc(...)` where appropriate); no bare `z-50` left on the outer modal/backdrop elements
- [ ] Sidebar in `+layout.svelte` no longer uses `z-[1300]`; it sits at or below `--z-sticky` (or below `--z-modal-backdrop`, whichever the implementer chooses with reasoning in PR)
- [ ] No regression in existing modal surfaces on /calendar, /providers — both still open above sidebar (they already did, but re-verify)
- [ ] The PR description includes the bare-`z-[0-9]` grep output as a list of follow-up candidates (not fixed here, just documented)

## Validation
- Browser (chrome-devtools MCP), MANDATORY:
    - `./scripts/start-chrome.sh`; `./run-dev.sh`
    - Navigate /settings → open noVNC sign-in modal → screenshot → assert sidebar IS NOT visible on top of the modal overlay (snapshot DOM, check computed z-index of `<aside>` < overlay's)
    - Repeat for the upload modal (BotSigninUploadModal) and method picker (BotSigninMethodPicker)
    - Resize to mobile width (< 768px) → toggle the sidebar → open a modal → assert correct stacking + dismissal behaviour
    - Cross-check: open a modal on /calendar and on /providers, assert no regression
    - Save under `.validation/Johnny-ckz-modal-zindex/NN-*.png`
- Frontend lint / typecheck: `docker compose exec frontend pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck` — green
- After edits, rebuild the container per persistent memory `johnny-frontend-no-bindmount`: `docker compose build frontend && docker compose up -d frontend`

## Required process — non-negotiable
- **Maximum-effort mode.**
- **Mandatory web search** for:
    - Tailwind v4 best practices for using CSS-variable-based z-index tokens (`z-[var(--token)]`) vs Tailwind's built-in `z-*` scale
    - Common z-index stack patterns for app shells with persistent sidebars + dialog overlays (Radix, shadcn, Headless UI baselines)
- Cite the references adopted in PR.

## Anti-patterns — do not close prematurely
- ❌ "Bumped BotSigninModal to z-[1400] — closing." → reject. Token system exists for a reason; use it. Stacking above `--z-toast` will break toast surfaces.
- ❌ "Only fixed BotSigninModal; sidebar still at 1300." → reject. Sidebar at modal-level z-index is the systemic bug; future modals will hit it.
- ❌ "Sidebar lowered but mobile slide-out broke." → reject. Mobile UX must be preserved.
- ❌ "Tests pass but you can still see the sidebar through the modal in the browser." → reject. Browser screenshot is the source of truth.
- ✅ "Sidebar lowered to --z-sticky; modal overlays migrated to tokens; mobile UX intact; chrome-devtools MCP screenshots demonstrate the fix on noVNC + upload + picker modals; calendar/providers modals show no regression." → accept.

title: Consolidate free_auto_speak into autonomous — remove FREE_AUTO_SPEAK BotMode
description:
## Context / Why
`BotMode` currently has both `FREE_AUTO_SPEAK` and `AUTONOMOUS`. Per the docstrings in `backend/app/db/models.py`:
  - FREE_AUTO_SPEAK: "like LIMITED_AUTO_SPEAK but the bot answers freely (no allowlist, no approval). Router's confidence_threshold still gates whether the bot speaks at all."
  - AUTONOMOUS: "free-form generation governed solely by the profile template's instructions and context. No allowlist, no approval round; router's confidence_threshold and a per-session rate limit keep cost + over-talking in check."

The two are operationally equivalent in the speak-or-not decision; AUTONOMOUS just adds two guard rails (non-empty instructions, lower rate-limit cap). Maintaining both is confusing for users and adds dead branches in the backend, frontend, and tests.

Decision: remove `FREE_AUTO_SPEAK`, keep `AUTONOMOUS` as the single "freely answers" mode.

## Scope (in)
### Backend
- Remove `FREE_AUTO_SPEAK` from `BotMode` enum in `backend/app/db/models.py`.
- Alembic migration: convert all existing rows with mode = 'free_auto_speak' to 'autonomous' across `templates`, `meeting_configs`, `agent_utterances`, and any other table that stores the mode. For rows whose `base_instructions` / `instructions` are empty (which AUTONOMOUS validation forbids), write a sensible default instruction string (e.g. "Respond freely when confident the user wants an answer. Do not paraphrase questions back; just answer.") — this preserves behaviour and satisfies validation.
- Update `backend/app/api/browser_sessions.py`:
    - line ~416 default `or "free_auto_speak"` → `or "autonomous"`
    - line ~482 `BotMode.FREE_AUTO_SPEAK.value` → `BotMode.AUTONOMOUS.value`
    - Playground sessions: if the request doesn't carry instructions, server must inject the same default migration string so AUTONOMOUS validation passes.
- Update `backend/app/services/session_status_subscriber.py`: drop 'free_auto_speak' from the mode tuple at line ~240. Behaviour for AUTONOMOUS is already covered.
- `backend/app/services/agent_utterances.py`: unknown-mode fallback already points at LIMITED_AUTO_SPEAK — fine to leave.
- Update API validation in `backend/app/api/meeting_configs.py` and `backend/app/api/templates.py`: no `free_auto_speak`-specific branches to drop (already absent), but make sure the autonomous-instructions validation isn't bypassed for rows migrated by the Alembic step.

### Frontend
- `frontend/src/lib/templates.ts`: drop `'free_auto_speak'` from the `BotMode` union, `BOT_MODES` array, and `BOT_MODE_LABEL` map.
- `frontend/src/lib/sessionDetail.ts`: drop from union.
- `frontend/src/routes/calendar/+page.svelte`, `templates/+page.svelte`, `playground/+page.svelte`: remove the description entry and any UI option.
- `frontend/src/routes/playground/+page.svelte`: change default `let mode = $state<BotMode>('free_auto_speak')` → `'autonomous'` and ensure the default instructions field is non-empty so AUTONOMOUS validation passes when the user hits Start.

### Tests
- Backend tests that reference `FREE_AUTO_SPEAK` / `'free_auto_speak'` — port to `AUTONOMOUS`.
- Add a migration test: an Alembic upgrade against a fixture DB containing templates/meeting_configs with `free_auto_speak` (some with empty instructions, some with non-empty) results in `autonomous` rows that all pass AUTONOMOUS validation.

## Playground / sandbox parity (REQUIRED)
After the change, the /playground default mode is AUTONOMOUS with a non-empty default instruction, and live Meet sessions starting from the calendar route also default to AUTONOMOUS. Both surfaces must launch without the user needing to type instructions on first use (server-side default is fine — but make it visible in the UI so users know what's set).

## Scope (out)
- Touching LIMITED_AUTO_SPEAK, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, SUGGEST_ONLY, LISTEN_ONLY — they have distinct semantics.
- Reworking the AUTONOMOUS rate-limit default.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `BotMode.FREE_AUTO_SPEAK` no longer exists in `backend/app/db/models.py`; Python imports compile clean.
- [ ] Alembic migration upgrade + downgrade pair exists; upgrade migrates existing `free_auto_speak` rows to `autonomous` with the default instruction text; downgrade restores the original value.
- [ ] No occurrences of `free_auto_speak` / `FREE_AUTO_SPEAK` anywhere in `backend/app` or `frontend/src` after the change (grep is clean).
- [ ] /providers, /playground, /calendar, /templates: the dropdown no longer offers "Free auto-speak" as an option.
- [ ] Starting a /playground session with default settings creates an AUTONOMOUS session that passes validation and the bot speaks.
- [ ] Starting a live Meet session via /calendar with the default mode also produces an AUTONOMOUS session that passes validation.
- [ ] All existing backend + frontend tests pass; tests that referenced `free_auto_speak` are ported and still green.
