title: Frontend migration: move ALL frontend to shadcn-svelte per llms.txt — foundation for all UI refactors (REQUIRES PLAN MODE)
description:
## Goal

Migrate the **entire** frontend to **shadcn-svelte** (https://www.shadcn-svelte.com) as the single component library. Every page, every component, every form, every modal, every list, every button uses shadcn-svelte primitives.

Reference / required instructions: **https://www.shadcn-svelte.com/llms.txt** — the migration must follow these instructions to the letter. Read the llms.txt fully before any setup work.

## Why this is the foundation

Every other in-flight UI ticket in this epic — [[Johnny-stt.5]] (unified provider settings UX), [[Johnny-stt.7]] (multi-instance regression), [[Johnny-stt.8]] (Add/Edit/Delete modal pattern) — depends on a coherent component library. Doing those refactors **before** the shadcn-svelte migration would mean rewriting the same UI surfaces twice. So this ticket lands first; .5 / .7 / .8 build on top of it.

## Priority

**P2 — not urgent.** User explicitly deprioritized in-session: *"actually right now it's not super important. Put everything into one single epic."* This is real work and important strategically, but it sits behind everything currently flagged P0 or P1 elsewhere in the project.

## 🚨 PLAN MODE IS MANDATORY 🚨

Same rule as Johnny-stt.5 and .8. This is the largest UI change in the project's history; it cannot be hacked together component by component without a plan.

Before writing any production code:

1. **Read https://www.shadcn-svelte.com/llms.txt fully.** Document the install/config steps, the component patterns, the theming approach, the dark-mode story.
2. **Inventory the current frontend** — list every page, every reusable component, every form, every modal. Cross-reference each to the shadcn-svelte primitive(s) that will replace it.
3. **Identify the surfaces in flight** — .3 streaming UI (currently in_progress), .5 / .7 / .8 (open). Coordinate with their assignees so they don't ship pre-shadcn UI that immediately needs re-migration.
4. **Enter plan mode** (`EnterPlanMode` / `/plan`) and produce a concrete plan covering:
   - Installation + theming setup (Tailwind config, components.json, CSS variables).
   - Per-surface migration order (probably: shared shell → navigation → settings pages → playground → calendar → modals).
   - The cutover strategy — big-bang single PR (small project, possible) vs. surface-by-surface PRs with both component systems coexisting briefly (lower risk, more churn).
   - The validation strategy — chrome-devtools MCP screenshot tour comparing before/after per major surface.
   - Whether to split into sub-tickets per surface if the single-ticket scope proves too large.
5. **Get the plan approved before exiting plan mode.**

## Scope

- Install shadcn-svelte per llms.txt.
- Configure Tailwind, design tokens, and theming.
- Migrate every existing UI component to its shadcn-svelte equivalent.
- Delete the previous component implementations once their shadcn-svelte replacements are in place.
- Ensure no mixed UX: nowhere in the app should a bespoke button / input / dialog sit next to a shadcn-svelte one (except briefly during a phased rollout, if that's the approved strategy).

## Out of scope

- Adding new features that don't exist today.
- Backend / provider plugin changes.
- The actual content / copy of any page (only the component primitives).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] shadcn-svelte installed, configured, and themed per llms.txt — repo follows the canonical structure (`components.json`, `lib/components/ui/`, etc.).
- [ ] Every existing page in the app renders using shadcn-svelte primitives. No bespoke alternatives remain where a shadcn-svelte primitive exists.
- [ ] Theming (light + dark, if applicable) works across every surface.
- [ ] All existing user flows still work end-to-end (playground, settings, calendar, sign-in, session management) — no functional regressions.
- [ ] No dead code: old bespoke components, unreferenced CSS, orphaned utilities are removed.
- [ ] Visual consistency: spacing, typography, color usage match the shadcn-svelte conventions across every surface.
- [ ] Lighthouse / bundle-size sanity check — final bundle is not dramatically larger than before (shadcn-svelte is copy-paste components, so this should hold).

## Validation — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

A representative screenshot tour for the PR description:

1. `navigate_page` → app root.
2. `take_screenshot` of: home / dashboard, provider settings, playground, calendar import, session list, session detail, sign-in.
3. For each captured surface: assert visual consistency vs. the shadcn-svelte design language (no leftover bespoke buttons, inputs, modals).
4. `list_console_messages` — no warnings about missing imports, deprecated components, etc.
5. `list_network_requests` — no 404s on stale stylesheets / removed assets.
6. Smoke-test every key user flow at least once: add a provider, create a session, click leave-now, open playground, send a chat message. Each must still work.

## Open questions

- Does the existing Tailwind config conflict with shadcn-svelte's expected setup? (To be answered during exploration.)
- Is there a dark-mode story in the current app? If yes, how does it map to shadcn-svelte's theme tokens?
- Single big-bang PR or staged surface-by-surface migration? Decide during plan mode.
- Should this ticket be promoted to an epic and split into per-surface sub-tickets? Acceptable if the assignee deems it necessary.

## Related

- [[Johnny-stt.5]] — unified provider settings UX refactor. Depends on this ticket.
- [[Johnny-stt.7]] — multi-instance per-kind regression. Depends on this ticket.
- [[Johnny-stt.8]] — Add/Edit/Delete modal pattern. Depends on this ticket.
- [[Johnny-stt.3]] — Live streaming STT in chat (IN PROGRESS). Coordinate so the streaming UI doesn't ship pre-shadcn.

## History

Filed 2026-06-06 in response to user direction: migrate the entire frontend to shadcn-svelte first, then do the provider-UX refactor work on top of the new base. Priority deliberately set to P2 — user explicitly said "right now it's not super important".
notes: Plan deliverable ready for user review at docs/shadcn-svelte-migration-plan.md (1,103 lines, 11 phases, big-bang cutover, 10 risks + mitigations, 13 open questions). NO production code written — bead description mandates 'Get the plan approved before exiting plan mode'. Bead deliberately left in_progress; next iteration should NOT redo the inventory. See .ralph-tui/progress.md for handoff details.

title: Provider settings UX: replace embedded per-category 'Add new X provider' dropdowns with a single 'Add provider' button → modal → reusable Add/Edit/Delete pattern (REQUIRES PLAN MODE)
description:
## Symptom — current Add-provider UX is an anti-pattern

Adding a new provider in the current settings UX is structured in a deeply unusual way:

- The page has **separate inline "Add new LLM provider" / "Add new TTS provider" / etc. sections**, each with its own embedded dropdown list of provider kinds, each rendered directly into the page.
- There are multiple parallel dropdown lists scattered across the page (one per provider category) instead of a single normalized entry point.
- There is **no single "Add provider" affordance** that users expect from standard CRUD UX.
- Editing an existing provider is not a click-the-row-it-opens-a-form interaction; there is no consistent edit modal.

User's verbatim frame:

> *"yes now it supports adding multiple providers, but this is stupidly stupid... There's a super anti-pattern of user experience... Why the fuck we configure some providers and then we have 'add a new LLM provider' with the stupidest list with providers — why can't we just have a button 'add provider', we click on that, we use just the regular select, we select the provider which we want to add (Anthropic or Google Gemini, whatever we need), then it shows all the fields that we need to fill up, we put the name and click save. And then we reuse this modal to edit the provider — we just click on the provider, it opens the modal and we can edit. Or we can delete. What the fuck is wrong... Why don't it use the past and the popular user experience practices."*

The user is asking, with reason: this is a solved problem in standard UX. Why was it reinvented poorly?

## Expected UX — standard CRUD modal pattern

One **"+ Add provider" button** at the top of the provider settings surface (regardless of LLM / TTS / STT category — the modal handles the category choice).

Clicking it opens a **single modal** with this flow:

1. **Step 1 — pick the provider kind.** A single `<select>` (or equivalent dropdown / combobox / searchable list) listing every available provider: Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, openai-compatible, Piper, ElevenLabs (TTS), Deepgram (STT), faster-whisper, Parakeet, OpenAI Realtime, etc. Optionally grouped by category (LLM / TTS / STT) in the dropdown.
2. **Step 2 — fill in the fields.** Once a kind is selected, the modal renders the fields required for that kind (display name, API key, base URL, model, voice, language, etc. — exact fields driven by the provider's schema).
3. **Step 3 — name and save.** User gives the instance a display name (e.g. "Ollama — Qwen 35B") and clicks Save. Modal closes, the new instance appears in the list.

The **same modal is reused for Edit and Delete**:

- Clicking an existing provider row opens the modal pre-filled with the instance's current values.
- The user can edit any field and click Save → updates the row.
- The modal has a Delete button (with a small confirmation) that removes the instance.

The provider list view becomes a plain table / list of instances: name, kind, key fields, edit affordance (row click), no inline add controls.

## 🚨 PLAN MODE IS MANDATORY 🚨

Same rule as [[Johnny-stt.5]]: do not start coding. The previous provider-UX implementation was shipped without planning and produced the current anti-pattern. The fix must not repeat that mistake.

Before writing any production code on this ticket, the assignee MUST:

1. Read the current provider-settings UI — every per-category "Add new X provider" section, every embedded dropdown, every save handler. Document each in the ticket notes.
2. Read the existing modal / dialog component library in the frontend — is there a shared modal component? Is there an existing form abstraction (e.g. a JSON-schema-driven form)? If yes, reuse it. If no, document the decision to add one.
3. Read the provider plugin schemas (`backend/app/providers/schema.py` and individual provider definitions) — confirm the per-kind field set is discoverable so the modal can render fields dynamically.
4. **Enter plan mode** (`EnterPlanMode` / `/plan`) and produce a concrete plan covering:
   - The modal's component tree (header, body, footer, fields area, save/delete buttons).
   - The kind-picker dropdown contents and grouping.
   - How the fields area swaps when a different kind is selected.
   - The save / edit / delete handler wiring to the existing backend endpoints (no new backend endpoints unless justified).
   - Migration of the current scattered inline add UI into the new pattern — what gets deleted, what gets added.
   - The chrome-devtools MCP validation steps.
5. Get the plan approved before exiting plan mode.

A PR shipping without evidence of a plan-mode pass will be rejected.

## Coordination with related tickets

This ticket overlaps heavily with [[Johnny-stt.5]] (full LLM+TTS+STT provider-UX refactor) and [[Johnny-stt.7]] (multi-instance regression fix). The cleanest path is for one assignee to fold all three into a single coordinated effort:

- Johnny-stt.5: unifies LLM + TTS + STT into one settings surface
- Johnny-stt.7: makes multi-instance-per-kind actually work end-to-end
- Johnny-stt.8 (this one): defines the Add/Edit/Delete modal pattern that lives inside that surface

If a single PR addresses all three, close the other two as superseded. If they ship separately, the assignees must coordinate so the final surface is consistent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A single **"+ Add provider"** button is present at the top of the provider settings surface (no per-category embedded add controls).
- [ ] Clicking the button opens a modal with a single provider-kind dropdown listing every available provider, optionally grouped by category.
- [ ] Selecting a kind dynamically renders the fields required for that kind (driven by the provider's schema — no per-kind hardcoded form file).
- [ ] The modal has a display-name field, a Save button, and (in edit mode) a Delete button.
- [ ] Clicking an existing provider row in the list opens the **same modal** pre-filled with that instance's values.
- [ ] Editing → Save updates the instance in place.
- [ ] Delete → confirm → removes the instance.
- [ ] The previous scattered per-category "Add new X provider" sections, embedded dropdowns, and inline add controls are **removed**. No dead code.
- [ ] The modal works correctly for at least one provider in each category: Anthropic (LLM), Ollama (LLM), Piper (TTS), ElevenLabs (TTS), faster-whisper (STT), Parakeet (STT), Deepgram (STT).
- [ ] Multi-instance per kind still works (regression check on Johnny-stt.7): adding a second Ollama instance via the modal succeeds.
- [ ] No regressions on existing configured providers — they keep working after the refactor.

## Validation — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

1. `navigate_page` → provider settings.
2. `take_snapshot` — assert exactly one "+ Add provider" button. Assert no inline per-category add dropdowns.
3. `click` the "+ Add provider" button → assert a modal opens.
4. `take_snapshot` of the modal — assert the kind dropdown exists with the expected options.
5. Select "Anthropic" → assert API key field appears.
6. Select "Ollama" → assert base URL + model fields appear (different shape from Anthropic).
7. Fill in valid Ollama config, save → assert modal closes, row appears in the list.
8. Add a second Ollama instance with a different model → assert it saves (Johnny-stt.7 regression check).
9. `click` an existing row → assert the modal reopens pre-filled with that row's values.
10. Edit a field, save → assert the row updates.
11. Click Delete in the modal → confirm → assert the row disappears.
12. Repeat steps 4–11 for at least one TTS provider and one STT provider.
13. `take_screenshot` of: empty state, add-modal (kind selected), edit-modal pre-filled, list with multiple instances.
14. `list_console_messages` — assert no warnings.
15. `list_network_requests` — assert clean 2xx on each save / delete; no 4xx on stale routes.

## Related

- [[Johnny-stt.5]] — full LLM+TTS+STT provider-UX refactor. This modal pattern is what should land inside that refactor. Coordinate to avoid duplicate work.
- [[Johnny-stt.7]] — multi-instance-per-kind regression. The modal pattern must support this from day one — adding a second Ollama instance through the modal must succeed.
- [[Johnny-stt.2]] — Catalog UI (CLOSED) that introduced the broken add-provider UX. Its component(s) get refactored or deleted as part of this work.

## Priority

**P0 — Highest.** The current UX is functionally usable but is causing repeated user pain and is being called out in nearly every interaction. The longer this sits broken, the more user goodwill is burned. Coordinate with Johnny-stt.5 and .7 to ship a single coherent fix.
close_reason: Superseded by Johnny-fe.10 (comprehensive /providers redesign — single modal for all CRUD + preview-without-save + dynamic model lists + Piper download + rename + delete). The Add/Edit/Delete modal pattern from this ticket is fully absorbed into Johnny-fe.10's scope. No live work tracked here anymore.

title: Provider settings regression: cannot add multiple providers of the same kind (DB allows it, new UI/API blocks it) — Ollama save fails with 'conflicts with another provider with the same kind/name/display'
description:
## Symptom

Trying to save a second provider of the same kind (e.g. a second Ollama LLM provider with a different model) fails with the validation error:

> *conflicts with another provider with the same kind/name/display*

The database row is never persisted. The new provider-settings UX rework (shipped under [[Johnny-stt.2]]) silently changed the contract from **N providers per kind** to **1 provider per kind** — without migrating the DB and without telling users.

User's verbatim frame:

> *"previously we could add the same type of providers multiple times. But now it's limited only to one provider at a time. However, the database wasn't fixed. We still need to be able to add multiple providers, even the same one. For example, I can add multiple OLAMA providers, but I can choose different models just for plane."*

> *"add a new task. Highest priority."*

## What worked before (and must work again)

The previous UX let users add multiple instances of the same provider kind, each with their own display name and config:

- *Ollama (Qwen 35B)* — kind=ollama, base URL=..., model=qwen-35b
- *Ollama (Llama 3 8B)* — kind=ollama, base URL=..., model=llama-3-8b
- *Ollama (some-finetune)* — kind=ollama, base URL=..., model=some-finetune

The user could then pick any of these per session / event / playground action.

The same applies to every other provider kind: multiple OpenAI keys for different orgs/projects, multiple Anthropic, multiple Piper TTS voices grouped as instances, multiple ElevenLabs with different default voices, multiple Deepgram with different language defaults, etc.

## Current broken behaviour

- Add an Ollama provider (instance A). Save: ✅.
- Add a second Ollama provider with a different model (instance B). Save: ❌ `conflicts with another provider with the same kind/name/display`.
- The DB schema still allows multiple rows — only the API / save-validation layer blocks it.
- Net effect: users with multi-instance setups can no longer configure their app. Nothing works properly until this is fixed.

## Root cause (user's hypothesis)

> *"exactly the missed interface opportunity and skipping the logic of multiple providers"*

The new provider UX appears to enforce a uniqueness check at the API / validation layer on `(kind, name, display)` — but the underlying DB has no such constraint (and shouldn't). So the UX is **inconsistent with the schema**, and the UI was never built to model "N instances per kind" in the first place.

## Fix shape (investigation, not prescription)

The assignee will need to:

1. Find the save-validation rule that emits the *"conflicts with another provider with the same kind/name/display"* error. Remove or correct the bogus uniqueness check.
2. Confirm the DB schema allows multiple rows per kind (per user, it already does — verify).
3. Rework the provider-settings UI to model **provider instances** (each with its own ID, display name, and config) rather than **one config per kind**:
   - List view shows each instance as a row with name/display + kind label + edit/remove.
   - Add button creates a new instance, not "edit the existing kind".
   - Each kind can have arbitrarily many instances.
4. Every UX surface that picks a provider (session start, event config, playground, voice picker, model picker, etc.) must reference an **instance ID**, not a kind. Audit and update each call site.
5. Migrate any existing single-instance config rows so they show up as named instances in the new model (don't lose user data).

This overlaps heavily with [[Johnny-stt.5]] (the unified provider-UX refactor). The work should not be duplicated — either:
- This fix lands first (urgent), and Johnny-stt.5 builds on it; OR
- Johnny-stt.5 folds this scope in and we close this ticket as superseded.

The assignee should coordinate with whoever is working on Johnny-stt.5 before starting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User can add **multiple Ollama providers**, each with a distinct display name and a distinct model — both save successfully, both appear in the list.
- [ ] Same for **OpenAI, Anthropic, Piper, ElevenLabs, Deepgram, OpenAI Realtime, faster-whisper** — any provider kind, multiple instances allowed.
- [ ] The provider settings UI lists every instance separately with its own display name, kind label, edit, and remove affordances.
- [ ] The *"conflicts with another provider with the same kind/name/display"* error never fires for a legitimate new instance.
- [ ] Session / event / playground UX selects providers by **instance ID**, not by kind. Two Ollama instances can be picked independently for two different sessions.
- [ ] Existing single-instance user configs are migrated cleanly to the instance model — no user data lost.
- [ ] Regression test in `backend/tests/` covers: create 2 instances of the same kind, save both, list both, select each independently. Test fails today; passes after fix.
- [ ] No regression on the single-instance happy path (a user who only ever has one provider of a kind still works fine).

## Validation — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

1. `navigate_page` → provider settings (wherever the unified UX lives — see Johnny-stt.5 for the refactor target).
2. `take_snapshot`.
3. Add Ollama instance A (display: "Ollama Qwen 35B", model: qwen-35b). Save — assert success, assert it appears in the list.
4. Add Ollama instance B (display: "Ollama Llama 3 8B", model: llama-3-8b). Save — assert success (no "conflicts" error), assert both instances now in the list.
5. `list_console_messages` and `list_network_requests` — assert no 4xx/5xx on either save.
6. Open the playground, `take_snapshot` of the provider picker — assert both Ollama instances selectable independently.
7. Send a message picking instance A, assert qwen-35b responds. Repeat with instance B, assert llama-3-8b responds.
8. `take_screenshot` of: settings list with both instances visible, playground picker showing both, response from each.

## Related

- [[Johnny-stt.5]] — major refactor of unified provider-settings UX (LLM + TTS + STT). This ticket is one specific symptom that .5 addresses. Coordinate to avoid duplicate work; if .5 ships first, this can close as superseded.
- [[Johnny-stt.2]] — Catalog UI (CLOSED) that introduced the regression by modelling "one config per kind".
- Any existing per-session-provider picker code that references a provider by `kind` rather than `instance_id` is in scope to audit.

## Priority

**P0 — Highest.** User explicitly flagged this as highest priority because the app is functionally unusable for any setup with multiple providers of the same kind, which is the common case (multiple Ollama models, multiple OpenAI keys, multiple Piper voices grouped as instances, etc.).

title: Refactor and unify ALL provider settings UX (LLM + TTS + STT) into one cohesive provider page — explore existing code FIRST, integrate everything, REQUIRES PLAN MODE
description:
## Symptom — current state of provider settings is fragmented

The provider-settings UX in this app is incoherent:

- **STT catalog page** (shipped under [[Johnny-stt.2]]) was added as a **standalone page** that is **not reachable from the main menu / navigation** and does not share visual or interaction patterns with the rest of the app.
- **LLM provider settings** live somewhere else, with their own UX (TBD by code exploration — the assignee will map this).
- **TTS provider settings** live somewhere else again, with yet another UX (TBD by code exploration).

User's verbatim frame:

> *"this kind of like user experience and user interface that was added is absurdly stupid because we can't even open this page to our menu or UI"*

> *"we had this UI catalogue for providers but it ... is not being integrated with the functionality that we had. We had special tab provider but for some reason ... everything like should be unified"*

> *"create a super huge refactor and rework of the provider's page including all our LLM TTS and STT things"*

> *"Everything inside of that epic"* — the refactor must cover everything in the Johnny-stt epic, alongside the existing LLM + TTS provider surfaces.

## Expected end state

**One unified Provider Settings surface in the app**, with:

1. A **single entry** in the main menu / app navigation (e.g. "Settings → Providers" — exact naming determined during plan).
2. **LLM, TTS, and STT each live as a tab (or sibling section)** inside that one surface — no separate isolated pages for any of them.
3. **Shared visual + interaction patterns** across all three tabs: same shell, same form layout, same save / reset behaviour, same Test-button pattern, same error/empty/loading states.
4. **Reachable in ≤ 2 clicks** from app entry. Zero URL typing.
5. **No bespoke standalone provider-config pages remain** anywhere in the app.
6. **No regressions** on any existing LLM, TTS, or STT functionality.

## 🚨 MANDATORY: codebase exploration + plan mode BEFORE coding 🚨

This ticket exists because the previous attempt ([[Johnny-stt.2]]) shipped without planning and produced a disconnected page. That will not happen again.

The assignee **must** complete the following BEFORE writing any production code:

### Phase 1 — codebase exploration
1. Find and read **every** provider-settings UI currently in the codebase:
   - LLM provider settings — files, components, routes, menu glue.
   - TTS provider settings — files, components, routes, menu glue.
   - STT catalog page (just shipped under Johnny-stt.2) — files, components, route, lack-of-menu-glue.
2. Identify shared / duplicated / divergent patterns across the three:
   - Form components — shared or per-feature?
   - Save / reset / Test buttons — shared or per-feature?
   - API-key fields, language pickers, model dropdowns — shared or per-feature?
   - Persistence layer — same backend endpoint pattern, or different?
3. Identify the main menu / navigation file(s) and where provider-settings entries live (or don't).
4. Document findings inline in this ticket's `--notes`.

### Phase 2 — plan mode
5. **Enter plan mode** (`EnterPlanMode` / `/plan`) and produce a concrete plan that covers:
   - The unified component tree (which shell, which tabs, which shared sub-components).
   - File-level migration: which files get added, which get edited, which get **deleted** (the standalone STT page from .2 should go away; duplicated form components should be consolidated).
   - Menu / navigation change: where the single Provider Settings entry lives and what label it carries.
   - Persistence-layer change (if any): unified config API vs. per-category endpoints.
   - The chrome-devtools MCP validation steps for the final UX.
   - Explicit list of regressions to verify against (existing LLM / TTS provider flows must keep working).
6. **Get the plan approved before exiting plan mode.**

### Phase 3 — implement
7. Only after sign-off, implement and validate.

A PR that lacks evidence of phases 1 + 2 (exploration findings in `--notes`, an approved plan) will be rejected.

## Scope

This is a **major refactor**, not a small add-on. Touches:
- LLM provider settings UI (refactor to fit the unified shell).
- TTS provider settings UI (refactor to fit the unified shell).
- STT catalog UI (move from standalone page to a tab inside the unified shell — the page shipped under Johnny-stt.2 gets deleted as part of this).
- Main menu / app navigation (single entry).
- Any shared form / field / button / state components needed to make the three tabs visually + interactionally consistent.
- Backend persistence layer (if needed to unify per-category save endpoints).

## Out of scope

- Adding **new** providers (that's Johnny-stt.4 and any future provider tickets).
- Changing provider **plugin** code under `backend/app/providers/` — only the UI / settings layer.
- Streaming-input UX in the chat (that's Johnny-stt.3).
- Replacing the playground or any non-settings surface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Single menu entry** for Provider Settings in the main navigation, reachable from app entry in ≤ 2 clicks.
- [ ] **Unified Provider Settings page** with LLM, TTS, STT each as a tab (or sibling section) inside it. No separate pages remain.
- [ ] **Visual + interaction consistency** across all three tabs: form shell, save/reset, Test button, error/empty/loading states all match.
- [ ] The standalone STT catalog page from Johnny-stt.2 (route + component) is **deleted**, not just hidden.
- [ ] Existing LLM provider flows still work end-to-end (regression: pick provider, edit config, save, test → unchanged behaviour).
- [ ] Existing TTS provider flows still work end-to-end (same regression check).
- [ ] STT provider flows (including the Johnny-stt.2 Test button) work inside the new unified tab.
- [ ] No dead code: orphaned components, unreferenced routes, duplicated form widgets are removed.
- [ ] Exploration findings + approved plan are documented in this ticket before any production code lands.

## Validation — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

1. `navigate_page` → app root.

title: Live streaming STT in playground chat input (mic icon + partial transcripts as user speaks)
description:
## Why
User wants to see the speech-recognition output appear instantly in the chat as they speak — explicitly asked to keep this as a separate ticket from the Parakeet integration.

## Scope
- Mic icon in the playground chat input.
- While held (or toggled), audio streams from browser → backend WebSocket → selected streaming-capable STT provider.
- Partial transcripts render in-place in the chat input as the user speaks.
- On stop/release, the final transcript becomes the message body and is sendable.
- Provider switch lives in the catalog (Johnny-stt.2). Default: Parakeet local (Johnny-stt.1). Fallback: Deepgram / AssemblyAI / ElevenLabs streaming.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Mic toggle visible in the playground chat input.
- [ ] First partial transcript visible ≤ 500ms after start of speech (Parakeet local target; cloud providers may be higher).
- [ ] Partials update at ≥ 2 Hz.
- [ ] On stop, the final transcript replaces partials and the message becomes sendable.
- [ ] Changing the selected STT provider in the catalog changes the streaming source on the next session.
- [ ] Mic-permission denial shows a usable error, not a silent failure.

## Validation
- Backend: WebSocket frame test with synthetic PCM stream and an assertion that partials are emitted ≥ N times.
- Frontend: component test for the mic toggle state machine.
- **Browser (chrome-devtools MCP):** navigate to /playground → grant mic → press mic button → assert `[data-partial-transcript]` updates ≥ 3 times → release → assert chat input contains final transcript → screenshot for PR.

## Depends on
- Johnny-stt.1 (Parakeet, default streaming provider)
- Johnny-stt.2 (catalog UI exposes the provider switch)

title: Add disable thinking/reasoning checkbox to LLM provider configs
description: Add a CHECKBOX field to all four LLM provider schemas (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible) allowing users to disable thinking/reasoning at request time. Wire each provider's chat() request body to honor the flag with the correct per-vendor mechanism: Anthropic thinking type=disabled, Gemini thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget=0, OpenAI reasoning_effort=minimal, Ollama think=false + /no_think system prefix. Also add any other commonly useful tuning parameters (top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty) where applicable.
notes: Implemented disable_thinking checkbox + universal tuning knobs (top_p, top_k, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, seed) on all 4 LLM providers. Per-provider wire format: Anthropic — no-op (extended thinking is opt-in and not enabled by adapter today); Gemini — generationConfig.thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget=0; OpenAI — reasoning_effort=minimal for o-series/gpt-5; OpenAI-compatible (Ollama/vLLM) — body['think']=false + chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false + /no_think system prefix. Adapter now sends all three Qwen mechanisms in parallel so vLLM-Qwen3.6 hosts get the right knob. Known limitation: Ollama uncensored Qwen3.6 remixes with bare {{ .Prompt }} chat template ignore ALL three mechanisms — user must install a Modelfile with proper Qwen3 thinking-control template or switch model. Documented in help_text. 258 provider tests pass.

Adapter now sends think:false + chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking:false + /no_think for Ollama/vLLM compatibility. Help text warns about bare-template Qwen3.6 remixes that ignore all three. title: Profile + tune end-to-end voice latency on real local STT/TTS/LLM, and add in-UI optimization tips on each provider settings page
description:
## Why this exists

Even when Local Piper is working, time-to-first-audio feels long. The user explicitly wants to (a) measure where the time goes on real models, (b) actually adjust settings to reduce it, and (c) capture the resulting know-how directly inside the provider settings UI so the next person tuning a model is not flying blind.

Sibling task [[per-session-activity-timing-log-surfaced-in-chat-history-per-turn-pipeline-events-with-durations]] (Johnny-ckz.7) ships the activity-log surface that this work feeds and that this work also exercises as its own measurement instrument.

## Constraints

- **Real models only.** No mocks. Use the providers exported in /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json (seed via JOHNNY_PROVIDERS_FILE per Johnny-d3e / Johnny-k3z).
- Cover Local Piper TTS, Local Whisper STT, and at least one local LLM (the JSON should have one configured; if not, document the gap and proceed with what is configured).
- Profile the **full path the user feels**: VAD-detected user-speech-end → first audible byte out. Not just synthesis time.

## Investigation deliverables

1. **Latency map** per provider on real models: VAD end → STT first-partial → STT final → LLM first-token → LLM total → TTS first-byte → first audio chunk delivered to the transport. Capture p50 + p95 from at least 20 turns of varied length.
2. **Bottleneck attribution** with evidence (logs / traces / activity-log entries from Johnny-ckz.7).
3. **Concrete optimizations applied** to the codebase / configs, not just recommendations. Likely candidates:
   - Persistent piper process per voice (vs spawn-per-utterance) — the docstring on backend/app/providers/piper_tts.py already names this.
   - Piper HTTP server variant if process-keep-alive isn't enough.
   - Verify the audio bridge to Meet / WebRTC actually forwards chunks as they arrive (suspect: buffers until end-of-utterance).
   - Tune chunk_bytes, native_sample_rate defaults if profiling shows mis-set values.
   - Whisper: model size vs latency trade-off; check whether faster-whisper is using GPU when available, CPU thread count, beam size.
   - Local LLM: context window trimming, prompt-cache reuse, lower-latency decode params.
4. **Documented target**: time-to-first-audio target on file (proposed: 300 ms p50 / 500 ms p95 for local stack); state whether the optimizations hit it, and if not, what would.

## In-UI optimization tips on every provider settings page (mandatory, not optional)

The provider settings window is where a user actually changes these knobs. After profiling, surface what was learned directly in that UI:

- A help section on each provider's settings card explaining what each option does and how it affects latency / quality / cost. Plain language, with rules of thumb (e.g. 'medium voices are ~2× slower than low voices but noticeably more natural; on CPU expect ~XX ms time-to-first-audio with default settings').
- Specifically for Local Piper: explain voice-tier trade-off (low / medium / high), native_sample_rate (which voices output 16k vs 22k), chunk_bytes, and call out the persistent-process optimization if it ships.
- Specifically for Local Whisper: explain model-size trade-off (tiny / base / small / medium), CPU vs GPU, beam size, real measured latencies on the test machine.
- Specifically for Local LLM(s): context window, decode settings, expected first-token latency.
- A small 'Measured on this machine' block per provider showing the most recent profile numbers (if cheap; otherwise just the static guidance).
- Each settings page should also link to the relevant section of any docs that this task produces.

Content style: short, useful, no marketing fluff. Imagine the reader is the operator at 11pm trying to make the bot snappier before tomorrow's demo.

## Out of scope

- The activity-log UI itself (Johnny-ckz.7).
- Cloud TTS / LLM provider tuning (separate ticket if interesting later).
- Aggregating latency analytics across many sessions (dashboard).
- Hyper-optimizations behind feature flags / experiments framework.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A written latency map of the local stack is on file with p50 / p95 numbers from ≥20 turns using real models seeded from /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json.
2. The dominant bottleneck is identified with evidence.
3. At least one concrete optimization is implemented and re-measured; before/after numbers are on file.
4. Each provider's settings page in the UI has a help / tips section explaining its options and their latency/quality trade-offs, including measured rules-of-thumb from this work.
5. The 'Measured on this machine' block (if shipped) reflects the latest profile numbers.
6. All UI additions (the in-settings help sections) are validated via chrome-devtools MCP per the AGENTS.md top rule, with screenshots in the PR.

## Testing approach — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

- Profile from the playground (Johnny-ckz.6) once it lands, OR a real Meet, using chrome-devtools MCP to capture browser-side timings via performance_start_trace / performance_stop_trace / list_network_requests.
- For every provider settings page that gets a new tips section, drive the UI in chrome-devtools MCP: navigate, snapshot, expand the tips section, screenshot, assert the rules-of-thumb match what was measured.
- Re-measure after each optimization and capture the delta in the PR.

## Related

- [[per-session-activity-timing-log-surfaced-in-chat-history-per-turn-pipeline-events-with-durations]] (Johnny-ckz.7) — sibling; produces the events this work uses as its measurement instrument.
- [[local-piper-follow-up-voice-catalog-fetcher-fails-on-hf-307-redirect-plus-model-dirs-must-move-to-host-bind-mounts]] (Johnny-ckz.5) — must be unblocked before Piper end-to-end profiling can happen.
- [[in-browser-voice-text-chat-with-the-bot-per-event-try-with-bot-button-plus-standalone-playground]] (Johnny-ckz.6) — natural profiling surface.
- [[run-the-two-bot-voice-interrupt-harness-end-to-end-against-real-models-fix-any-bugs-it-surfaces]] (Johnny-ckz.4) — uses the same real-models constraint and credentials JSON.
design: Profile before changing — measure where time actually goes (model load vs subprocess fork vs bridge buffering vs resampling). Per piper_tts.py docstring, the named upgrade path is a persistent piper process (or Piper HTTP server) fronted by an adapter that reuses the long-lived process; evaluate first. For Whisper, check whether faster-whisper is using the CPU thread count and beam size we think it is. Surface findings in the settings UI as a help section per provider, written for the 11pm-before-demo operator audience. Use Johnny-ckz.7's session_timings as the measurement instrument once it lands; until then, instrument ad-hoc.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Latency map with p50/p95 from ≥20 real-model turns on file, seeded from /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json. (2) Dominant bottleneck identified with evidence. (3) At least one optimization implemented and re-measured with before/after numbers. (4) Each provider's settings page in the UI has a help/tips section covering its options and their latency/quality trade-offs, including measured rules-of-thumb. (5) All settings-page UI additions validated via chrome-devtools MCP with screenshots in the PR.

title: Per-session activity / timing log surfaced in chat history (per-turn pipeline events with durations)
description:
## Why this exists

The session detail view today shows transcripts and bot utterances, but nothing about the pipeline that produced them. When a turn feels slow, or the wrong provider was used, or an interrupt arrived but didn't cut, there's no on-page way to see what actually happened. The user asked for a 'super useful' activity log inside the chat history — so an operator can land on a session and immediately see, per turn, the timing and the events.

This task is **the log itself** — capture the events, persist them, render them. Profiling + tuning + in-UI optimization tips live in a separate task (filed alongside this one).

## What to log (per user-turn → bot-reply round-trip)

- User speech start / end (from VAD)
- STT: first-partial latency, final-transcript latency, model / provider used
- Router / LLM: time-to-first-token, total generation time, model used, finish reason, token counts if cheap to get
- TTS: time-to-first-audio-byte, total synth time, voice / provider used, output bytes / duration
- End-to-end: user-speech-end → first-audio-out-to-user (the single number users actually feel)
- Interrupts: when user interrupted, when TTS was cut, latency delta (ties into Johnny-ckz.4)
- Provider switches mid-session (the active provider changed between turns)
- Errors / retries / fallbacks (which provider failed, what we fell back to)

## Persistence

A thin session_timings table is the minimum viable shape — keyed by (session_id, turn_id, event_type, started_at, duration_ms) with a small JSON payload for the per-event detail (e.g. {'model': 'gpt-4o', 'tokens': 312}). If a session-events stream already exists, extend that instead of adding a new table — the investigation under Johnny-ckz.7's sibling profiling task can confirm the cleanest fit; this implementation task should pick one and stick with it.

## UI

A collapsible 'activity' panel per turn in the session detail page (or a single timeline at the top — designer's call), in plain log form with badges per provider. Not a full Gantt chart. Goal: a user scanning a session can see in one glance which turn was slow and which step in that turn was the cost.

Render contract:
- Collapsed by default; expanded shows the per-event list with absolute and relative timings.
- Provider name is visible per row (so 'TTS: 1.4s — Local Piper' is immediately legible).
- Errors are visually distinguished (red badge or icon).
- Works on a session that has only some of the events (older sessions without the new logging just show what they have, no crashes).

## Out of scope

- Optimizing latency (covered by the sibling profiling task).
- Cross-session analytics / dashboards aggregating timing across many sessions.
- Exporting the log to CSV / JSON — additive later if needed.
- Live streaming the log into the UI mid-session — initial version can render after the turn ends; mid-turn streaming is a nice-to-have.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A new session that goes through a full user-turn → bot-reply round-trip produces session_timings rows (or session-events entries) for every applicable event type listed above.
2. The session detail page shows a per-turn activity panel reflecting those events with absolute and relative timings.
3. Provider name is shown per event so it's obvious which TTS / STT / LLM was used.
4. Interrupts (when present) are visible in the panel with their measured latency delta.
5. Sessions that pre-date this change still load with no crashes and no empty-panel error (they just show fewer events).
6. The DB migration is reversible.

## Testing approach — MANDATORY chrome-devtools MCP

Per the AGENTS.md top rule:

- Drive a real session (in the playground from Johnny-ckz.6 if it has shipped, otherwise a real Meet) using the credentials in /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json so the log includes real STT/TTS/LLM events.
- Open the session detail page in chrome-devtools MCP and take a screenshot of the rendered activity panel — collapsed and expanded.
- take_snapshot the per-turn panel and assert (in the test transcript) that every required event type is present and timed.
- Drive an interrupt turn and confirm the interrupt row + its latency delta show up.
- Load an old session (pre-migration) and confirm the panel degrades gracefully.

Unit tests are necessary but not sufficient. The PR description must include the chrome-devtools-MCP screenshots above.

## Related

- [[run-the-two-bot-voice-interrupt-harness-end-to-end-against-real-models-fix-any-bugs-it-surfaces]] (Johnny-ckz.4) — the harness will produce real timing data this log can render.
- [[in-browser-voice-text-chat-with-the-bot-per-event-try-with-bot-button-plus-standalone-playground]] (Johnny-ckz.6) — natural first surface to land the panel on.
design: Thin session_timings table keyed by (session_id, turn_id, event_type, started_at, duration_ms) with a small JSON detail blob; OR extend the existing session-events stream if one is in place. Emit events from the same spots that already log to logger — wrap them in a thin emitter so the writes are cheap. UI: collapsible per-turn panel, log style, badge per provider, red badge for errors. Mid-turn streaming is a nice-to-have; initial version may render after turn-end.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Per-turn session_timings entries are persisted for every applicable event type (STT, LLM, TTS, end-to-end, interrupts, provider switches, errors). (2) Session detail page renders a collapsible per-turn activity panel with absolute + relative timings and visible provider names. (3) Interrupts appear with their latency delta. (4) Pre-migration sessions render with no crashes. (5) DB migration is reversible. (6) Validation includes chrome-devtools-MCP screenshots of collapsed + expanded panel and an interrupt-turn capture, using real models seeded from /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json.

title: ElevenLabs TTS: handle 'exceeds quota' 401 gracefully in the response loop
description:
When ElevenLabs returns 401 with 'exceeds your quota of N, M credits required', the pipeline's _stream_answer_into_tts raises TTSError. The _respond_loop catches it via the broad 'except Exception' guard and logs — the session continues, transcription keeps working — but the user gets silence with no surface indication that TTS broke.

Found during the Johnny-ckz.4 real-provider harness work: the configured ElevenLabs key in /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json had ~2 credits remaining and every harness invocation tripped this.

What we should do:
- Emit a structured event when TTS fails (e.g. AgentTTSFailed with provider name + reason).
- Surface in the session UI so the user can see 'TTS provider out of credits' rather than 'bot just stopped speaking'.
- Probably: add a circuit breaker so we don't keep hammering a broken provider for the whole session.

Reproduction: configure ElevenLabs with an out-of-credits key, ask the bot to speak. Bot will fail silently.

Found by: Johnny-ckz.4 real-provider harness work.

title: Interrupt harness real-mode: clarification assertion shape doesn't match real behavior
description:
The Johnny-ckz.4 real-provider harness for clarification_redirects_long_answer expects TWO AgentSpoke events: the cut original answer + the follow-up. In real mode, the cut original answer publishes NO AgentSpoke because _answer_and_speak's 'if not text or not collected: return False' fires when the interrupt cuts in before any sentence has flushed to TTS. Only the follow-up answer (real bot saying 'Regarding the launch date, we are currently targeting...') emits AgentSpoke.

Observed (from artifacts/2026-06-06T11-40-53Z-interrupt/report.json):
- fast_barge_in_count=1 (interrupt fired correctly).
- transcripts_persisted=['Give me a summary...', 'Wait. What about the launch date?'] (real STT works).
- utterances_persisted=[{'output_text': 'Regarding the launch date, we are currently targeting...'}] (FOLLOW-UP answer was generated and persisted).
- agent_spoke_durations_ms=[17658] (one event, the follow-up).
- played_frame_count=208 — more audio than the follow-up alone (~9s of CUT answer also played).

Two possible fixes:
- Update real-mode assertions: 'success' is fast_barge_in_count>0 AND a follow-up utterance whose text mentions the new question keyword ('launch').
- Or: change _answer_and_speak to emit AgentSpoke even for cut answers with at least N played frames so the cut path stays observable.

Probably both — the second is the real fix (observability) and the first makes the assertion sensible.

Reproduction: uv run python -m johnny.e2e.interrupt --real --providers-file /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json --fallback-tts-openai --only clarification_redirects_long_answer

title: Interrupt harness real-mode: stop scenario flakes when LLM round-trip is slow
description:
The Johnny-ckz.4 real-provider harness for stop_interrupts_long_answer is flaky: 1-in-3 runs the bot fails to produce ANY AgentSpoke because the user starts saying 'stop please' before the answer LLM has streamed enough text to produce a first TTS frame. When this happens, the assertion 'first_agent_spoke_truncated' fails with 'no AgentSpoke published'.

Root cause: The scenario waits 8 s after the 'tell me about yourself' prompt before the 'stop please' interrupt. On slow LLM days (OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini occasionally takes 2.5-3 s to first token), the bot has not yet produced any audio when the interrupt fires.

Options:
- Bump REAL_MODE_EXTRA_SILENCE_MS to 10000+ (longer wait, slower test).
- Or: switch the bot to a faster LLM for the harness (e.g. gpt-4o-mini).
- Or: change the assertion to accept 'fast_barge_in_count > 0 AND no AgentSpoke' as a valid pass for the stop scenario.

Reproduction: uv run python -m johnny.e2e.interrupt --real --providers-file /Users/nikita/Downloads/johnny-providers-2026-06-06.json --fallback-tts-openai --only stop_interrupts_long_answer

title: LLM providers: fetch model list dynamically from each provider's API instead of hardcoding
description:
Currently the model picker for LLM providers shows only a hardcoded short list (e.g. OpenAI shows 'GPT-4.1' and a couple more, not the full lineup). Users can't pick newer / less-common models without editing config.

Wanted: every LLM provider's model dropdown fetches the actual available models live from the provider's API, so the list stays current as providers ship new models.

Coverage needed (at minimum):
- OpenAI — GET /v1/models with the configured API key
- Anthropic — GET /v1/models
- Google (Gemini) — equivalent list endpoint
- Ollama — GET /api/tags against the configured base URL (this is local, so the list IS literally whatever models the user has pulled)
- Any other LLM provider already registered in backend/app/providers

Behavior:
- Fetch on demand when the user opens the provider config (or on a refresh button); cache briefly so we don't hammer the API.
- If credentials are missing/invalid, surface a clear 'enter API key to load models' message instead of falling back to the stale hardcoded list.
- Ollama in particular should ALWAYS fetch fresh — it reflects what's on disk and there is no static list to fall back to.

Out of scope: STT and TTS providers (those have separate model/voice taxonomies; see the Piper UX issue for the local-TTS analogue).
acceptance_criteria: Opening an LLM provider's config in the UI shows a model dropdown populated from the provider's live /models endpoint (or /api/tags for Ollama). New models the provider ships are visible without code changes. With no credentials, the UI shows a clear prompt to enter the key rather than a stale fallback list.

title: ElevenLabs e2e plan uses library voice incompatible with free tier
description:
## Why this exists

The e2e provider harness uses the Rachel voice id `21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM` for the ElevenLabs TTS plan. Library voices require a paid subscription — on a free-tier key (current `.env`) the smoke test fails with HTTP 402 "Free users cannot use library voices via the API".

Johnny-jrd closed the API-key question (key is valid). This is the next layer: the plan voice itself is paywalled.

## Fix options
- Switch the e2e plan to a non-library voice id (e.g. a user-cloned voice that the free tier can call), OR
- Have preflight probe `/v2/voices/{voice_id}` and SKIP with "voice requires paid plan" when the API returns 402 there.

## Acceptance
- `tts-elevenlabs` plan PASSes against the current `.env` ElevenLabs key, OR SKIPs with a clear hint pointing at the free-tier limitation.

title: Bot carries the whole meeting's context (not a 6-turn rolling window) when routing and answering
description:
## Why this exists

Today the voice pipeline at \`backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/pipeline.py\` keeps the last **6** transcripts in memory and nothing else (\`DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_WINDOW_SIZE = 6\`, line 69; rolling delete at line 850-851; window assembly at line 853-874). Older parts of the meeting fall out of the prompt entirely.

The static \`config.context\` field on a \`MeetingConfig\` exists (line 130, used at lines 740 and 789) but only carries pre-meeting context the user typed in by hand. Nothing accumulates *during* the meeting.

Effect: ten minutes into a meeting, the bot has forgotten the first nine minutes. Ask "what did we decide about the staging deploy earlier?" and it has no idea. That defeats most of the value of a long-form meeting bot.

## What "whole context" means here

Three layers, all needed:

1. **Pre-meeting context** — already there (\`config.context\`), but should also pull from the Google Calendar event's description / attachments / linked docs if available.
2. **In-meeting accumulation** — every finalised transcript from this session, in order, available to both router and answer LLMs, not capped at 6.
3. **Cross-session continuity (optional, smaller scope)** — if the same calendar event recurs (same recurring_event_id), surface the most recent prior session's summary as additional context. File a follow-up bead if too much; can be deferred.

## What to build

### Storage is already there

\`transcript_chunks\` (\`backend/app/db/models.py\` and the persistence layer in \`app/services/transcripts.py\`) already persists every finalised STT chunk per session — that's the source of truth. The pipeline just doesn't read from it; it works from its in-memory window.

### Pipeline changes

- Drop the \`DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_WINDOW_SIZE = 6\` cap as the default. Replace with an unbounded list per session, capped by **token budget** instead of turn count.
- Make \`_build_input_window\` (line 853) emit the **full** session transcript when within budget, otherwise apply a rolling summarisation step: oldest N transcripts get collapsed into a short summary line ("Earlier: …"), recent transcripts kept verbatim.
- Token budget knobs configurable per provider (different LLMs have different windows). Default safe: 75 % of the provider's max context, reserving the rest for the answer.
- Summarisation can be a lightweight call to the same router/answer LLM with a "summarise the following meeting transcript in <= N sentences" prompt; cache the summary against the session so it's not recomputed every turn.

### Crash / resume

- On worker (re)start mid-session — e.g. container respawn — rehydrate \`_transcript_history\` from \`transcript_chunks WHERE session_id = ?\` so the bot doesn't reset to zero context.

### Calendar context

- Read the calendar event's \`description\` (already fetched per \`app/services/calendar_polling.py\`) and append it to the pipeline's system prompt as additional context, distinct from the user-typed \`config.context\` so both are visible to the LLM and persisted separately for audit.
- If the event has attached Google Docs / Sheets URLs in the description, **out of scope** for this bead — list as a follow-up.

### Persistence / audit

- The system prompt the LLM sees per turn (with full or summarised context) should be persisted on \`agent_decisions\` (or alongside it) so audits can reproduce why the bot answered the way it did. Today the snapshot in \`_build_input_window\` (line 858-873) captures \`transcript_window\` and \`instructions\` / \`context\` — extend with the summarised-history snapshot when summarisation kicks in.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In a 30+ minute session, asking the bot a question about something said in the first 5 minutes produces an answer that references that earlier context (not a "I don't know").
- [ ] No 6-turn cap on transcript history — capped by token budget instead.
- [ ] When over the token budget, oldest transcripts are summarised; the summary is cached per session and reused across turns.
- [ ] Pre-meeting context = \`config.context\` + calendar event description, both visible in the system prompt and persisted for audit.
- [ ] On worker container restart mid-session, the next turn picks up the full prior transcript from \`transcript_chunks\` (no context reset).
- [ ] The \`_build_input_window\` snapshot stored per decision includes whatever the LLM actually saw (full or summarised) so audits are reproducible.
- [ ] Token-budget knob is configurable per LLM provider; defaults to 75 % of the provider's max context.
- [ ] Tests cover: full session under budget, session over budget triggering summarisation, mid-session restart rehydration, calendar description merged into context.
- [ ] Quality gates pass: \`uv run pytest\`, \`uv run ruff check\`, \`uv run mypy\`, \`pnpm typecheck\`, \`pnpm lint\`.

## Out of scope

- Cross-session continuity for recurring events (file a follow-up under \`Johnny-ckz\` if you want it).
- Reading attached Google Docs / Sheets URLs from the event description (separate bead).
- Vector-search retrieval over transcripts (already a separate workstream — \`agent_decisions\` and \`transcript_chunks\` have embeddings via \`compute_pending_embeddings\`; this bead is about *in-session* context, not retrieval).
- Per-speaker memory / who-said-what diarisation upgrades.

## Notes

The current 6-turn cap was a scaffolding default, not a designed limit — \`config.transcript_window_size\` is already configurable. This bead is the natural next step: lift the cap, switch to token-budgeted, and persist what the LLM actually saw.

## Related

- \`Johnny-ckz\` — parent epic (join-stuck fix + e2e harness). This bead reinforces the value the harness needs to prove.
- \`Johnny-ckz.2\` — Autonomous mode. Autonomous benefits most from full context since it has no per-utterance approval gate.
- \`Johnny-pdf\` — master e2e validation. When this lands, \`Johnny-pdf\` Phase 5/6/7 scripts should include a question that requires context from earlier in the same session, otherwise the test never exercises this.
- \`Johnny-kgc.33\` — US-033: Transcript and audit persistence. The data layer this bead reads from.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline no longer caps transcript history at 6 turns; carries the full session transcript within a configurable token budget, summarising older content when over budget; merges calendar event description into pre-meeting context; rehydrates from transcript_chunks on worker restart; persists whatever the LLM actually saw per decision; tests cover under-budget, over-budget, restart, calendar merge; quality gates pass.
notes: Spawned 2026-06-06 from user request — explicitly wants the bot to hold the whole meeting's context. Lives under Johnny-ckz alongside Johnny-ckz.2 (Autonomous mode), which benefits most from real context.

title: Add 'Autonomous' mode: bot speaks freely per profile instructions, no whitelist, no approval gate
description:
## Why this exists

Today \`BotMode\` (\`backend/app/db/models.py:51-55\`) ships four values:

1. \`listen_only\` — STT only, bot never speaks.
2. \`suggest_only\` — pipeline runs, decisions logged, bot stays silent.
3. \`approval_required\` — pipeline proposes a reply, user must Approve/Reject in the UI before it speaks.
4. \`limited_auto_speak\` — bot speaks, but only verbatim from the profile template's \`allowed_replies\` whitelist (currently required for this mode at \`app/api/templates.py:52\` and \`app/api/meeting_configs.py:138\`).

There's no mode for "let Johnny act on its own, guided only by the profile template's instructions and context". The user wants exactly that: free-form generation, no approval round-trip, no allowed-reply whitelist — the bot self-governs against the profile instructions.

This is the natural fifth mode that the existing scaffolding was clearly designed to support but never delivered.

## What to build

### New enum value

- Add \`AUTONOMOUS = "autonomous"\` to \`BotMode\` in \`backend/app/db/models.py\`. Naming options considered: \`AUTO_SPEAK\` (parallel with \`LIMITED_AUTO_SPEAK\`), \`FREE_SPEAK\`, \`AUTONOMOUS\`, \`UNRESTRICTED\`. Recommendation: \`AUTONOMOUS\` — communicates the *intent* (operates on its own per instructions) rather than the surface behaviour. UI label: "Autonomous".
- Alembic migration in \`backend/alembic/versions/\` extending the PG enum type. Pattern to follow: \`0003_decision_outcome_suggested.py\` already adds a value to an enum and is the template to copy.

### Validation rules

- \`allowed_replies\` requirement at \`app/api/templates.py:52\` and \`app/api/meeting_configs.py:138\` is currently \`if mode is BotMode.LIMITED_AUTO_SPEAK\` — leave it as-is. For \`AUTONOMOUS\`, \`allowed_replies\` must be **empty or ignored** (the whole point is no whitelist).
- Profile template instructions and context **must be non-empty** for \`AUTONOMOUS\` — they are the only governance. Add a parallel validation that rejects an autonomous-mode template/meeting_config with blank instructions.

### Pipeline behaviour

- Reuse the existing router → answer → TTS path (same as approval/limited_auto_speak).
- Skip the approval gate entirely (no \`agent_decisions.status = pending\`, no browser push, no countdown).
- No whitelist match against \`allowed_replies\` — the answer LLM's free-form output goes straight to TTS.
- Decisions are still persisted to \`agent_decisions\` with \`outcome = spoken\` (or \`suppressed\` if the router declines, e.g. low confidence / non-question) so the audit trail stays intact.
- Honour the same per-session rate limit knobs the limited mode uses (cost + talking-over-others control), but default the cap a bit lower for autonomous since each utterance is free-form and longer. Make the cap overrideable per meeting_config.

### Frontend

- Add the new mode to \`frontend/src/lib/templates.ts\` — both the union type (line 10-13), the iteration list (16-19), and the human label map (23-26). Suggested label: \`'Autonomous'\`.
- Add the mode to \`frontend/src/lib/sessionDetail.ts\` (line 24-26 area) so the session detail view renders it.
- Surface a small "no approval, no whitelist — driven by profile instructions" note in the mode picker so a user picking Autonomous knows what's at stake.
- The template form should make \`instructions\` required when the mode is \`autonomous\` (mirror the backend validation).

### API

- Schemas at \`app/api/sessions.py:146\`, \`app/api/meeting_configs.py:65,89,128\`, \`app/api/templates.py:39,72\` already type as \`BotMode\` — they will accept the new value automatically once the enum lands, but verify with a unit test per endpoint.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] \`BotMode.AUTONOMOUS\` exists and is persisted via meeting_configs and templates.
- [ ] Alembic migration adds the value to the PG enum and \`alembic upgrade head\` is clean against a populated database.
- [ ] Autonomous-mode template / meeting_config rejects blank \`instructions\` with a clear validation error.
- [ ] Autonomous-mode template / meeting_config does **not** require \`allowed_replies\`.
- [ ] In an autonomous session, the router proposes a reply, the answer LLM produces free-form output, TTS speaks it within ~4s of the question — no approval round-trip.
- [ ] Decisions still land in \`agent_decisions\` with \`outcome=spoken\` (or \`suppressed\` for declined cases); \`agent_utterances\` rows persist as in other speaking modes.
- [ ] Per-session rate limit applies; over-cap requests log a \`suppressed\` decision with \`reason=rate_limited\`.
- [ ] Frontend renders 'Autonomous' as a fifth option in the mode picker and on the session detail view.
- [ ] Quality gates pass: \`uv run pytest\`, \`uv run ruff check\`, \`uv run mypy\`, \`pnpm typecheck\`, \`pnpm lint\`.

## Out of scope

- Per-template instruction templates / prompt library.
- Anti-jailbreak guardrails against malicious instructions — the bead assumes the user owns their template.
- Voice-tone / persona tuning (uses whatever the configured TTS provider produces).
- A "kill switch" UI button to immediately silence an autonomous bot mid-meeting — file a follow-up bead under \`Johnny-ckz\` if you want it; it's a different shape of work.

## Notes

This belongs under \`Johnny-ckz\` because the lived-journey validation in \`Johnny-pdf\` (Phases 4-7 explicitly enumerate all four modes) needs a fifth phase or an extension of Phase 7 to cover Autonomous. When that lands, update \`Johnny-pdf\` acceptance to include the new mode.

## Related

- \`Johnny-ckz\` — parent epic (join-stuck fix + e2e harness).
- \`Johnny-pdf\` — master e2e validation, currently enumerates Phases 4-7 across the four existing modes; will need extending.
- \`Johnny-kgc.26\` — US-026: Listen-only and Suggest-only modes (closed; precedent for adding modes).
- \`Johnny-kgc.27\` — US-027: Approval-required mode (closed; reference for pipeline behaviour without approval gate).
- \`Johnny-kgc.28\` — US-028: Limited auto-speak (closed; nearest neighbour — same speak path, different governance).
acceptance_criteria: BotMode.AUTONOMOUS lands with migration; validation enforces non-empty instructions and ignores allowed_replies; pipeline speaks free-form output without an approval gate; decisions and utterances persist as in other speaking modes; per-session rate limit honoured; frontend exposes 'Autonomous' as the fifth mode option and on session detail; quality gates pass.
notes: Spawned 2026-06-06 from user request — explicitly wants a mode that lets the bot act on instructions alone with free speech and no per-utterance confirmation. Lives under Johnny-ckz so the e2e harness picks it up.

title: openai-realtime STT adapter targets deprecated Realtime Beta API
description: The E2E harness (Johnny-upg) flagged that POST /providers/{id}/test against an openai-realtime row fails with: "The Realtime Beta API is no longer supported. Please use /v1/realtime for the GA API." The adapter at backend/app/providers/openai_realtime_stt.py still sends `OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1` and connects to the beta endpoint. Update it to the GA endpoint /v1/realtime and re-run `uv run python -m tests.e2e.providers_ui` until stt-openai-realtime PASSes.

title: Surface undecryptable Google account tokens with a clear reconnect path
description:
When a stored Google account row's refresh token cannot be decrypted (typically because FERNET_KEY was rotated since the OAuth flow, or postgres data outlived the host .env), the Calendar page surfaces the raw backend error 'google api client error: failed to decrypt refresh token for account N' and offers no recovery path. The user is stuck at a dead end even though Settings → Disconnect can already clean the row up.

## Repro

1. Connect a Google account via /settings (account row stored, refresh token encrypted with key K1).
2. Regenerate FERNET_KEY (e.g. user re-ran the setup guide §3) and restart the stack — postgres volume persists.
3. Open /calendar — Refresh attempt against /calendar/events?account_id=N raises GoogleApiClientError → 502 → top-of-page red error.

## Root cause

backend/app/services/google_client.py:96-102 — _decrypt_refresh_token() raises GoogleApiClientError with the literal account id. backend/app/api/calendar.py:117-121 maps it to HTTP 502 with the bare exception string. The frontend (frontend/src/routes/calendar/+page.svelte:104-111) just renders error.message.

## Fix (proposed scope)

Backend:
- Introduce a distinct error class (e.g. TokenUndecryptableError) or carry a structured code on the existing GoogleApiClientError so callers can tell 'tokens unreadable, needs reauth' apart from transport / quota / scope errors.
- Map this code to a dedicated HTTP status (409 Conflict with detail {code: 'account_needs_reauth', account_id, email}) on /calendar/events and any other endpoint that calls GoogleApiClient (calendar polling worker should mark the row dirty and skip rather than throwing).
- Add a 'token_health' field to the AccountRead response: 'ok' | 'needs_reauth'. Computed cheaply at list time by attempting a no-op decrypt of refresh_token_encrypted (do not fetch userinfo).

Frontend:
- Settings: badge accounts whose token_health=='needs_reauth' as 'Token unreadable — reconnect'. Reuse the existing Add-account OAuth flow with the same role / default-user tags; on success, the row is replaced in place because upsert is keyed by email (google_client.py:265).
- Calendar: when the selected account.token_health=='needs_reauth', skip the /calendar/events call entirely and render an empty state with a deep link to /settings#account-N and a 'Reconnect this account' inline action that initiates OAuth right there.

Docs:
- docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md §3 — move the 'if you lose the key, all encrypted rows must be deleted' warning to a callout at the top of the section. Add a copy-paste recovery snippet that disconnects all accounts via the API (which is already key-loss-safe per auth.py:474-479) instead of dropping postgres data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New typed error path distinguishes 'undecryptable token' from other GoogleApiClient failures
- [ ] /auth/google/accounts response includes token_health for every row, computed without a Google round-trip
- [ ] GET /calendar/events returns 409 with {code: 'account_needs_reauth'} (not 502) when the selected account's token cannot be decrypted
- [ ] Settings page shows a 'Reconnect' affordance for accounts in needs_reauth state; clicking it runs OAuth and the row is replaced after callback
- [ ] Calendar page detects needs_reauth before fetching and renders a non-error empty state with a Settings deep link
- [ ] Recovery callout added at the top of docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md §3 with the disconnect-via-Settings instruction
- [ ] Backend tests cover: undecryptable refresh token → typed error, /calendar/events 409 response, /auth/google/accounts token_health field
- [ ] Frontend tests cover: Settings reconnect button visibility, Calendar empty-state branch
- [ ] chrome-devtools screenshot of Calendar empty state and Settings reconnect badge attached

## Non-goals

- In-place key rotation (decrypt with old key, re-encrypt with new key) — out of scope; user is told to reconnect instead
- Multi-key support / key versioning on encrypted columns
- Detecting and auto-clearing meeting_configs whose identity_account is broken — Disconnect already cascades with force=true; document that path instead

## Notes

Current immediate workaround: /settings → Disconnect on the broken account (already handles undecryptable tokens — auth.py:474-479) → re-add via 'Add account'.

title: Refactor provider settings UI: per-provider structured forms instead of generic Credentials/Options textareas
description:
The current provider settings UI (US-018, Johnny-kgc.18) exposes only two generic textareas per provider — "Credentials" and "Options" — both accepting raw key=value lines. This is opaque: users must already know the exact env-var-style keys each provider expects (e.g. DEEPGRAM_API_KEY vs api_key vs token; OLLAMA base_url vs OPENAI_API_BASE; ElevenLabs voice_id vs voice). It causes silent typos, hides which fields are required, and makes provider switching painful.

This task replaces the two-textarea design with structured, row-based forms — one form schema per concrete provider adapter. Each provider type renders its own clearly labeled fields with inline guidance (placeholders, descriptions, links to where to get the value), required/optional markers, validation, and field grouping (auth vs config vs model selection).

The backend provider registry (US-011) already knows each provider's required/optional fields; this task surfaces that schema to the frontend rather than dumping a free-text textarea on the user.

## Scope

### Backend
- Extend the provider adapter base classes (STTProvider, LLMProvider, TTSProvider) with a class-level `field_schema()` classmethod that returns a list of field definitions: { name, label, type (text/password/url/number/select), required, placeholder, help_text, default, options? (for select), group? }
- Each concrete adapter (DeepgramSTT, OpenAIRealtimeSTT, FasterWhisperSTT, OpenAI LLM, Anthropic LLM, Gemini LLM, OpenAICompatibleLLM, ElevenLabsTTS, OpenAITTS, PiperTTS) declares its own field_schema with the right fields, labels, and help text
- New endpoint GET /providers/schemas returns all registered provider schemas grouped by kind so the frontend can render dynamic forms
- Persist values into the existing provider_credentials table — split fields into "credentials" (encrypted) and "config" (plain) buckets server-side based on the schema's type/sensitivity
- Validation: backend validates incoming payloads against the schema (required, type) before save; returns 422 with field-level errors
- Migration is not required if the underlying storage already uses JSONB; this is a UI/schema-presentation refactor, not a data-model rewrite

### Frontend
- New `/providers` UI replaces the two textareas with a per-provider form generated from the schema fetched from /providers/schemas
- Each provider card shows: provider name, kind badge, set of structured rows (label + input + help text + required marker), Test button, Save button, Delete button
- Field types render appropriately: password fields are masked, select fields use a dropdown, URL fields show a leading protocol hint, etc.
- Inline help text links to the provider's signup/docs page when relevant ("Get a key →")

title: Build interactive CLI setup wizard for Johnny
description:
Build a Python CLI wizard that walks the user through Johnny's full local setup interactively. The wizard should be the friendlier alternative to docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md — instead of copy-pasting commands, the user answers prompts and the wizard does the work.

The wizard should:

- Run via 'uv run python -m johnny.wizard' or a script entrypoint like 'johnny setup'
- Use a rich TUI library (questionary, rich, or textual — pick one and stick to it)
- Detect prerequisites (Docker, uv, pnpm, available disk space, GPU presence) and report what is missing with direct install links
- Guide Google OAuth setup: open the Google Cloud Console URL in the default browser, prompt for client ID / client secret, write to .env
- For each provider kind (STT, LLM, TTS), ask: cloud or local?
  - If cloud: list options (Deepgram, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, ElevenLabs) with provider sign-up URLs and 'best for' notes; prompt for API key; write to .env and call backend API to register
  - If local: list recommended models per kind with size on disk and quality notes; let user pick; download automatically via huggingface-hub, ollama pull, or direct URL; place in correct volume path; call backend API to register
- Recommend best defaults per kind for local-first (e.g., faster-whisper small for STT, Llama 3.1 8B via Ollama for LLM, Piper en_US-amy-medium for TTS)
- Generate FERNET_KEY automatically and write to .env (only if missing)
- After provider setup, run the same smoke test the Providers UI offers ('Test' button) for each registered provider and report pass/fail
- Offer to start the Docker Compose stack at the end and open the UI
- Be re-runnable safely: detect already-completed steps and offer to skip or reconfigure
- Provide a '--non-interactive' mode that reads answers from a YAML file for CI / scripted setups

The wizard is a complement to docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md (Johnny-mxx), not a replacement — the docs should reference it as the recommended path.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard runs via a single 'uv run python -m johnny.wizard' command; detects missing prerequisites with install links; configures Google OAuth, all three provider kinds (cloud and local), and FERNET_KEY end-to-end; downloads local models automatically into the correct Docker volumes; runs provider smoke tests and reports pass/fail; safely re-runnable; supports --non-interactive YAML mode

title: Write local-first setup guide with copy-paste commands and direct download links
description:
Create a step-by-step setup guide for running Johnny entirely locally. The guide must be copy-paste ready, super simple, and include direct download links for every model and dependency.
